who_can_apply: Sophomores (80 to 90 credits) and juniors (140 to 150 credits by January) with a 2.0 GPA or higher, good attendance, Algebra I or Integrated Math I done, and currently in Geometry or higher.
how_to_apply: Register for the Evergreen Valley College placement test at (408) 274-7900 x6636, attend a recruitment and info meeting to get the application, then mail it or hand-deliver it to the Roble Building mailroom at Evergreen Valley College.
notes: Page lists no age rule and no 2026-27 meeting dates; call the coordinator (Kathleen Leal, (408) 274-7900 x6881) for the schedule. Must also be taking biology, chemistry and physics and English 2 (sophomores) or English 3 (juniors).
duration: 2 years
pay_detail: No cost listed on the page (public school program)

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 21, currently in high school or college. Alameda County program. No income or residency rule is listed on the page.
how_to_apply: Call the Alameda County Workforce Development Board main line at (510) 259-3842. You can also use the Contact Us link on the youth page.
notes: Out-of-school youth ages 16 to 24 use the Future Force program instead. The youth page says to find a local Future Force provider through its Future Force page. The youth page lists no individual provider phone numbers.
pay_detail: Not stated. The youth page mentions paid and unpaid work experience but gives no wage.

who_can_apply: Girls in 11th grade. A local American Legion Auxiliary Unit must pick and sponsor you. Each high school can send only one delegate. If no Unit sponsors your school, you can apply as a statewide alternate. No age rule is stated.
how_to_apply: Ask your school counselor. Or contact a local American Legion Auxiliary Unit. The site has a list to find one. Each Unit picks a delegate and two alternates. Many use a form, an essay or an interview. Picked students then fill out an online form. It opens in February 2027. Is there no Unit at your school? You can apply as a statewide alternate. That form opens in April 2027.
notes: Separate from the coed American Legion California Boys State (Boys & Girls State) program, which has its own card on this site. The FAQ says a student may apply to either American Legion CA Boys State or American Legion Auxiliary CA Girls State, but not both. Selection criteria, grade-school rules beyond the 11th grade note, and cost are not stated on the pages. The 2027 session will be the 84th. Adult staff must be at least 20 or out of high school for at least three years, so staff roles are not for teens.
duration: One week. The 2026 session (83rd) ran June 22 to 27, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the program pages. The site says there are opportunities for scholarship consideration, including the Samsung American Legion Scholarship.

who_can_apply: Ages 12 to 15, in grades 7 to 10. You need a 2.5 GPA or higher and must pass a Red Cross Level 4 swim test. You also need your own ride.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Add an unofficial school transcript, two letters of recommendation and a resume. Add a short letter, about one page, under the heading "Tell Us About You". Interviews follow.
notes: The program page does not give start and end dates or pay. Ask the aquatics team. Email arpdaquatics@alamedaca.gov or call the city at 510-747-7400. It is held at Encinal Swim Center, 230 Central Ave. Residency is not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Students aged 16 and older. The program page does not list residency or other rules.
how_to_apply: Use the Application link on the program page. It goes to the city job site. Watch for the posting in March.
notes: The program page does not say if the job is paid, how long it lasts, or if a work permit is needed. Ask Human Resources at 510-747-4900.
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Ages 10 and up. Teens 15 to 17 may volunteer on their own. Under 15 needs an adult (1 adult for every 5 youth).
how_to_apply: Book shifts on the volunteer calendar or email volunteer@accfb.org, phone 510-635-3663 ext. 308.
notes: 7900 Edgewater Dr, Oakland. Wear closed-toe shoes that cover your whole foot. BART to Coliseum, then AC Transit 98.
duration: Shifts

who_can_apply: High school students interested in local government. The program page does not list an age or grade rule.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online intern application. The link is on the program page.
notes: Projects serve Dublin, Fremont, Livermore, Pleasanton, Sunol and the eastern unincorporated areas of Alameda County. The program page does not give hours, start dates or pay. The office is at 4501 Pleasanton Ave, Pleasanton. The intern director is Katy Felton. The page shows two different email addresses, so call the office to check.
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: You must be 16 or older. If you are 17 or younger, you need a work permit from your school unless you have already graduated. Some jobs, such as racing, cash handling, childcare, amphitheater usher, entertainment transport and parking seller, need you to be 18 or older.
how_to_apply: Fill out the job form online. Or print the paper form and send it in.
notes: Pay examples from the program page: Admissions Ambassador $18.00, Exhibits Attendant $17.00, Event Operations Tech $20.00. The job email is jobs@alamedacountyfair.com. The phone is 925-426-7600. The fair office is at 4501 Pleasanton Ave. The program page does not say how many hours a week you will work.
pay_detail: $17.00 to $20.00 per hour, depending on the job, as listed on the program page.

who_can_apply: High school, college and STEM trade school students. The program page does not list an age or residency rule.
how_to_apply: The program page does not say how to apply. Check it again in February or March 2027.
notes: The program page does not give program dates, pay or an age limit, so ask before you plan. Questions: alcoitd@acgov.org.
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Not stated on the page. Ages and requirements vary by role and are shown on the portal.
how_to_apply: Browse and apply on the library's Better Impact volunteer portal. The link is on the page. The library phone is 510-745-1500.
notes: The teen page is thin and does not name a teen role or branch. Ask the Fremont Main Library which roles take teens.

who_can_apply: Teens. The TAG page does not state an age or grade. Other teen volunteer roles on the same page use grades 7 to 12 or ages 12 to 17.
how_to_apply: Complete the online TAG registration form on the library page. Questions: refdesk@alamedaca.gov or (510) 747-7777.
notes: Meets at the Main Library in the Stafford Room. The page states no age rule, so ask the library if you are younger than 12 or older than 17. See also Alameda Free Library Teen Volunteers (Book Reviewers and Coding with LEGO) for volunteer roles such as book reviews and LEGO coding.
duration: 1st Tuesday of the month, 4:30 to 5:30 pm
pay_detail: Community service hours only

who_can_apply: Teen Book Reviewers: grades 7 to 12. Coding with LEGO: ages 12 to 17.
how_to_apply: LEGO program: email Fernanda Nunez at fnunez@alamedaca.gov. Book reviews: use the 'How to become a Book Reviewer' page linked from the teen page. Questions: refdesk@alamedaca.gov or 510-747-7777.
notes: Book reviews are limited to one a month. No coding experience needed for LEGO. See also Alameda Free Library Teen Advisory Group (TAG) for the advisory role, where teens suggest ideas for library events and projects.
pay_detail: Community service hours only

who_can_apply: Enrolled in high school AND either live in Oakland or attend an OUSD school or charter, both when you apply and during the cohort. Spring cohorts are for 10th to 12th graders. Summer 2027 is for current 11th graders.
how_to_apply: Online application that must be done in one sitting (no save). Pick your cohort, upload a resume, and answer short-answer questions (75 words minimum each for spring, 150 for summer). Draft answers first. Then an interview. Questions: healprogram@alamedahealthsystem.org.
notes: As of 2026-10-16, the 2026-27 dates, pay and rules are on the HealthPATH page, healthpath-ahs.org/healprogramapply. That page does not load with https. So this card links to the AHS news post that points to it. Type healthpath-ahs.org/healprogramapply into your browser for the live dates and the form. The page says HEAL is for high school students of color. The written rule is that you live in Oakland or go to an OUSD school. The AHS volunteer program is a different program, and it is for ages 18 and up. The page does not say if you need a work permit for the stipend. Ask the program.
duration: Spring 2027: about 5 weeks, Mon to Thu 4 to 6 pm (Cohort A Jan 11 to Feb 11, B Feb 22 to Mar 25, C Apr 5 to May 13). Summer 2027: June 14 to July 23, weekdays 9 am to 4:30 pm.
pay_detail: Fall 2026 cohorts: $400 stipend. Summer 2027: $2,000 stipend. Spring 2027 pay is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Students at Alameda High School. You can choose to enroll as early as 9th grade. The program page lists no other rules.
how_to_apply: Read the CTE brochure and watch the Try Out a Career videos on the program page. Then pick CTE classes when you choose your courses. The program page links to a district enrollment page.
notes: The program page does not describe the courses in each pathway or any work based learning. School office phone: 510-337-7022. Ask the CTE teachers if a class earns college credit.
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page. These are school classes.

who_can_apply: Middle and high school teens in grades 6 to 12. No experience is needed.
how_to_apply: Sign up online on the city registration page. Go to the meetings. Finish your scene prep. Work at least two event nights. Help clean up after.
notes: Meetings are at the Veterans Building, 2203 Central Ave. The haunted house is at South Shore Mall. Questions: call 510-747-7529 or 510-747-7575, or email arpd@alamedaca.gov. The program page does not give event dates or a fee.
pay_detail: Volunteer. You can earn community service hours.

who_can_apply: Local youth, especially students in Alameda Unified School District career technical education programs.
how_to_apply: No sign-up is listed; admission is free. Contacts: Jennifer Padilla (City) 510-747-6852; Amanda Vigil (AUSD) 510-337-7091.
notes: Held at Encinal Jr/Sr High, 210 Central Ave, Alameda. It is an annual fair, but the 2027 date has not been posted.
duration: One afternoon
pay_detail: Free to attend. The fair covers part-time jobs and internships, but the page does not say if they are paid.

who_can_apply: Teens. The program page does not give ages or grades.
how_to_apply: Open the Underground Teen Center page. Use the Alameda Youth Committee link to sign up online with the city.
notes: Ages, grades, meeting times and any fee are not stated on the program page. Call City Hall at 510-747-7400 to ask. The same page describes the Underground Teen Center, where the After Dark program is for middle and high school teens.
pay_detail: Volunteer. The program page does not list pay or a fee.

who_can_apply: Anyone at least 13 years old. No school or city rule is stated for these year-round roles.
how_to_apply: Fill out an application and book a free fingerprint check with the Volunteer Coordinator. Call 714-765-4994 or email VolunteerOffice@anaheim.net. Some roles also need a TB test from the last 2 years.
notes: Fingerprinting is free, but you pay for your own TB test. The page does not post open shifts, so ask the coordinator which roles need help now. Court ordered hours go to the Graffiti Removal Program instead (714-765-5158).
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 21. If you are 15, you must have finished 8th grade. You must keep a GPA of 2.0 or higher and be able to run, lift, climb and crawl.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Fire Explorers Interest Form on the program page. You will be told when spots open. Email FireExplorer@anaheim.net with questions.
notes: Spots go first to Public Safety Pathways grads. Then to Anaheim residents. Then to Anaheim students. Explorers do not enter burning buildings. They do not replace firefighters.
duration: Meetings every other Tuesday, 5:30 to 9:00 p.m.
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Students ages 14 to 21. The page also says you must be a current 7th to 12th grade student. Keep a 2.0 GPA or higher and good attendance. You must never have been arrested and must not use drugs. You must be able to run and do push-ups and sit-ups.
how_to_apply: Email Explorers@anaheim.net to say you are interested. Go to 4 meetings in a row as a guest, in business casual clothes. Then fill out an application. You must pass a written test, an interview and a background check.
notes: Meetings are at the Anaheim Police Department. Academies are held twice a year, often at a military base, and are strict, with drills and exercise. Every Explorer must go to at least one. Questions: Youth Engagement Coordinator, 714-765-1928. The city volunteer page links to an old Explorer page that is gone, so use the police site.
duration: Weekly meetings, Wednesdays 6 to 8:30 p.m., plus at least one 4 day academy
pay_detail: Unpaid. The department pays for most of the uniform. You buy a few items, like shoes and a flashlight.

who_can_apply: Teens who are at least 14 years old and in high school.
how_to_apply: Pick a branch on the program page. Contact the coordinator listed for that branch. Each branch has its own contact and its own rules.
notes: An accepted application does not promise hours. Hours are given out as needed. The library does not give court-ordered service hours. The Mobile Library (Bookmobile and STEAM Van) takes summer applications in April and needs volunteers 2 to 6 p.m. on at least one Monday to Thursday. The Teen Podcast takes applications at the start of fall.
duration: At least 2 hours a week at Central Library and Canyon Hills
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: Teens 13 to 17 years old. Space is small. Anaheim residents and Anaheim students go first.
how_to_apply: Apply online. You need a TB clearance slip from the last two years. Book a free fingerprint appointment at City Hall. Pick a VolunTEEN orientation date. Choose your program, site and weeks. Sign the waivers.
notes: You pay for your own TB test. Fingerprinting is free. Bring a photo ID to the fingerprint appointment. Last cycle, site assignments were emailed by May 30. Questions: Volunteer Coordinator, 714-765-4994. The city also lists other volunteer jobs for ages 13 and up. Examples are trail work at Oak Canyon Nature Center and youth sports coach assistants.
duration: Weeks you choose when you apply
pay_detail: Unpaid. You get a letter that confirms your community service hours.

who_can_apply: Teens 14 to 16. Applicants complete an online application and an on-site interview, then required trainings. Both a parent and the teen sign liability forms.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer application during an open window, attend an interview, then the online and on-site training days.
notes: Spring and Fall sessions are weekends only; Summer shifts run seven days a week. The Aquarium also lists other youth roles for ages 11 to 18 (Ocean Neighbors, Teen Science Cafe Volunteer, Student Eco-Ambassadors). The Education Volunteer role is for ages 16 and up with at least 100 hours in six months.
duration: 60 hours over a 10-week session (Spring, Summer or Fall), one shift a day each week, 9:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program (60 service hours).

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 at Center, Del Campo, El Camino Fundamental or Inderkum High School who meet federal rules for financial need and/or being first in the family to go to college, and want to go beyond high school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Upward Bound application, then staff review eligibility and interview the student and family if eligible. Contact arctrioub@arc.losrios.edu or (916) 484-8033 (Mon to Fri, 9 am to 6 pm).
notes: Only for students at the four listed partner schools. Summer participation is required. The dedicated application page did not show details when read. Ask staff for current dates.
duration: Year-round, including a required summer component
pay_detail: Free program. No stipend mentioned on the page.

who_can_apply: Anyone at least 14 and a half years old. The page lists this rule for all volunteers and links a separate Teen Volunteer Application.
how_to_apply: Complete the Teen Volunteer Application (Google form on the page). Questions: armc-volunteers@armc.sbcounty.gov or Volunteer Management, 400 N. Pepper Avenue, Colton, CA 92324.
notes: Minimum age is 14 and a half. The page lists no application deadline or start dates.
duration: At least 100 hours; one 2-hour shift a week
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 18 who start tasks on their own. You like the arts and feel at ease with kids.
how_to_apply: Use the Learn More and Sign Up link on the volunteer page, which opens a Google Form. You can also call the Armory at (626) 792-5101.
notes: Hours and session dates are not on the page. The Armory's Fall Studio 2026 classes are on a separate page.
duration: Each Studio session (hours not listed)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Young women and men in grades 7 to 12. You must work at least 30 hours a year. Meetings and events count toward hours.
how_to_apply: Call 949-645-6929 to ask how to join. The chapter volunteer page has an Adult Member Application. Ask the chapter whether teens can use it.
notes: Membership costs are not stated on the program page. The thrift shop and office are at 2220 Fairview Road, Costa Mesa. Awards go to those with 50, 75 and 100 or more hours a year. Events include a spring luncheon and a June Senior Medallion Event.
duration: Monthly meetings in the school year. At least 30 hours a year.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program.

who_can_apply: At least 16 years old, and enrolled in high school or college (or enrolled within the past 12 months). A community group must sponsor your placement.
how_to_apply: You cannot apply to BART directly. Ask a community organization or your school to sponsor you and have them email workforcedevelopment@bart.gov.
notes: Sponsor organizations fund the placements. Build a relationship with a community group and ask them to contact workforcedevelopment@bart.gov.
duration: June 22 to July 31, 2026, 10 to 20 hours a week
pay_detail: $20 per hour (high school, 2026)

who_can_apply: Berkeley High students in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe enrollment. Contact CTE Manager Wyn Skeels, WynSkeels@berkeley.net, (510) 644-8727, or your counselor.
notes: Pathway classes meet the a-g rules for getting into college. Middle schoolers get a STEM exploration track.
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Age 12 or older. Ages 12 to 15 must have a parent or guardian with them 1 to 1. Age 16 and up can volunteer alone with a release form.
how_to_apply: Sign up for a General Volunteer Orientation online, read the manual, attend orientation. Contact volunteer@berkeleyhumane.org, (510) 845-7735.
notes: Internships need 18 or older (10 to 20 plus hours a week for 3 months or more).

who_can_apply: Finished 10th or 11th grade, 3.0 GPA, 16 by June 21 (2026 rule).
how_to_apply: Apply online on the Pre-College Scholars site. The 2026 window opened Feb 2, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.
notes: Very expensive. Aid is limited. Also needs a 3.0 GPA and good standing at your school.
duration: 6 or 8 weeks
pay_detail: 2026 cost: $15,987 (8 weeks, June 22 to Aug 14) or $14,687 (6 weeks, July 6 to Aug 14). There is also an application fee. One media scholarship was offered in 2026.

who_can_apply: Teen volunteer: fill out the application. No age is stated. Youth Worker: ages 14 to 25. No experience is needed. A work permit is required if under 18.
how_to_apply: Volunteers: complete the Teen Volunteer Application form. Paid work: go through Berkeley YouthWorks (2180 Milvia St, 510-981-4970); see the YouthWorks page for the current interest form.
notes: The library page also lists other groups that take teen volunteers. Berkeley YouthWorks serves Berkeley residents. You must show proof that you live there. The library page says YouthWorks takes applications in March and October.
duration: Youth Worker up to 15 hours a week
pay_detail: Volunteering is unpaid. Youth Worker jobs are paid (rate not posted; no benefits).

who_can_apply: Bay Area high school students. A new group starts at the beginning of each school year.
how_to_apply: Join the Teen Council mailing list on the Teen Council page, or email teencouncil@berkeleyrep.org.
notes: No grade or age rule is listed beyond high school. Competitive: only 10 to 15 spots.
pay_detail: Transportation stipend. Free admission to teen programs and shows, and free food at events.

who_can_apply: Berkeley residents (proof of residency at onboarding). Priority for youth facing barriers, such as foster care or legal system involvement, English learners, young parents, and students with IEPs or 504 plans. The page states no age rule.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online YouthWorks interest form. Chosen candidates get an email for a 15 to 20 minute interview. Contact: youthworks@berkeleyca.gov, (510) 981-4970.
notes: An interest form does not guarantee a placement. Berkeley Public Library lists the Youth Worker age as 14 to 25. Berkeley residents only.
duration: Winter 2027 placements run January to March 2027
pay_detail: Wage not posted. Ready to Work workshop stipend if you attend at least 7 of 8 sessions.

who_can_apply: Current and former foster youth in Alameda County, per the homepage (it says it serves over 500 each year). The age range and intake steps are not stated on the pages.
how_to_apply: Call 510.980.9010 or email info@beyondemancipation.org (both from the site footer). Staff connect youth to coaching, training and job resources.
notes: Corrected on 2026-10-07. The site loaded this time (the earlier certificate error is gone). The homepage and employment page say who is served and what coaching covers, but do not state an age range, costs or an intake process, so those are left blank or not stated. This is a coaching service rather than a paid job, so the type is the closest available. The employment page lists outside job boards and training partners (Civicorps, Oakland Private Industry Council, EASTBAY Works), which are separate organizations. The jobs page is for B:E staff openings, not youth jobs. Call before relying on it.
pay_detail: No pay to the youth is stated. The cost of services to the youth is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18 who have been Club members for 2 or more years and meet academic requirements. The page does not list the academic requirements.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the page. Ask staff at your Clubhouse. The site lists a 3300 High Street address.
notes: The same Teens page lists Keystone Clubs (ages 14 to 18) and Youth of the Year (ages 16 to 18, a $20,000 scholarship opportunity, not a job). They are not separate cards because the page gives no joining steps. Staff openings are posted on LinkedIn (the careers page does not list them). Season, pay rate, hours and deadlines are not stated, so confirm with the Club before a teen applies. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.
pay_detail: The page says 'Paid positions and income.' The pay rate and hours are not stated.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 and up. Summer Teen Internship: rising high school freshmen through seniors who are 14 or older. To intern or volunteer you must have a Social Security Number and be able to complete a background check.
how_to_apply: Use the Sign Up and Apply Here links on the club's Volunteer page. Questions? Email Emily Mungul at emungul@bgcp.org.
notes: The page links a separate document on the application process and compliance rules. The SSN requirement is for the club's background check; a teen without an SSN cannot do this one. Summer internship hours are 8:00 am to 12:00 pm, 1:00 to 5:00 pm, or both. BGCP's paid Youth Program Leader jobs ($22 to $25 an hour) do not list an age. Mid-Peninsula Boys & Girls Club and Boys & Girls Clubs of North San Mateo County have joined BGCP, per BGCP's news page.
duration: Program Support: at least 1 hour a week on the same day for at least 6 weeks, Monday to Thursday, 3:00 to 6:00 PM, September to May. Summer internship: at least 3 weeks in June to July, Monday to Friday, mornings, afternoons or both.
pay_detail: School-year Program Support is unpaid volunteering. Pay for the Summer Teen Internship is not stated; it is listed on the club's Volunteer page.

who_can_apply: LIT: ages 15 to 17. CIT: ages 16 to 17 who already did LIT (in person or virtually). CITs must commit to two sessions, one of them a 7-day session. No city or residency rule is stated.
how_to_apply: Fill out the LIT/CIT online application on the Teen Leadership page. Then register for camp and pick the 'CIT/LIT programs' price option, which waives the fee once you are accepted. Training is at camp in Session 1A, or a required virtual training.
notes: Apply early. The FAQ says spots often fill by early April. The camp told teens in rounds. For example, it replied by March 2 for the Feb 16 deadline. Buses leave from San Francisco. For Session 1, there is also a stop near Travis Air Force Base. Teens who are 15 can sign up as regular campers instead. People 18 and up can apply for camp staff jobs. Contact: camperapplication@kidsclub.org.
duration: In 2026, LIT/CIT training was June 17 to 20, then camp sessions ran June 20 to Aug 5. LITs can do one or more sessions; CITs do two.
pay_detail: Free: the camp fee is waived for all sessions for accepted LITs and CITs. Not a paid job.

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 9 to 12 who are current Club members. Membership costs $20. Teens may take part only once per calendar year.
how_to_apply: Join the Club ($20 membership) at kidsclub.org/register, then contact the High School Services Director or Clubhouse staff at your Clubhouse to sign up. You must attend one training session.
notes: Contact: Earl Declet, edeclet@kidsclub.org. The 2025-26 flyer lists LIT at these clubs: Willie Mays (Bayview), Excelsior, Don Fisher (Fillmore), Columbia Park and Mission (Mission), Tenderloin, and Springer (Sunnydale). Finishing LIT can lead to summer jobs. Teens under 18 cannot join the adult volunteer program. The site says to join a club, where there are youth volunteer roles. Club teens can also join Keystone Club. Its members raise at least $3,000 to go to a national meeting. The flyers do not say if you need a work permit.
duration: About 10 weeks: 70 hours of on-the-job experience after 10 hours of Work-Based Learning training.
pay_detail: Teens who complete the requirements receive an $800 gift card.

who_can_apply: High school students, rising 9th to 12th grade. The program page does not list a city rule.
how_to_apply: Use the Summer Starts Here button on the program page. It goes to the parent portal. Check back this spring for the class list.
notes: Hours are 10:00am to 5:30pm. The clubhouse has a tech center, recording studio, industrial kitchen and gym. The program page does not list jobs or paid internships. Phone: 510-483-5581. The same club runs a drop-in teen center for ages 13 to 18.
pay_detail: Free for teens. This is a program, not a paid job.

who_can_apply: Last time, the program took Orange County high school students entering grades 10 to 12. You need a Bowers Family Membership. Show your interest in art, culture and history.
how_to_apply: Go to the open house with your family. Then apply. Students are picked based on the application and an interview.
notes: You can earn community service hours. The museum is at 2002 North Main Street, Santa Ana. Call 714-567-3600 for questions.
duration: Summer program. Exact length is not stated on the page.
pay_detail: A Bowers Family Membership is required. The page does not state its price. You can use a membership your family already has.

who_can_apply: The page says Breakthrough uses college and high school students as teachers and tutors. No age or grade rule for teachers is posted. Students attend the summer program before 7th, 8th or 9th grade.
how_to_apply: Use the Teaching Intern application link on breakthroughsac.org (online account login). Questions: BSAC@BreakthroughSac.org or 916-234-3905.
notes: Age minimum, pay and dates are not posted on the site, so call or email before applying. Training is two weeks (80 hours) on site.
duration: 6-week summer program
pay_detail: Pay not stated. Ask the program.

who_can_apply: High school students who completed junior year and have a semester left. There is no application. Your school recommends you. A local American Legion Post interviews and sponsors you. California Girls State is a separate program with its own card.
how_to_apply: In junior year, tell your counselor you want to go. Or contact a local American Legion Post. Use Find a Post on calegion.org. The Post picks its delegates. Then each delegate signs up online.
notes: Two separate programs. This one has been coed since 2023. California Girls State (American Legion Auxiliary, cagirlsstate.org) is its own program. It ran June 22 to 27, 2026 for 11th graders sponsored by a local Auxiliary Unit, one delegate per school. You can apply to only one. An old note about a 2020 article and a Sanger phone was out of date.
duration: One week in June at Sacramento State. The site counts down to June 19, 2027.
pay_detail: Registration fee listed as $550 per delegate on the Key Dates page (the page does not label the year). Ask your sponsoring Post who pays.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 21, per the 2026 Explorer competition packet. This is the competition age rule. Post membership rules such as GPA or background checks are not stated on the pages.
how_to_apply: Email CHPExplorers@chp.ca.gov or call (916) 843-3210 (both listed in the 2026 packet) to ask how to join a post near you.
notes: Both official pages were read on 2026-10-07. The page covers the statewide competition and does not say how to join a post. The 2026 packet is the source for the 15 to 21 age rule, which it states for the competition. Whether a post near you has room, and any background check or GPA rule, must be asked of CHP. The CHP East Sacramento post page returns 403 to automated reads, so use the email or phone above. See also CHP Explorer Post (East Sacramento) for a local post. Ages differ by source: the 2026 competition packet says 15 to 21, while the CHP lists 15 to 20 for Explorers.
duration: Not stated for post membership. The 2026 competition ran April 25 to 26, 2026.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Cost to you: 2026 competition fees were $150 per explorer, $125 per advisor and $75 per spectator.

who_can_apply: California law says an apprentice must be at least 16 (Labor Code 3077, in the state child labor guide). Each registered program sets its own minimum age, education and tests, shown in the DAS search, and may set a higher age.
how_to_apply: Use the Apprenticeship Search on the DAS site, check each program's minimum age and requirements, and apply the way the listing says.
notes: The DAS homepage states no age rule. The 16 minimum comes from the 2013 DLSE child labor guide, which also says apprentices need a school-issued work permit. DAS's How to Become an Apprentice page says search results list each program's minimum age. DAS runs a youth apprenticeship grant and reports 5,776 registered pre-apprentices on its homepage.
pay_detail: DAS describes apprenticeship as earn-and-learn. Wages depend on the program; DAS has a tool to look up apprenticeship wages.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 15 to 25 who need extra help to finish school or find work. Examples listed are offense history as a minor and teen parent. Others are foster care or no stable housing, and gang involvement or risk. Minority group, low income, and disability or reading difficulty are also listed. You may still qualify if you do not match these.
how_to_apply: The page has no separate enrollment steps. Use the YEOP Contact Information page. It helps you reach a YEOP specialist in your area. Or contact your local America's Job Center of California.
notes: The page says clearly: this is not a job placement program. It is help and coaching toward school and work.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: No pay. The page does not say whether services cost anything.

who_can_apply: Young people ages 14 to 24 who meet certain requirements. The EDD page does not list the requirements. It points to the Youth Employment Opportunity Program page and fact sheet for criteria.
how_to_apply: Find your local America's Job Center of California with the EDD Office Locator (edd.ca.gov/en/Office_Locator/). The page also suggests building a resume in CalJOBS and visiting the center to ask about internships, apprenticeships and training.
notes: The EDD page does not say the youth services are free. It says Job Centers connect employers with job seekers at no cost. Eligibility criteria are not on the EDD page; it links to the YEOP services and eligibility criteria. Teens under 18 who take a paid job in California need a work permit from their school (CDE page).
duration: Ongoing, set by each local center
pay_detail: The services are free (the page says Job Centers connect employers with job seekers at no cost). Work experience can be paid or unpaid; no pay rate is given.

who_can_apply: Under 18 needs written parent or guardian permission. Specific age minimums vary by park.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the State Parks volunteer portal or print a paper application and mail it to the park you want. Questions: Volunteer.inparksprogram@parks.ca.gov or (916) 653-9069. The application link is on the official page.
notes: A criminal background check may be required. Park-level age minimums were not on the page, so ask the park. Student volunteer or intern roles are mentioned only as a general possibility at local parks. No Junior Ranger details were on this page.
duration: Varies by park
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 30 on the first day of service. You must meet at least one of: foster care, justice involved, mental health or substance abuse system, low income, hard time finding work, or unemployed and/or out of school.
how_to_apply: Pick your local program from the partner list on the state page and apply through its link. Or use the state interest form. State office: info@californiavolunteers.ca.gov (say Youth Service Corps) or (916) 323-7646.
notes: Partner list on the page: Anaheim, Antioch, Bakersfield, Chula Vista, Fresno, Irvine, La Puente, Long Beach, Los Angeles, Oakland, Rancho Cucamonga, Riverside, Sacramento, San Francisco, San Diego, San Jose, Santa Cruz, South Gate, Stockton, Marin County, Monterey County, Mechoopda Band of Chico Rancheria and Ramona Band of Cahuilla. California requires a work permit for minors in paid jobs (CDE page), so under 18 you will need one. The state page does not say whether each city requires you to live there, so check the local program.
duration: Not stated on the state page; set by each local program
pay_detail: At least minimum wage; the rate varies by location (page wording).

who_can_apply: Your school district must run an approved WEE program. Exploratory WEE students can be as young as 12 and do not need a work permit. General WEE usually needs a work permit. Career Technical WEE needs a job related to a career technical class you take.
how_to_apply: Ask your counselor or CTE/work experience coordinator whether your district has a WEE program and what class goes with it.
notes: The 2013 state child labor guide says students must be 16 to enroll in WEE, with exceptions in the Education Code (14 and 15 year olds can get permits in some cases). The CDE page says Exploratory can start at 12. Programs exist only where the district chose to run one. Use the three current names above.
pay_detail: Exploratory is unpaid. General and Career Technical WEE combine paid work with a class.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors interested in engineering, robotics or AI. Bonita Unified School District students get priority.
how_to_apply: Email the RASIM Center at rasim@cpp.edu to sign up during the January to April window.
notes: The page's sample schedule is labeled Summer 2027 but gives no exact dates. Confirm by email.
duration: Held each July, daily 9:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., at Cal Poly Pomona Building 17
pay_detail: $25 per person. Parking permit and daily lunch included.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 5 to 18 by Dec 31 of the 4-H year, anywhere in California.
how_to_apply: Find your county 4-H office on the Join page. A parent signs up in ZSuite and pays the county fee.
notes: The old ucanr.edu/sites/ca4H address now goes to this page. Projects and fees depend on your county.
duration: The 4-H year runs July to June.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Your county sets a fee, and some projects cost extra. Fee waivers are available.

who_can_apply: Students at a school that runs a California Cadet Corps unit. Participation is voluntary. The pages do not say how a student enrolls beyond being at a host school.
how_to_apply: Ask your school whether it has a Cadet Corps unit. The program site says schools that want to start one should email Recruiting@cacadets.org. The site's Contact Us page is cacadets.org/about/contact.
notes: Program pages did not include a school finder, so the best first step is to ask your school office or email the program. The program site says more than 7,000 students are in over 100 schools.
duration: Ongoing school year program
pay_detail: Free. The program site says it is fully funded by the state with no cost to families or host schools. Cadets earn up to ten elective credits per year.

who_can_apply: Students at a California school with an FBLA chapter. The FAQ says FBLA is open to students enrolled in a Career and Technical Education (CTE) business program.
how_to_apply: Ask whether your school has a chapter: email hello@cafbla.org or call (714) 824-4489. If not, fill out the FBLA Interest Form so staff can help your school affiliate; that needs your school administration.
notes: You join through a school chapter, so you need a business pathway or class at your school. If your school has no business program, the FAQ says starting one has to be started with school administration.
duration: Ongoing through the school year
pay_detail: Not a job. The join page lists no dues amounts.

who_can_apply: Join through a school that has an agricultural education program; chapters are chartered in schools with ag classes. California reports over 103,000 members. The pages do not state age or grade rules.
how_to_apply: Take an agriculture class at a school with an FFA chapter.
notes: Not every school has an FFA chapter. Ask your counselor or ag teacher. Age and grade limits and dues were not on the California or National FFA pages checked.
duration: School year; SAE can be year-round
pay_detail: Dues are not stated on the program pages. Ask your ag teacher what your chapter charges.

who_can_apply: Students at schools that host an academy. Each academy has its own way to apply. Look on the school's website for 'Partnership Academy'.
how_to_apply: Ask your counselor if your school has an academy. The CDE page links a directory of academies (a spreadsheet updated September 2026). The page does not say how students apply.
notes: Read the CDE page on 2026-10-09. It confirms a three-year program for grades 10 to 12, structured as a school-within-a-school, with academics plus career technical education, business partnerships, mentoring and internships. It posts only school and district grant dates, not student application dates, and does not say whether students from other districts may transfer in. Academies are run by individual schools, so ask your counselor. Fremont Unified says some CTE courses sit inside Partnership Academies.
duration: 3 years
pay_detail: The CDE page does not say whether internships pay or give school credit. Ask the school.

who_can_apply: High school sophomores and juniors with at least a 2.0 GPA who live or go to school within 3 miles of the California Science Center. Seniors were not taken in the 2026-27 cycle. You must be allowed to work in the US.
how_to_apply: Apply on the program page when it opens. The page says the program is competitive. You need a work permit from your high school if you are hired.
notes: Only for teens near Exposition Park (the 0 to 3 mile rule). No science background is needed. Public speaking helps but is not required. Interns can also apply for the summer Dive Team or Flight Team. The page lists no minimum age.
duration: 7 months, late October to late May. About 7 hours a week, including Saturdays and school holidays. You can keep the job each school year until you graduate.
pay_detail: $18.42 per hour

who_can_apply: Rising juniors and seniors. You need a 2.0 GPA or higher. You must go to one of three schools: Math, Science, and Technology Magnet Academy, Roosevelt High School or Mendez High School. You must be at ease in the water. You must be allowed to work in the US.
how_to_apply: Apply on the program page when it opens. The page says the program is competitive. You need a work permit from your high school if you are hired.
notes: Only students at three Los Angeles high schools can apply. Paid for by a gift from the Vera R. Campbell Foundation. The page lists no minimum age.
duration: 6 weeks, full time on weekdays, 35 hours a week (June 15 to July 31 last summer)
pay_detail: $17.87 per hour

who_can_apply: Rising juniors and seniors. You need a 2.0 GPA or higher. You must go to one of three schools: Math, Science, and Technology Magnet Academy, Roosevelt High School or Mendez High School. You must be allowed to work in the US.
how_to_apply: Apply on the program page when it opens. The page says the program is competitive. You need a work permit from your high school if you are hired.
notes: Only students at three Los Angeles high schools can apply. Paid for by a gift from the Vera R. Campbell Foundation. The page lists no minimum age.
duration: 6 weeks, full time on weekdays, 35 hours a week (June 15 to July 31 last summer)
pay_detail: $17.87 per hour

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors who are 16 or 17.
how_to_apply: Fill out the youth form on the volunteer page. Then email it to the volunteer office. Or mail it to the Science Center at 700 Exposition Park Drive, Los Angeles, CA 90037. The email is VolunteerDept@californiasciencecenter.org.
notes: Spots are limited. The same page lists other volunteer roles open at 16 (greeter, floor programs, gift store, office help) that ask for 4 hours a week for 6 months on the adult application. Volunteer Office: 213-744-2124.
duration: One 4-hour shift a week, usually on the weekend, for 14 weeks (50 or more hours)
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn community service hours.

who_can_apply: Students currently enrolled in a Pasadena Unified School District (PUSD) high school. Grade and age rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: The page has no form. Use the email link for the program contact (Mitch Aiken) on the Summer Research Connection page.
notes: Only for PUSD students. Contact early in the school year because spots fill by early spring.
duration: 6 weeks
pay_detail: The page does not say whether interns are paid or what it costs. Ask the program contact.

who_can_apply: High school freshmen, sophomores and juniors who live in Los Angeles County. Seniors in the class of 2027 cannot apply. You cannot apply if you went to Camp CHLA before. You must be able to come all 5 days.
how_to_apply: Apply online in the short January window. Write one essay of 200 to 250 words and give your and your parent's contact details. If you are picked, you upload shot records and other papers before your session.
notes: The window is only 5 days, so mark your calendar. An online info session is Dec 9, 2026 at 6:30 p.m. You need your own ride to the hospital. Use a personal email, since school email has blocked camp emails before. The page lists the 2027 session dates under Discovery Day, so confirm them. Email campchla@chla.usc.edu.
duration: 5 days, about 8 a.m. to 3 p.m. (Discovery Day is one day)
pay_detail: Free. There is no charge to attend.

who_can_apply: High school students who meet at least one criterion, such as low income, foster youth, system-involved, homeless, pregnant or parenting, English learner, below grade level in math or reading, or an IEP.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth Referral Form (online form linked on the CCCOE page) or call: West County (925) 296-1507 or 296-1504; East County (925) 296-1505 or 296-1506.
notes: The out-of-school program is for ages 18 to 24, so only the in-school program fits most teens. Help can include transportation, interview clothes and school supplies.
pay_detail: Paid workforce prep and work experience (rate not posted)

who_can_apply: Eligible youth ages 16 to 24. The page does not list the rules for each program. Use the referral form or call a Youth Services specialist to find out which program fits you.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth Referral Form linked on the program page. Or call the Youth Services Supervisor, Esperanza Ellis, at 925-942-3313.
notes: Youth Services specialists have their own phone lines on the page, for example 925-296-1505 and 925-296-1507. Another card covers the WIOA in-school program from the same office. Businesses can ask to become a worksite with the worksite form on the page.
pay_detail: Paid work experience. The pay rate is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Students 14 to 18 enrolled in high school with a transcript showing at least a 3.2 GPA. New volunteers and one parent or guardian must attend a mandatory in-person Teen Information Session.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application with your transcript, finish the online volunteer orientation, complete health screening and flu vaccine (flu season Nov 1 to Apr 30), and attend the Teen Information Session (Monday, Jan 11, 2027, 5:30 to 7:00 p.m.).
notes: Spots are limited and fill fast, so apply the day the window opens. Shifts run Monday to Sunday. Teens who want research should look at Cedars-Sinai's separate INSPIRE Internship Program (not checked here). Questions: TeenVolunteerProgram@cshs.org or 310-423-8044.
duration: Winter/Spring and Fall: one 2-hour shift a week for 10 weeks (20 hours). Summer: two 4-hour shifts a week for 5 weeks (40 hours).
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers buy the required volunteer jacket for $30 (cash) and wear black or white scrubs.

who_can_apply: Current high school students. Each semester you complete a Chabot application and the concurrent enrollment packet. You can take any class except basic skills and PE.
how_to_apply: Apply to Chabot, pick a class, fill out the IDE Enrollment Form, then register through MyPortal. Questions: Admissions & Records, 510-723-6701.
notes: Also offers CCAP classes at your high school and a Summer Academy. Middle schoolers have a separate Bridge to College program.
duration: Per term
pay_detail: Enrollment fees are waived. Out-of-state and international students pay $370 per unit. You buy your own books and arrange your own transportation. Maximum 11 units.

who_can_apply: High school students. The page encourages students of all backgrounds to apply, especially Oakland public and charter school students. No skills, experience or GPA is needed. Admission is competitive: an initial review, then an information session for applicants and families. Age and residency rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Online application from February 1 to March 31, then an initial review and an information session for applicants and families. The page also has an interest survey to get application updates.
notes: Corrected on 2026-10-07 after reading the program's own page. The old chabotspace.org/volunteer/ link now returns 404, so the card points to the Galaxy Explorers page. This is a fee-based program ($1,500 a year tuition) unless the family qualifies for Career Access, which is based on need and census tract data. Floor shifts are 2 per month in the school year and 3 per month in summer. Whether paid Interns need a California work permit is not stated on the page, so we leave the work permit answer blank.
duration: 3 years (summer before 10th grade through 12th grade)
pay_detail: Annual tuition is $1,500 per student (one payment by June 1, or $750 by June 1 and $750 by September 1). The need-based Career Access program covers tuition and adds a stipend. 12th-grade Interns receive a stipend.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12 in the fall after the program. A 3.0 GPA or higher is suggested. You should like research or health science.
how_to_apply: For a waitlist spot, email the program director, Dr. Hamid Montazeri, using the contact on the program page. Watch the page for the next registration.
notes: You get a certificate of completion and can ask for a letter of reference. Sessions are online and in person. The page lists a full refund if you cancel by June 29, 2026.
duration: 3 weeks. In 2026 it ran July 13 to July 31.
pay_detail: The page lists the total cost for 2025 as $1,503. It does not list a 2026 price. Cost covers lab access, food on in-person days and materials.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 10 to 12 in the fall after the program. Students who just finished high school can join too. A 3.5 GPA or higher is suggested.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Summer 2027 priority list form on the program page. You will be told when registration opens. Questions go to program director Dr. Ann Gordon.
notes: 2026 was the first year of this program. You get a certificate of completion.
duration: Weekdays 9 a.m. to 12 p.m. Exact 2027 dates are not posted.
pay_detail: The 2027 cost is not posted yet. You also buy an SPSS grad pack for about $34.95 and bring your own laptop.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 8 to 12 for the 2026-27 school year. No prior experience is needed.
how_to_apply: Join the interest list for 2027 on the program page. Sign up for each workshop on the same page when it opens.
notes: Workshops are at the Keck Center for Science and Engineering, 450 N. Center St., Orange. Questions: engineering@chapman.edu or 714-516-5616.
duration: Workshops. The 2026 bioprinting workshop was one day.
pay_detail: The cost is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Students who have finished their freshman year of high school and are 15 to 17 years old by the orientation date (June 14 last cycle). The page says no exceptions.
how_to_apply: Apply online during the one-week window. Write two short answers (150 words each) and one essay (300 words). Give the emails of two teachers, counselors, coaches or mentors. Then a video interview with a parent, a health screening and a full-day orientation.
notes: The window is only one week, so mark late January on your calendar. This is not job shadowing or an internship, and contact with patients who stay in the hospital is limited. You need full shot records, a TB blood test and a drug and alcohol screening. No weekend shifts. You may not miss more than one week. Questions: Volunteer Resources, 323-361-2317, Volunteers@chla.usc.edu.
duration: 7 weeks, 16 hours a week in 4 blocks, Monday to Thursday, 112 hours in all
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Current juniors at a public high school in Los Angeles County. You need papers to work legally in California. You should have strong grades and a real interest in science.
how_to_apply: Apply online. You need an essay, a transcript and one letter from a science or math teacher or a counselor. Your letter is only asked for after the rest is done, so finish early. Info sessions are held in November and January.
notes: Very competitive. If you accept, you must turn down all other summer programs and go to every required meeting. The page mixes dates from different years, so check it again in November. Questions: Danielle Nunez, danunez@chla.usc.edu. Ask whether you need a work permit for the stipend.
duration: Summer lab work, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday to Friday, for 7 weeks. College counseling runs from April through senior year.
pay_detail: Stipend, plus a Metro card and meals at the hospital. The page does not give the amount.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 20 on the CHP Explorer eligibility page (the East Sacramento office page says 15 to 21). You need at least a 2.0 GPA, no drug or alcohol use and no felony convictions.
how_to_apply: Email the East Sacramento Explorer advisor, Sergeant John Daubner (JDaubner@chp.ca.gov), or call the office at (916) 464-1450 to get an application. After you apply you need a background check and a medical exam by a doctor.
notes: Read in a browser on 2026-10-19. The old Explorer post page on chp.ca.gov now loads blank. So the card links to the East Sacramento Area office page. It has an Explorer section and the advisor's email. The office is at 11336 Trade Center Drive, Rancho Cordova. The eligibility rules come from CHP's careers site (linked from chp.ca.gov). Ages differ: the eligibility page says 15 to 20 and the office page says 15 to 21, so ask the advisor. Meeting times are not posted. See also California Highway Patrol Explorer Program for the statewide competition.

who_can_apply: There is a separate application for ages 16 to 17. Animal care and docent roles are 18 and up. Animal care also needs 100 hours of earlier volunteering.
how_to_apply: Submit the 16-17 volunteer application. Then go to the next orientation. They tell you about it by email.
notes: The center does not take court-ordered community service right now. If you have questions, write to volunteers@thelivingcoast.org.
duration: Ongoing, based on availability. In animal care, 3 absences within 60 days may result in losing your spot.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Youth ages 12 to 18 (the page is titled 'Become a Cadet (Ages 12-18)'). The page says your local squadron can answer eligibility questions.
how_to_apply: Find a local squadron. Contact it and visit with a parent. Go to about three meetings. Then apply. You can apply online if your squadron commander says you are eligible, or by mail or fax. Contact: pao@cawgcap.org.
notes: Prices on the California Wing cost page are from 2021 and 2022. Ask your squadron for current amounts. The Northern California Bay Area squadrons are listed on the wing site. The cost page says you must go to encampment to advance to Cadet Second Lieutenant.
duration: Ongoing; weekly squadron meetings
pay_detail: Dues plus uniforms. The cost page (2021 and 2022 figures) lists $45 national dues, $25 squadron dues (can be waived for hardship), and about $205 to $300 total to join with uniforms. Encampment was $300 in 2021, with financial help available. No 2026 figures are posted, so check the National site for current dues.

who_can_apply: High school students at participating schools in 14 counties, including Sacramento and Yolo. Ask the FARMS coordinator at your school.
how_to_apply: Ask your ag or science teacher whether your school participates. Contact Mindy Cunha at mindy@landbasedlearning.org.
notes: Advanced FARMS tier (year-long research, job shadowing) also exists. Main office (530) 795-1520. CLBL headquarters is The Maples Farm in Woodland.
duration: school year, 6+ field days
pay_detail: No cost or stipend listed on the page.

who_can_apply: Students at Luther Burbank High, Grant Union High and Sacramento Academic and Vocational Academy (SAVA).
how_to_apply: The page does not explain how to apply. Ask a teacher or counselor at your host school, or contact the Center for Land-Based Learning: info@landbasedlearning.org or (530) 795-1520.
notes: Only at the three host schools. Grant Union students can earn college credit through a Sacramento State partnership (ACE program). Pay rate and hours per week are not posted. Paid job for a minor, so a work permit is likely needed.
duration: year-long
pay_detail: Pay rate not posted on the page.

who_can_apply: High school students. You need a principal's recommendation, a parent's consent and approval from the college. The program page does not name a grade or age limit.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school counselor and pick a class. Apply to a Peralta college online. Fill out the high school special enrollment form, signed by a parent and your counselor. Bring your transcript and a photo ID to Admissions and Records. Meet a college counselor, then sign up for classes.
notes: Most students may take up to 11 units in fall and spring and 9 units in summer. The page lists higher limits for CCAP dual enrollment, which has its own agreement. Dual enrollment does not replace a course your high school offers. College of Alameda phone: 510-522-7221.
pay_detail: Tuition and fees are free for up to 15 units of approved classes each semester. Books and travel costs are not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Concurrent enrollment: high school students in grades 9 to 12. Dual enrollment: students at CSM's partner high schools; talk to your school counselor.
how_to_apply: Create an OpenCCC account and apply to CSM online. For dual enrollment, meet with your high school counselor first, then register with the Dual Enrollment team. Questions: csmoutreach@smccd.edu.
notes: Dual enrollment is only through CSM's partner high schools. Concurrent enrollment is open to any high schooler but may need your counselor's approval at some schools. Skyline and Canada colleges run similar programs (not checked here).
pay_detail: Free. Dual enrollment includes textbooks and materials; concurrent enrollment is free for up to 11 units per semester.

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form on the CHM internships page to join the mailing list.
notes: CHM says it is not accepting Teen Program applications right now; the page gives no reopening date. Join the interest list to be told when it opens. Pay and length are not stated.
duration: Not stated on the page
pay_detail: Not stated on the page

who_can_apply: Youth 16 and up can make their own volunteer account and sign up for some shifts. Youth 11 to 15 can volunteer with an adult.
how_to_apply: Register as a Food Bank volunteer on its volunteer site. Pick a shift on the calendar. If you are 11 to 15, a parent or guardian signs up too and adds you with the Sign up with a Team button.
notes: The rules for youth come from the Food Bank volunteer FAQ. Youth 5 to 10 can only volunteer at the Family Food Sorts. Youth under 5 cannot volunteer at the Food Bank. Team captains must be 16 or older. The FAQ lists the volunteer help desk as volunteerhelpdesk@foodbankccs.org or 855-309-3663, extension 605. The Food Bank hosts groups too, and a group can send a Group Volunteer Request. Youth 16 and up can sign up for select shifts. The shift details show which ones.
duration: By shift
pay_detail: Volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 21 when you are appointed. You must live in Concord or go to school in Concord. You must be able to serve for one year, September 1 to June 30. Part-time seasonal city workers can apply.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth Commission Application from the city website. Email it to the City Clerk. The adult commissioners pick the youth members.
notes: The commission has five adult members and two youth members. The youth term is one year. The Clerk email is cityclerk@cityofconcord.org. The commission meets at 6 PM as needed at 1950 Parkside Drive, Concord.
duration: One-year term, Sept 1 to June 30
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Youth who are 9 by December 31 of the program year and have not turned 19 by that date can join as regular members. Younger children can join as Primary Members.
how_to_apply: Find a club near you by place and meeting time. Contact the club leader. Then enroll online in the 4-H system linked on the page, or call the County 4-H Office for help. Pick your projects and pay the fee.
notes: Adults who want to volunteer enroll too. Their fee is $30. Adult enrollment opened July 15, 2026. Open the page in a browser to see the club list and the enrollment links.
duration: Program year runs July 1 to June 30; most meetings are August to May
pay_detail: $150 per youth. Financial help is available for youth members.

who_can_apply: Students at West Contra Costa USD, Leadership Public Schools, Griffin Technology Academies, or Middle College High School on campus. Requirements vary by school.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school counselor. Questions: earlycollegecredit@contracosta.edu.
notes: Serves West Contra Costa County (Richmond, San Pablo). No deadlines are listed on the page.
duration: Per term
pay_detail: Free: no tuition, textbook or enrollment fees.

who_can_apply: Summer Read: entering 8th grade or above, with parent consent. Computer Docent and Homework Help: age 16 or older.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer interest form on ccclib.org/volunteer. You may be called for an interview. Forms stay on file for six months.
notes: Contact your branch to see if it is taking volunteers now.
duration: Summer Read 1 to 2 hours a week; Computer Docents at least 2 hours a week

who_can_apply: Youth and young adults ages 16 to 24 who have barriers to finishing school, finding a job or starting a career. The page asks if you have a disability, are low income, or have been in the justice system. Those answers can get you Priority of Service.
how_to_apply: Register on CalJOBS, the state job site linked on the page. Then contact the board at the email or phone number on its site. Ask about youth services.
notes: The board office is at 4071 Port Chicago Highway, Suite 200, Concord. The page lists wdb@ehsd.cccounty.us and (925) 655-3800. The Mt. Diablo school district runs a WIOA youth program for Central County and Bay Point. Its page points East and West County youth to the County Office of Education. See those cards.
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page. The page lists work experience as one kind of help.

who_can_apply: California high school students completing grades 8 to 12. Non-California residents and international students cannot apply. Selected on academic strength and interest in math and science. You pick one campus and cluster choices.
how_to_apply: Online application plus teacher recommendations and parent signature. Pay the application fee. If accepted, pay one-third by Apr 7, 2027 and the rest by Apr 16, 2027.
notes: Competitive. Residential, so you live on campus for four weeks. Financial aid is reviewed separately from admission and needs a parent income document; it has a hard deadline. Program session dates are listed as TBA. Pick UC Davis as your campus on the application. COSMOS runs on several UC campuses (UC Davis, UC Irvine, UC San Diego and UC Santa Cruz); this card is the Davis campus. See the UC COSMOS site for the others: https://jacobs.ucsd.edu/cosmos. The dates page lists the application fee as both $48 and $46, so confirm the amount before paying.
duration: about 4 weeks (2027 dates TBA)
pay_detail: Program cost $5,793 (2027 page), plus $48 application fee and a 2.5% card fee. Financial aid is available for admitted students with need, but not guaranteed.

who_can_apply: California high school students completing grades 8 to 12. Only California high school students can apply. The page says a typical student has a GPA of 3.5 or higher. You apply to one COSMOS campus.
how_to_apply: Apply online by the deadline. You need teacher letters, a parent signature and the fee. If you get in, pay one third first. Pay the rest about a week later.
notes: UC Merced first hosted COSMOS in summer 2026. Each campus takes about 160 to 200 students, so it is competitive. The financial aid deadline has no extensions. All money matters must go through a parent or guardian. COSMOS also runs at UC Davis, UC Irvine, UCLA, UC San Diego and UC Santa Cruz.
duration: 4 weeks, living on campus (July 5 to Aug 1 in 2026)
pay_detail: $5,518 for the four-week program (2026), which covers housing, meals, field trips and activities. $46 application fee. Card payments add a 2.5% fee. Optional financial aid application.

who_can_apply: Students who have finished 8th grade. A parent must send a one-time consent form. Your high school principal signs the concurrent form.
how_to_apply: Apply online to OCC. Pick "Enrolling in High School and College at the same time." Then your parent sends in the consent form. You email the signed Concurrent Enrollment Form to dualenrollment@occ.cccd.edu. Only handwritten signatures count.
notes: The one-time parent consent form is also honored at Golden West College and Coastline College. After you graduate you must re-apply as a first-time college student. Help: fpr@occ.cccd.edu.
duration: By term. Up to 11 units in fall or spring, 10 in summer, 3 in winter.
pay_detail: Per-unit enrollment fees are waived. Concurrent students pay the College Service, Student Health and Student Representation fees plus books and supplies. CCAP classes at high schools may only need textbooks.

who_can_apply: You must be 16 or older. High school students may need a work permit. Lifeguards must get Red Cross lifeguard training within 6 weeks of being hired. Jobs with children need a TB test from the last 2 years.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the city's job board at governmentjobs.com. Pick Community Services Leader or Instructor Lifeguard, then make an account and apply. If you are picked, the city contacts you in 4 to 6 weeks.
notes: The Apply Here link on the city's own page is broken, so go to the job board directly. The lifeguard posting itself shows $10.00 to $12.16 an hour, which is below the state minimum wage and does not match the city salary page, so ask HR. The Police Cadet job needs you to be 18. The city also runs free teen centers for grades 7 to 12. Paid work under 18 in California needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=ca for the steps.
duration: Part time, up to about 20 hours a week. Some jobs are seasonal and some are year-round.
pay_detail: The city salary page lists $20.00 to $24.31 an hour for Community Services Leaders and Instructor Lifeguards.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12 (two separate groups).
how_to_apply: Use the Register HERE link for your committee on the Teen Committees page (cosumnescsd.gov/460/Teen-Committees). Questions: call The Grove Teen Center at 916-405-5622 or email thegrove@Cosumnescsd.gov.
notes: Meeting times, location and deadlines are not posted on the page, so ask the District. Other volunteer roles on that page (adaptive recreation, youth coaching) are 18 and older.
duration: One school year. Teen Action Academy runs September to June; Teen Leadership Committee runs August to May. Meets every other week.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18, high school juniors and seniors, 2.0 GPA, and a physician-completed medical exam form.
how_to_apply: Email explorers@cosumnescsd.gov to get application details. Fire Admin phone: 916-405-7100.
notes: Serves the Elk Grove area. Needs a physician-completed medical exam form. Meeting schedule and any costs are not posted on the page.
duration: School year

who_can_apply: High school students can start at 14. The Solvang hospital is different. It takes teens only at 17 and up.
how_to_apply: Apply online. The link is on the volunteer page. You can also call 805-569-7357. Or email volunteering@sbch.org.
notes: Cottage Health has three hospitals: Santa Barbara, Goleta Valley and Santa Ynez Valley. The pages do not list teen tasks or health checks, so ask the volunteer office. As of Oct 16, 2026, the online form did not load, so it was not read.
duration: About 4 hours a week
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Ages 16 and older. Some departments accept only people 18 and older. Junior volunteers under 18 need a signed parental consent form.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application, then an in-person interview and a health screening. The background check applies to adults only. Questions go to cpmcvolunteer@sutterhealth.org.
notes: Read on the official Sutter Health listing 2026-10-07. Not stated on the listing: TB test or immunization requirements, application window, and pay (unpaid volunteer role). The health screening is required but its contents are not described on this listing. Sutter's separate CPMC student volunteer page could not be read from this environment, so no details from it are used here. The listing is a lobby role, so it fits teens 16 and older who want to try hospital volunteering; it is not a high school program.
duration: Minimum 100 hours in one year, at least three to four hours per week
pay_detail: Volunteer role; no pay stated on the listing

who_can_apply: California residents in grades 8 to 12. Up to 20 students from out of state and other countries may also be enrolled. Each department has its own assignments.
how_to_apply: Apply online by department. A full application has the form and two teacher references, not peers. It has an unofficial transcript and department assignments. It has the $20 fee. It has the financial aid request if you want aid. Students can apply to more than one department. Each needs a full application.
notes: Students who finish can get 3 units of college extension credit from the California State University system (per the FAQ). Not a job. The pages did not name the 2027 campus, so check before planning travel.
duration: About one month: first day of classes July 5 and graduation July 31, 2027
pay_detail: Tuition and fees for California residents were $5,174 for 2026; 2027 rates 'will be posted soon'. Need based aid is available to California residents (nearly half of past students had much of tuition covered). $20 application fee, with fee waivers for students with financial need.

who_can_apply: Teens who will be at least 14 by the first day of in-service training. The page describes it as a program for Cupertino teens. No other residency or school rule is stated.
how_to_apply: The form opens in February. It has a few extra questions. Staff pick teens by their answers, a talk with staff, and the weeks they are free. If you get in, you get a TB test and fingerprints, pay the fee, and sign forms. Ask Robert Kaufman: robertk@cupertino.gov.
notes: You must attend the in-service training week and get yourself to and from program sites. Program assignments come out in late May. The 2027 dates are based on last year's pattern. The page does not list the fee, so ask before you apply.
duration: Volunteers are encouraged to help for 4 to 8 weeks in the summer, after a required in-service training week.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role. The page says payment is collected after you are accepted, and your spot can be taken back if fees are not paid on time. The fee amount is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Students in 9th to 12th grade for that school year who are at least 14. No residency rule is stated.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application, including two short questions (300 words max each). You hear back after the next review period.
notes: Some events fall on holidays, weekends, and evenings. Members who do more events are recognized at Bronze, Silver, and Gold levels.
duration: School year. Members help at 2 or more major events and 2 or more minor events, and go to monthly meetings.

who_can_apply: Anyone ages 14 to 18 may apply. You must be at least 14 by the first day of training. Space is limited.
how_to_apply: Send the form, the signed volunteer agreement, and your answers to a few extra questions. Staff pick teens by their answers, a talk with staff (mid April in 2026), and the times you are free. Late forms are not taken.
notes: You must attend all training, be fingerprinted and cleared, and bring your own ride (VTA and Silicon Valley Hopper are options). Staff can sign off on service hours. 2027 dates will likely follow the 2026 pattern.
duration: In 2026: training on June 8, then a 2-hour shift every week from June 10 to August 7.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role. If picked, you pay $30 to cover fingerprinting, a program shirt, a name tag, and training materials.

who_can_apply: Cupertino residents who are in 7th to 10th grade now. The city page says seniors are not eligible to apply.
how_to_apply: When recruitment is open, use the 'Apply to be a Teen Commissioner' form on the city page. The page also links a supplemental questions list. Questions about applications go to cityclerk@cupertino.gov.
notes: Meets monthly, September through May, at 6 p.m. on the second Wednesday. It meets in the Quinlan Community Center Conference Room (10185 North Stelling Road), with a teleconference option. Commission email teencommission@cupertino.gov. Staff liaison Sonya Lee, Recreation Manager, (408) 777-3121. Pay is not mentioned on the page, so it is listed as unpaid. The page says members may be in 12th grade during their term. The 8th-to-11th rule applies to applicants.
duration: Two-year staggered terms

who_can_apply: Students in grades 8 to 11 for the next school year. Anyone in those grades may apply. Students who live in Cupertino get picked first.
how_to_apply: Answer four short questions (up to 300 words each). Send one letter from someone who is not family, on their work paper, to robertk@cupertino.gov. Share a one minute YouTube video about you. It can be private or unlisted. Late items are not taken.
notes: Past events: Hack Cupertino, Pizza and Politics, a teen speaker series and the Cupertino Spelling Bee. Members plan an event about every other month. The 2027 last day is not posted. Last year it closed in early May.
duration: One school-year term (for example, the 2027-28 term).

who_can_apply: Volunteers 12 years and up. If a posting has its own age rule, it is listed in that posting. Volunteers under 18 need a parent or guardian to sign the Volunteer Agreement.
how_to_apply: Make a volunteer profile on the town website. Look at the open events and service projects. Sign up for one. For a long project, you send an interest form and town staff contact you.
notes: The Teens page says the town has volunteer chances for ages 13 and up. The volunteer page says 12 and up. Check each posting. Verification of community service hours is emailed by request after a volunteer event.
duration: One-time events or longer projects
pay_detail: Volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Any Danville resident can join. So can any student enrolled in a Danville middle school or high school. The page gives no age range.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Danville Youth Council application. It is an online form linked on the program page.
notes: Meetings are at the Town Offices, 500 La Gonda Way, Danville. The Teens page says the Town is recruiting for part-time positions in youth and teen programming. It does not give an age for those jobs.
duration: Monthly meetings, September to May
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Lifeguard Training: you must turn 15 by the last day of the class. On day one you take a swim test. Swim 150 yards, tread water 2 minutes with only your legs, then swim 50 yards. You also bring up a 10 pound brick in a timed test. Junior Lifeguarding and Junior Swim Instructor are for 11 to 15 year olds. Junior Lifeguarding has a swim check on day one.
how_to_apply: Register for a course through City of Davis online registration (the page links to it). Questions: 530-757-5626 or csweb@cityofdavis.org.
notes: These classes can lead to city pool jobs. Junior Swim Instructor is for teens who may want to work for Davis Aquatics later. You may get to volunteer after the class. The page does not promise a job. To get a lifeguard card, you must come to every class and pass the tests. City lifeguard jobs start at 15. Swim teacher jobs start at 15, or 14 if you did Junior Swim Instructor. That is from the 2026 job posts. See the City of Davis Seasonal Lifeguard and Swim Instructor Jobs card.
duration: varies by course
pay_detail: Summer 2026 fees: Lifeguard Training $275, Junior Lifeguard Training $185, Junior Swim Instructor $100. Check the current Rec Guide or online registration for new prices.

who_can_apply: Age 15 or older to officiate or keep score, and 16 or older to coach. You need CPR and First Aid certification before the season starts and a working knowledge of basketball rules.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the City of Davis job page (NEOGOV). Applicants are screened on experience and may be interviewed.
notes: Temporary part-time with no benefits. Games are Saturdays at the Davis High School community gyms. Other City of Davis seasonal postings such as Parks Maintenance Aide (18 and older) and Pool Maintenance Aide (21 and older) are not open to teens.
duration: 6-week season starting the week of January 18, 2027
pay_detail: $17.39 an hour

who_can_apply: RLIT: ages 13 to 15. Returning RLIT: ages 13 to 16, only if you finished RLIT before and were invited back. Outdoor Education Volunteer: ages 14 to 16 in the Summer 2026 RecGuide (the 2026 Summer Camp Handbook says 13 to 16); you need your own bike and helmet and must ride at least 10 miles a day. RLITs must clear a local records check.
how_to_apply: RLIT: sign up on the city's WebTrac site when summer sign ups open. Returning RLITs must be approved first. Outdoor Education Volunteer: fill out the online form. The link is on the city's volunteer page. Then go to a group interview. Questions? Call 530-757-5626 or email csweb@cityofdavis.org.
notes: These facts come from the Summer 2026 Rec Guide and the 2026 camp handbook. The summer 2027 guide is not out yet. After RLIT, you go on a list for more volunteer hours. You may be asked back as a returning volunteer. The city's paid camp leader job starts at 15. So RLIT is a good first step. You need a bike and helmet for RLIT and Outdoor Education. Davis residents sign up first. Others sign up the next Monday. As of Oct 16, 2026, the volunteer page did not list camp volunteers.
duration: RLIT 2026: Session 1 June 15 to July 2, Session 2 July 13 to 31, Monday to Friday 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m., with week three spent volunteering at a camp (about 30 hours, 8:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.). Outdoor Education Volunteers work at least three weeks between June 15 and August 21.
pay_detail: Unpaid, and there is a program fee. Summer 2026 fees: RLIT $247 (Session 1) or $264 (Session 2). Returning RLIT $66. Outdoor Education Volunteer $122, paid only after you are accepted.

who_can_apply: Lifeguard: 15 or older. You must pass a swim skills test before you start. When hired, you need Red Cross Lifeguard Training with First Aid, CPR and AED. You also need First Aid for Public Safety (Title 22). Swim Instructor: 15 or older, or 14 if you did the city's Junior Swim Instructor class. You must be at ease in the water. You need some time spent with kids. Babysitting, tutoring, camp or volunteering counts.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the city's NEOGOV jobs page. Paper forms are not taken. If you get an interview, lifeguards must turn in their cards. The best fits get an interview, alone or in a small group. Everyone who applies hears back by email.
notes: 2026 mandatory trainings: lifeguards the weekend of May 16 and 17 and the week of June 15 to 18; swim instructors May 2 and 3 and June 15 to 18.
