You must be free on those dates to be considered. Lifeguard shifts fall between 7:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m., any day of the week, and planned vacation is capped at 14 days and must be approved before summer. To get certified first, the city's Red Cross Lifeguard Training course needs you to be 15 by the last day of the course (summer 2026 fee $275, per the Summer 2026 RecGuide). The Off-Season Lifeguard job (fall to spring) needs weekday morning and noon availability. Paid work under 18 needs a California work permit.
duration: 2026 pool season: May 18 to September 7 for lifeguards. Swim lessons ran May 18 to August 16, 2026.
pay_detail: 2026 rates: Lifeguard $17.83 to $18.27 per hour. Swim Instructor $16.97 to $17.39 per hour. Temporary part-time, no benefits.

who_can_apply: DJUSD high school students. The page does not list which schools offer which pathway. Ask your counselor.
how_to_apply: Contact your school counselor to enroll in a CTE course. Internships are on the Student Internships tab. See the Internship and Career Development Course.
notes: Page does not say which schools offer which pathways, or give grade or age rules. DJUSD office: (530) 757-5300. Related: the Internship and Career Development Course and the Summer Apprenticeship.
pay_detail: School classes, no pay. Course credit.

who_can_apply: Summer Playgrounds camps (Rainbow Summer, Summer Quest, Kids in the Kitchen, Arts and Crafts, Kinder Camp, PM Kids Club, Teen Camp): 15 or older before camp starts. Outdoor camps (Camp Putah, Summer Sampler, Backyard Adventures): 16 or older. You must own a bike and ride up to 10 miles a day. Both jobs need CPR and First Aid cards before camp starts.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the city's NEOGOV jobs page. Paper forms are not taken. Good fits get an email to set up an interview. In 2026, Summer Playgrounds picks had to be free on Friday, March 13 for a group interview day.
notes: In 2026, all staff had to come to training on June 6. More trainings ran June 1 to 13. Staff also met on Monday or Tuesday nights in summer and took online trainings. Other leader jobs open to teens: Inclusion Recreation Leader (2025 post: 15 for level I, 16 for level II, open Jan 22 to Apr 1, 2025). There is also a fall leader job for the Davis Children's Nutcracker. It needs you to be 15 with a work permit and pays $16.97 an hour. The 2026 post ran Aug 31 to Sep 28, 2026, and the work runs Nov 9 to Dec 13. Senior leader and Camp Putah leader jobs need you to be 18 or a high school grad. Paid work under 18 needs a California work permit.
duration: June through August. 2026 camps ran ten weeks, June 15 to August 21, Monday to Friday. Summer Playgrounds shifts fall between 7:30 a.m. and 6:00 p.m. (schedules vary).
pay_detail: 2026: $16.97 per hour (Community Services Specialist I). Temporary part-time, no benefits.

who_can_apply: Davis teens ages 14 to 17. Up to 24 members. Needs a full school-year commitment.
how_to_apply: Fill out the TLC application on the Teens page. Questions: Micayla Valceschini, mvalceschini@cityofdavis.org.
notes: Meetings are at the Veterans Memorial Center, 203 E. 14th St. Up to 24 teens, and it is a full school-year commitment. The application closed Oct 2, so ask the city whether late applicants can still join.
duration: Oct 13, 2026 to May 18, 2027, meets 2nd and 4th Tuesdays, 7:00 to 8:30 pm

who_can_apply: Students enrolled in any California high school, grades 9 to 12 (rising 9th graders included). Needs permission from a parent or guardian and your school principal. No GPA requirement.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor, apply for admission, set up MyPortal, finish the Dual Enrollment overview, check prerequisites, submit the school permission form, then register. Questions: outreach@deanza.edu.
notes: Math and English classes need an assessment (usually based on your school transcript). Students can buy a VTA SmartPass for unlimited bus and light rail rides. Undocumented students can take part. Parents cannot see your college records without your written consent.
duration: Quarter system (fall, winter, spring, summer); a standard class is 12 weeks
pay_detail: No enrollment fees for up to 11 units a quarter (De Anza and Foothill combined). You still pay for textbooks in most courses and may pay other fees.

who_can_apply: High school students join through a school chapter and its advisor, or a school can start a chapter. Contact the DECA advisor at your school.
how_to_apply: Ask your school for a DECA advisor. DECA lists an Online Membership System for joining.
notes: DECA says it has about 317,600 high school members in 4,510 chapters. Not every school has a chapter. California-specific details were not on the page.
duration: School year
pay_detail: Not stated on the program pages. Ask your advisor for chapter dues and conference fees.

who_can_apply: High school students, including home-schooled students. You need a Special Admissions Recommendation Form each term. You, a parent, and your principal or their designee must sign it. Students on an F-1 international visa cannot be in high school and DVC at the same time.
how_to_apply: Apply to DVC. After you are accepted, submit the Special Admissions Recommendation Form in the student portal. List the classes you want. Then check prerequisites and sign up for classes.
notes: A signed form with no classes listed is not accepted. You can only sign up for the classes listed on the form. If you use a school district program such as dual enrollment, follow that program instead. Not sure which one to use? Ask your counselor.
duration: By term
pay_detail: California high school students pay no tuition. You pay student union fees and the cost of class materials.

who_can_apply: High school students in a partner school district: Acalanes, Martinez (Alhambra High School), Mt. Diablo, or San Ramon Valley. Clayton Valley Charter High School also takes part. Each program has its own steps, so talk to your counselor.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school counselor first. Then follow the steps for your school district on the DVC page. Questions go to the Early College Credit office at DVC.
notes: College Now is a middle-college program for Mt. Diablo 11th and 12th graders. Classes are at the DVC Pleasant Hill campus. CollegeConnect lets students earn up to 30 college units before they graduate. Diamante Scholars is a separate program for Mt. Diablo seniors. The page lists the Early College Credit email as EarlyCollegeCredit@dvc.edu.
duration: Classes by school term
pay_detail: Free. You pay no tuition, textbook or enrollment fees.

who_can_apply: The classes are made for high school students. In summer they are open to all students. You must come every day. Fields include animation, business, computer programming, health, robotics and trades.
how_to_apply: Apply to DVC for summer. Then send the Special Admissions Recommendation Form, signed by you, a parent and your counselor. Then sign up for your academy in the student portal. Use the interest form on the page for updates.
notes: Health is at the Pleasant Hill and San Ramon campuses. The Special Admissions form is for students who are not graduating this spring or earlier. Public Safety is mainly for teens and new graduates who want to be police explorers or cadets.
duration: Short courses of about 1 to 2 weeks. In 2026, Health ran July 27 to 31 and Public Safety ran July 6 to 17.
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the academies page.

who_can_apply: Teen volunteers, around age 15 and up. The page says a 14-year-old may start the application one month before their 15th birthday. The page does not state a maximum age.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application for a role. The roles are Exhibit Host, Team Spark and Team Celebration. Email a resume and a letter from an adult who is not family. Send them to VolunteerLA@discoverycube.org. Then do an interview and a mandatory orientation.
notes: The museum is in Sylmar in the San Fernando Valley. The letter of recommendation cannot come from a family member. Questions: 818-686-2835.
duration: Minimum 60 hours; two 4-hour shifts every 30 days
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: The page gives one age rule: if you are 14, you may start the application process one month before your 15th birthday. No grade level is stated.
how_to_apply: Online application form, a resume, a letter of recommendation, then an interview. The full application must be in before an interview is scheduled.
notes: Plan for the 60-hour minimum if you need service hours that are checked. Location: 2500 N Main Street, Santa Ana, CA 92705. Questions: volunteeroc@discoverycube.org.
duration: At least one four-hour shift every 30 days. 60 hours of service before the Cube verifies your hours.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page lists no fees.

who_can_apply: Davis Joint Unified high school students. Some sites have priority rules (Dignity Health for Patient Care pathway students; Ford ACE for Transportation pathway students).
how_to_apply: Talk to your counselor or contact Internship Specialist Alexha Contreras (alcontreras@djusd.net, 530-757-5400 x170).
notes: Many other 2026-27 host sites are listed on the page; some have priority rules (Mercy General: Patient Care pathway students; Ford ACE: Transportation pathway students). Credit needs weekly meetings, an evaluation and a reflection. The page is written for DJUSD students.
pay_detail: Unpaid internships; course credit with evaluation and reflection required.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 and up for Community Programs, Special Events and Sports Leagues. You do not have to live in Dublin. Volunteers under 18 need a signed parent consent form. Younger kids can join park cleanup projects with an adult.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the city's volunteer posting (you make a free account). Staff review your application within 2 business days and reply within 8 business days. Then go to orientation and start your shift. Questions: recreation@dublin.ca.gov or (925) 556-4500.
notes: The city guide says Splatter (September) has short shifts that are good for teens. Volunteer coaches must have AED certification. Staff can write a letter verifying your hours for school or clubs; allow 5 to 7 business days. The Special Events listing on the volunteer page said 'currently unavailable' on Oct 16, 2026.
duration: Community Programs: ongoing, a set day and shift weekly, every other week or monthly (Senior Center shifts are usually 2 to 4 hours). Special Events: one-time shifts. Sports: one season.

who_can_apply: Teens entering 7th grade or higher. Complete the online application; staff review it and then tell you how to register. The page lists separate fees for Dublin residents and non-residents.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application when it is open (closed for 2026). Staff review it and then tell you how to register at dublinrecguide.com. Questions: Dublin.Lead@dublin.ca.gov.
notes: This is a fee-based training and volunteer-style program run by the city, not a paid job. Families pay the registration fee; the city page does not say teens are paid. The page does not name a residency rule for applying. Shifts are not pre-assigned; participants pick their own shifts in the registration system.
duration: The 2026 program ran June 8, 2026 to August 7, 2026. Participants are encouraged to help with recreation or aquatics programs for at least two weeks.
pay_detail: Registration fee for the 2026 program: $119 for Dublin residents, $143 for non-residents. No wage is stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Students in high school with a program idea. Programs must be free, open to the public and non-commercial. You may not sell or promote products or collect attendees' contact info.
how_to_apply: Fill out the library's online Program Proposal form, linked on the event page, before the window closes. A proposal does not guarantee a spot.
notes: The page does not say if presenters are paid; treat it as unpaid. Library programs are booked at least 3 months ahead. The proposal windows open on the third Monday of their months. Questions: dublin@aclibrary.org or (925) 803-7252.
duration: One program you lead. Presentation dates are set later.

who_can_apply: Students ages 14 to 18 interested in criminal justice. You must pass a background check and have parent consent. Up to 25 teens.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form linked on the Teen Academy page. Questions? Call the Crime Prevention Unit at 925-833-6677 or 925-833-6686.
notes: It used to be called the Youth Academy. The 2026 form is on the city site. A new form will likely go up for 2027. The police office is at 6361 Clark Avenue, Dublin.
duration: One week. In 2026 it ran June 8 to 12, 9 a.m. to noon.
pay_detail: Free.

who_can_apply: Must live in the City of Dublin and be enrolled in middle or high school (committee bylaws). The committee has 13 members and 3 alternates; at least 6 members must be high school students.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the city page. Call Parks and Community Services at 925-556-4500 or use the contact link on the committee page to ask when the next recruitment opens.
notes: Meets 7:00 pm, second Wednesday of the month, Dublin Senior Center, 7600 Amador Valley Blvd; July and August meet only as needed. Bylaws say members must stay enrolled in middle or high school, and a member is removed if they stop living in Dublin or stop being enrolled. Older (2020 and 2021) notices mention late-winter recruitment; that is last-cycle information and was not confirmed for 2027. Teens who want a seat should check the city page each spring.
duration: One-year term. The 2026-27 members are listed for June 2026 to May 2027.
pay_detail: Volunteer committee seat. No pay is stated on the city page.

who_can_apply: Not stated.
how_to_apply: The home page has a Sign Up button for volunteers, but the volunteer page it links to showed a 404 error on 2026-10-09. Contact EBAYC directly (offices in Oakland and Sacramento are listed on the home page).
notes: Read the home page on 2026-10-09. It says EBAYC has many volunteer opportunities and welcomes volunteer groups and student internships, but it gives no ages, dates or pay. The volunteer page linked from it (ebayc.org/volunteer/) returned a 404 error on Oct 7 and again on Oct 9, 2026. Confirm the minimum age with EBAYC.

who_can_apply: High school students in the EBMUD service area. For 2026 the East Bay program took students referred by partner groups. The Maintenance track (Stockton) required age 16 by June 24, 2026.
how_to_apply: In 2026 you could not apply to EBMUD directly for the East Bay program. Ask a partner to refer you: ACE Mentor, Biotech Partners, Eden Area ROP, Girls Inc. of Alameda County, Youth UpRising. Email internships@ebmud.com, (510) 287-0710.
notes: Referral only in 2026. Separate Mokelumne programs (Fisheries in Lodi, Ranger in Valley Springs, Maintenance in Stockton) ran in 2026 with rolling review.
duration: 6 weeks, mid-June through August, about 16 hours a week
pay_detail: Paid stipend (amount not posted)

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17. The program page does not list a swim test or a home city rule.
how_to_apply: Download the Junior Cadet application packet from the program page. Turn it in by the deadline. If you are picked, register by the second deadline.
notes: This is a training class, not a paid job. Sessions are full day only. The program page does not list session dates. It also lists Junior Lifeguards for ages 8 to 12 and Junior Lifeguard Aides for ages 13 to 15, with no details. Call 1-888-327-2757. For lifeguard jobs at age 16 and older, see the district lifeguard jobs page.
duration: 2 weeks per session, about 4 sessions each summer
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the program page. Financial aid is offered through the Regional Parks Foundation Campership program.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17. The program page does not list a grade or home city rule.
how_to_apply: Apply when applications open in 2027. If you are picked after the interview, you then register for the week. Ask about the $30 scholarship through the park district financial aid line.
notes: The program page says teens earn 35 community service hours, build job skills and may get a future camp job. It does not name the parks. Contact: Stewart Reid, Recreation Coordinator, 510-544-2558. Financial aid: 1-888-327-2757, option 2.
duration: 1 week
pay_detail: $50 for the one week. A limited number of $30 scholarships are available. The page lists 35 community service hours and does not mention pay.

who_can_apply: You must be 16 or older when the Lifeguard Academy starts in late April. You must swim 550 yards in 10 minutes or less. The district also tests a deep dive and carrying a 150 pound person in open water.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application on the park district job portal. Pick the lifeguard posting. You must be free for all 10 days of the academy.
notes: Lifeguard I is the entry job at age 16. Head lifeguard jobs need age 18 and a finished 12th grade. The program page does not say if a work permit is needed for 16 and 17 year olds, so ask HR. The district also lists younger water programs: Junior Lifeguard Aides (ages 13 to 15) and Jr Lifeguard Cadets (ages 14 to 17), with no details on that page. Call 1-888-327-2757.
duration: 10 day paid academy, then a seasonal job
pay_detail: Paid. The program page says a competitive wage but gives no hourly rate. The 10 day Lifeguard Academy is paid, so there is no tuition.

who_can_apply: Gate Attendant (high school pathway): at least 16 and completed 10th grade. Other jobs have their own rules; check each posting.
how_to_apply: Apply on governmentjobs.com/careers/ebparks. HR: (510) 544-2154.
notes: The 16 minimum is from the Gate Attendant page; other roles (for example lifeguard) may differ. The park district says it hires hundreds of seasonal students each year.
duration: Seasonal
pay_detail: Pay is not posted on the youth pages. See each job posting.

who_can_apply: Berkeley residents ages 15 to 24, recruited through Berkeley YouthWorks.
how_to_apply: Apply through the City of Berkeley YouthWorks interest form (the Ecology Center sends you there). Contact alex@ecologycenter.org or 510-697-4808.
notes: Berkeley residents only. YouthWorks asks for an interest form and a 15 to 20 minute interview. Pay rate and exact academy dates are not posted.
duration: 8 weeks (summer) or 12 weeks (spring)
pay_detail: Paid; rate not posted

who_can_apply: Juniors and seniors attending high school in the Castro Valley, Hayward, San Leandro or San Lorenzo Unified school districts.
how_to_apply: Ask your home high school counselor to contact the Eden Area ROP career counselor at (510) 293-2973. Main office (510) 293-2900.
notes: Center is at 26316 Hesperian Blvd, Hayward. Cost, pay and ages are not stated on the page. Some pathways are offered only at certain high schools. Students outside the four districts are not listed as eligible. Work-based learning is mentioned (for example in education careers) but no formal internship structure is described.
duration: Classes are held Monday to Friday; course length varies by class
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Any high school student who has finished freshman year.
how_to_apply: The volunteer office takes names in April, according to a November 2025 article. The article gives no form or phone number for the junior program. The hospital main phone is 760-340-3911.
notes: Confirm first: the dates come from a November 2025 article, not a page. The Volunteers page does not mention the junior program, and the number 760-773-1304 appears on it with no label.
duration: One shift a week from June orientation to the end of July
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Qualified students in grades 9 to 12 who can benefit from college classes. No age rule is listed.
how_to_apply: Do the Steps for Dual Enrollment each term you want to register. The steps are listed on a separate page. Call 310-660-3344 or email dualenrollment@elcamino.edu.
notes: Unit limits are not on this page. Dual enrollment uses Remind to post updates for students.
duration: By term
pay_detail: Enrollment fees are waived for dual enrollment students.

who_can_apply: Age 14 or older and done with 8th grade. One-year minimum. No summer internships or programs shorter than one year. Selection starts with an annual application seminar.
how_to_apply: Go to the yearly sign up meeting first. Then apply. The steps are on the El Camino Health junior volunteer page.
notes: Read again on 2026-10-16. There is no summer only option. Once you are in, you can stay through the summer after you graduate. Call Mountain View at 650-940-7214 or Los Gatos at 408-866-3940. Check the page in mid January 2027 to sign up for the next junior meeting.
duration: At least 1 year
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program; no cost stated on the page

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 18 with at least an average C grade or better in school. You can stay in the Post until your 21st birthday. A criminal record does not always block you, but every applicant gets a background check. The form has a line for a parent or guardian to sign.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Police Explorers application, a PDF on the city website. Give three reasons you want to join. A parent or guardian signs it too. Every applicant gets a background check.
notes: The paper application has a line for a Social Security number. Ask the department why before you write it down, and never send it by email. The form has no date, so ask the department if it is the current one. The same page lists a paid Cadet Program for college students. It also lists Volunteers in Police Service for adults 18 and older.
duration: At least 12 hours a month
pay_detail: Explorers donate at least 12 hours a month, counted every quarter. The department buys the uniform. You bring your own shoes or boots.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18 who go to El Cerrito High School or live in El Cerrito. A parent or guardian must give written consent. You can serve until your 19th birthday or until you graduate from El Cerrito High School.
how_to_apply: Submit the youth application on the city page. A parent or guardian must give written consent. Applicants will be invited to interview with the City Council at a publicly noticed meeting. The City Clerk handles questions.
notes: Ten city groups want a youth member. They include the Park and Recreation Commission, the Planning Commission and the Committee on Aging. The full list is on the page. Youth members must follow attendance rules and do orientation training. They also take a one-hour harassment prevention training. City Clerk phone: 510-215-4305.
duration: Until age 19 or graduation
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Youth appointed by the Mayor with City Council approval (10 voting seats). The page does not list ages or grades. A city factsheet in search results reportedly said ages 13 to 18, grades 7 to 12, but that is unconfirmed. The City tries to balance seats by school and council district.
how_to_apply: When a seat opens, use the Apply to the Youth Commission link (City Clerk vacancies page). Questions: youthcommission@elkgrove.gov or (916) 627-3254.
notes: Age and grade rules were not on the pages, so confirm with the City before applying. Appointed seats, so competitive. Sign up for vacancy emails on elkgrove.gov to hear when a recruitment opens. Re-checked on 2026-10-09: the City page returned HTTP 403, so it could not be read again and the card stays snippet-only.
duration: Meets 2nd Tuesday, Sept to May, 6:00 pm, Elk Grove Council Chambers

who_can_apply: You must be enrolled in high school. New applicants are interviewed. A non-parent adult must fill out your reference form.
how_to_apply: Fill out the LIT application on the program page. Your reference fills out the reference form. Staff set up interviews after both are in. You must come to a training of about 1.5 hours before each camp.
notes: Camps are held in Newport Beach and Modjeska Canyon. Students, not parents, must talk to ENC staff. Returning LITs do not need to interview again. Bring school paperwork on your last day.
duration: Winter Nature Camps: December 21 to 23 and December 28 to 31, 2026
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program.

who_can_apply: Local teens. The page does not give an age range or grade rule.
how_to_apply: Get the Teen Advisory Board form from the page as a PDF. You can also pick one up at the Youth Services Desk on the 2nd floor. Email the finished form to teens@escondidolibrary.org (shown on the page).
notes: Phone for the Teen Services Librarian: 760-839-4283 (listed on the page with a call-to-ask-questions note). Page lists no age range or cost.
duration: 2026-2027 school year; meetings on the second Monday of each month, 4:30 to 5:30 p.m.
pay_detail: Not stated

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 14. Volunteers need fingerprinting and a background check. Review Crew and Teen Advisory Board members do not need them. You must have an interview with the Volunteer Coordinator. The library does not accept court-ordered community service.
how_to_apply: Go to the City of Escondido volunteer website. Fill out the application there. You can call or email the City Community Engagement Liaison with questions. The number is 760-839-4523.
notes: Some roles on the page are for adults only. They are shelver, Friends shop and literacy tutor. The Review Crew and Teen Advisory Board do not need fingerprinting or a background check.
duration: A regular schedule is expected
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens on the Review Crew earn 1 community service hour for every 2 qualifying book reviews.

who_can_apply: California students without a high school diploma or GED. You need approval from your school counselor or principal.
how_to_apply: Submit the dual enrollment application, get your high school counselor or principal to approve, then enroll. Counseling: mycounselor@evc.edu, 408-270-6475.
notes: CCAP classes are closed cohort classes held at partner high schools, so ask your school if it has an agreement. The page does not state a grade or age rule. Textbook costs for non-CCAP students are not stated.
duration: By semester
pay_detail: No enrollment fees for dual enrollment students; material fees are waived for CCAP students only

who_can_apply: 11th graders at high schools that EXP supports. The 2025-2026 list includes Carson, Gardena, Lawndale, San Pedro, Phineas Banning and Sato Academy. It also lists some Long Beach schools: Cabrillo, Jordan, Lakewood, Long Beach Poly and Wilson. Some schools in Orange County and Barstow are listed too.
how_to_apply: You cannot apply to the Port directly; placement goes through EXP. Ask your school counselor if your school is an EXP school, or email internship@expfuture.org.
notes: Only for students at partner schools. Phone: 424.368.7100. The Port of Los Angeles Summer Internship (10 weeks, paid) is college students only. The page does not mention work permits.
duration: Port of LA placement is 2 to 6 weeks; other placements not stated
pay_detail: EXP lists 171 paid internships for Summer 2026. The hourly pay is not stated.

who_can_apply: Local high school students. Past interns came from Davis Senior High, Dixon High and Natomas Pacific Pathways Prep.
how_to_apply: No application process is posted. Use the contact page on the Facciotti Lab site to email the lab with a short note about your interests.
notes: Informal opportunity with no posted process, pay, dates or contact on that page. The lab names a partner teacher at Davis Senior High and lists one current intern, so openings may be rare.
pay_detail: Pay not stated. Ask the lab.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 15. Space is limited. Register in WebTrac.
how_to_apply: Register through Folsom WebTrac.
notes: Source is the city's May 22, 2026 news post, which does not list a fee or the 2027 dates. Held at Oak Chan Elementary School. Check the Folsom Parks and Recreation site and WebTrac in spring 2027.
duration: 8 weekly sessions (2026: June 8 to July 31, Mon to Fri 8:30 to 4:00)
pay_detail: Fee not stated in the news post.

who_can_apply: Any current high school student in grades 9 to 12. Apply to Foothill, then submit the Special Admit form signed by a parent or guardian and your high school principal or administrator. Meet course prerequisites; talk to your high school counselor.
how_to_apply: Apply for admission to Foothill, submit the Special Admit form (parent and principal signatures, plus an unofficial transcript if asked), register, and pay any fees. Admissions: (650) 949-7325.
notes: Foothill can give a free Clipper SmartPass for VTA buses and light rail. Undocumented students are welcome. Grades go on your permanent college record, and your parents cannot see college records. Partner-district options also exist: Middle College, College Now! (MVLA), Firebird Academy (Fremont Union).
duration: One quarter at a time
pay_detail: No cost up to 11 units in a regular quarter (6 in summer), counting Foothill and De Anza together. Textbooks and other fees are not covered.

who_can_apply: Anyone 16 or older. Those 18 and over also pass a background check and need a valid Social Security number. You commit to 150 hours a year.
how_to_apply: Fill out the PDF application form and email it to the Volunteer Office. Then do an interview, an orientation, two TB tests and a flu shot.
notes: Volunteer Office: (714) 378-7000, Mon to Fri 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Patient Care Pavilion, 18111 Brookhurst St. The application PDF was not checked.
duration: 150 hours per year
pay_detail: Unpaid. If accepted you pay a $25 registration fee.

who_can_apply: High school students. The page says all Fremont high school students are welcome.
how_to_apply: Go to the volunteer portal page. Click Fill in an application. If you already volunteer through MyImpactPage.com, log in. Questions: ebuchanan@aclibrary.org.
notes: Some events in the community need extra forms. They also have a separate sign up.
duration: Tuesdays 4:00 to 6:00 p.m. (October 13, 20 and 27, 2026 listed)

who_can_apply: High school students in the Fremont, New Haven or Newark school districts. Charter, home school and independent study students should call to ask about the price.
how_to_apply: Sign up during pre-registration at your home school. Ask your school counselor, College and Career Specialist or Career Center for help with scheduling. Buses take students to and from the ROP center.
notes: Center is at 5019 Stevenson Blvd, Fremont. Phone (510) 657-1865. College credit partners named on the site: Chabot, Las Positas, Mission, Ohlone and Universal Technical Institute. Grade levels are not stated on the pages. The site's jobs page for high schoolers only links to Indeed and a company careers page.
pay_detail: Free for students in those three districts.

who_can_apply: Teens 14 to 18 when they join. You must be in high school or have finished it. You need a C+ (2.5) grade average and must turn in report cards each term. No school discipline in the last year for things like theft, bullying or violence.
how_to_apply: When it opens, send four things: a one page essay on why you want to join, your latest report card, the Teen Volunteer Application and the Explorer application. Then you have an interview and a background check. Questions: (510) 790-6691.
notes: The background check takes about 1 to 2 months. You must go to the first three meetings. If you are not accepted, you can apply again after one year.
duration: Weekly meetings and training. New Explorers do a 4 to 6 month field training and a one week academy in San Diego their first summer.
pay_detail: This is a volunteer program. The program page does not mention pay.

who_can_apply: Each job lists its own age. Sports Instructor jobs are for ages 15 and up. Cooking, After School and Facility jobs are for ages 18 and up. You do not need work experience.
how_to_apply: Look at the current openings and apply online. No work experience? List volunteer work, clubs, group projects and sports teams. Questions: (510) 494-4347.
notes: Workers must get CPR, First Aid and AED training within 30 days of being hired. The city offers classes. Fingerprints and a TB test are also required. See each job description for the full list.
duration: Seasonal and year-round part-time jobs, with day, evening and weekend shifts.
pay_detail: These are paid part-time jobs. The program page does not list the pay; each job posting has the details.

who_can_apply: Age 14 and up. Teens aged 14 and 15 must come with an adult who also registers as a volunteer. Under 14 is not accepted.
how_to_apply: Create an account at volunteer.tcvfoodbank.org, sign the Volunteer Handbook and Consent forms, then sign up for shifts. Email volunteer@tcvfoodbank.org or call 510-598-4066.
notes: TCV does not sign court or traffic ticket hours. The page did not say whether school service hours are signed, so ask. Orientation was not mentioned on this page.

who_can_apply: Students at Fremont Unified middle and high schools. The page says limited English is not a barrier to joining career and technical education programs.
how_to_apply: The page gives no sign-up steps. Ask your school counselor or principal, or contact Leslie Heller, Director of Secondary Education, (510) 659-2513.
notes: The page is general. It lists 15 industry sectors and 58 career pathways. It does not list internship partners or work-based learning. Ask your counselor which pathways your school offers.
pay_detail: Not stated on the page

who_can_apply: The page does not state ages, grades or residency rules. Ask the Recreation Division.
how_to_apply: The page does not explain how to apply. Call the Recreation Division at 510-494-4300.
notes: Meets 6:30 to 8:30 p.m. on the first Monday of each month except July and August, at City Hall, 3300 Capitol Ave. The page lists 12 members.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17.
how_to_apply: Fill out the VolunTeens Application linked on the zoo's support page. Group questions: volunteer@fcz.org.
notes: Fresno is in the Central Valley, outside Merced County. The page uses one application link for both VolunTeens and the junior camp counselor role.
duration: Year-round; 1-day training
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Jr. Camp Counselor Application linked on the zoo's support page.
notes: Listed on the zoo's volunteer page; pay is not stated. Fresno is in the Central Valley, outside Merced County.
duration: Summer camp weeks; hours not stated
pay_detail: Not stated; listed on the zoo's volunteer page.

who_can_apply: Teens 15 and older use the teen application. The page puts a star by the age and does not explain it, so ask the city.
how_to_apply: Use the teen form on the city volunteer page. Fill it out. Then email it to the city. The address is FullertonCenter@cityoffullerton.com.
notes: Most volunteers help with day to day youth programs and events, or as needed. The page says the work can count for school community service or internship requirements. Adults 18 and up use a separate application. The Fullerton Public Library has its own teen volunteer program.
duration: Seasonal: fall, winter and spring, and summer
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Students going into grades 7 to 12.
how_to_apply: Attend a Teen Advisory Board meeting or submit a book review. The page does not describe a sign-up form. Allow up to 7 business days after an activity for your credit to show. Call (714) 773-5719.
notes: Easy way to start earning service hours. The Teen Advisory Board page on the same site has more detail; it was not read.
duration: Board meets on the first and third Tuesday of each month at 6 p.m. (starting Sept 1, 2026)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Earns volunteer service hours (1 hour per meeting or approved review).

who_can_apply: High school students age 15 and over. The hospital picks based on your application. It looks at whether you can keep the weekly commitment. It also looks at your school background and career interests. There is no job shadowing or internship.
how_to_apply: When applications open, contact St. Jude volunteer services at Stjudevolunteers@providence.org or 714-992-3000 ext. 2878. Questions should come from the student. Accepted volunteers must go to an orientation and get a health screening. This takes about one month in all.
notes: Questions: Stjudevolunteers@providence.org or 714-992-3000 ext. 2878. Questions should come from the student. Health screening and orientation are required (about one month).
duration: Minimum one year and 140 hours a year. Shifts: Mon to Fri 4 to 7 p.m. or weekends 8 a.m. to 9 p.m.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Youth 13 to 17 years old. You must fill out the application yourself.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Counselor-In-Training application linked on the program page. Fees are due two weeks before your assigned week. Call the recreation counter at 714-741-5200 to ask where to turn it in.
notes: This is a program you pay to join. It is not a paid job. Camp Grove is at Edgar Park, 12781 Topaz Street.
duration: Camp Grove runs 9 weeks. In 2026 it ran June 8 to August 7.
pay_detail: You pay $60 for each week. Week 8 costs $120 and week 9 costs $85, and those two fees are not refundable. The weekly cost includes the camp trip fee.

who_can_apply: For the Atlantis Play Center and Sports jobs, you must be at least 16 years old by May 20, 2026. Day camp and resource center jobs on the same page are for ages 18 and up, by May 20, 2026.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now link on the city page to apply on the city job site.
notes: Lifeguard and Instructor Guard jobs are on the same page. The page does not state a minimum age for them. Atlantis Play Center and Sports jobs are year round. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work.
duration: Part time. Hours vary with the program.
pay_detail: Recreation Leader pay is $17.00 to $19.00 an hour. Recreation Specialist pay is $18.50 to $20.50 an hour.

who_can_apply: Teens who are 13 to 17 years old by November 19, 2026. The page calls it a program by and for Garden Grove teens. A parent or guardian must sign the forms.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application and the contract. A parent or guardian signs them. You can email them to ggtac@ggcity.org. You can also drop them off at City Hall, 11222 Acacia Parkway. Or bring them to the next general meeting.
notes: Members must go to the monthly meetings and join at least 2 volunteer events. Meetings are at the Community Meeting Center, 11300 Stanford Avenue, and food is provided. Planned events include Foods of Garden Grove Live, Jack O Lantern Jamboree and Winter in the Grove. To win a scholarship you must go to at least 4 meetings and volunteer at 2 GGTAC events. Questions: 714-741-5360.
duration: September 2026 to April 2027, one meeting a month
pay_detail: Unpaid. No fee is listed on the program page. Members can apply for scholarships.

who_can_apply: Motivated rising high school seniors enrolled at a Genesys Works partner school. The Bay Area page says 100% of its students qualify for free or reduced lunch. No GPA is stated.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application, then interview if accepted, then get summer training details. Phone 415-442-0280, email gwba@ba.genesysworks.org.
notes: You must attend a partner school, and the lists of schools and counties were not on the pages. Ask them whether your school is a partner. No 2027 dates or deadline are posted. Interns work for pay, so a California work permit applies if you are under 18.
duration: 8 weeks of training, then a school-year internship
pay_detail: Paid internship; hourly rate not posted (the page only lists total interns' wages)

who_can_apply: Sophomores and juniors currently enrolled in high school in Los Angeles County, who are at least 16 when the program starts and live within 25 miles of the Getty Center.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the window opens in early February. Questions: gettyteens@getty.edu.
notes: Supported by the Vera R. Campbell Foundation. The page calls it a paid summer internship but says only that interns receive a stipend. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.
duration: Mid-June to early August; interns commit to all program days
pay_detail: Every intern gets a stipend after finishing the program. Amount not stated. Lunch and transportation to the Getty sites are provided.

who_can_apply: Girls and young women in grades 9 to 12. Programs run at the Simpson Center in Oakland (year-round) and Cal State East Bay in Hayward (summer).
how_to_apply: Use the Contact Us page at girlsinc-alameda.org. Office: 510 16th St, Oakland. The site does not list application steps.
notes: The page checked on 2026-10-10 does not mention Code the Game, a fall offering, or grades 10 to 12 for coding. Internship pay, hours and ages are not posted.
pay_detail: Programs are free to families; internships are paid (rate not posted)

who_can_apply: Current high school students. Dual Enrollment: students in Glendale Unified (GUSD) and Burbank Unified (BUSD) taking courses on the class offerings list. Jump Start: everyone else, for college credit only.
how_to_apply: Apply at OpenCCCApply. Then send the Annual Digital Form signed by a parent and your counselor. Find classes, clear any prerequisites and register in MyGCC. Email dual@glendale.edu or call (818) 240-1000 ext. 4767.
notes: Jump Start credit is not guaranteed to count toward high school graduation. A weekly Zoom help hour runs Tuesdays 3:30 to 5:00 PM.
duration: By term
pay_detail: Costs and fee waivers are not stated on the page. Ask dual@glendale.edu.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 21 and in school. You have a disability or health condition, such as an IEP, 504 plan, ADHD or anxiety.
how_to_apply: One online Apply Now form covers all GYA programs. A case worker contacts you in 3 to 5 business days. STEP contacts: (818) 937-8005 or (818) 937-8057.
notes: The GYA page does not mention work permits or income rules.
duration: 120 hours
pay_detail: Paid work experience. The hourly rate is not listed.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24. The page lists it as a first job or summer job program. GYA serves youth from Glendale, Burbank and La Canada-Flintridge and the greater Los Angeles County area.
how_to_apply: One online Apply Now form covers all GYA programs. A case worker contacts you in 3 to 5 business days. Office: 1255 S Central Ave, Glendale; (818) 937-8073, Mon to Fri 8 to 5.
notes: The page does not give the hourly rate or weekly hours, so ask the office. The GYA page does not mention work permits. Checked 2026-10-10: the page says one Apply Now form covers all programs and lists no dates, so we cannot tell if summer spots are open now. Left unconfirmed.
duration: Not stated on the page
pay_detail: Paid work experience. The hourly rate is not listed.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 21 and low income. GYA serves Glendale, Burbank, La Canada-Flintridge and the greater Los Angeles County area.
how_to_apply: One online Apply Now form covers all GYA programs. A case worker contacts you in 3 to 5 business days. Contact for TEAM: (818) 937-8006.
notes: Income limits and funding sources are not spelled out on the page checked 2026-10-10.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Not stated whether TEAM itself pays. GYA says its other youth programs include paid work experience.

who_can_apply: Goleta residents ages 15 to 18. One of the four open seats is for a youth member.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the city's boards page. It is due Nov 12, 2026. Send questions to the City Clerk at cityclerkgroup@cityofgoleta.gov.
notes: Only one youth seat, so it is competitive. The city notice was posted Oct 13, 2026. It lists the same 4-year term for the youth seat as for the general seats, so ask the City Clerk how long the youth term lasts. Meetings are public.
duration: The notice lists a 4-year term for this commission. About 6 regular meetings a year, plus more as needed.
pay_detail: $75 per meeting

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17.
how_to_apply: Fill out three forms for your branch. They are the teen form, the volunteer waiver and the insurance waiver. Drop them off at the branch. Or email them. Each branch has its own email on the library page.
notes: The Goleta Valley Library also runs the Buellton and Solvang branches. Each has its own forms. The City of Goleta has a separate form for teens who want other city jobs, like park cleanups.
duration: Varies with the library's needs
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn community service hours.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 18 by the first day of class. You must volunteer, since you cannot be forced. You must be credit deficient or at risk of dropping out. You must be a U.S. citizen or legal resident and a California resident. You must be clear of felony charges. You must live in one of these places: Santa Cruz, Santa Clara, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Monterey, San Benito, Kings, Tulare, Inyo, San Luis Obispo, Kern, Santa Barbara or Ventura County, or in Lancaster or Palmdale.
how_to_apply: Make sure you meet the rules to apply. Fill out the Interest Form on the site. Then watch the required virtual orientation video. It is a must for the application.
notes: Meant for teens who dropped out or are at risk of dropping out. The FAQ says each ChalleNGe program runs its own admissions. Call or write the academy (contact page on its site) about county rules. Many cadets can earn a GED during the residential phase (FAQ). Some counties on the site have no separate region tag in this guide. They are Santa Cruz, Madera, Fresno, Monterey, San Benito, Kings, Tulare, Inyo, San Luis Obispo, Kern and Ventura. Lancaster and Palmdale are in Los Angeles County.
duration: The page states a 17 1/2 month residential program. The length of the follow-up phase is not stated on this page; ask the academy.
pay_detail: Free to participants (the site says offered free of charge, paid by federal and state partnerships).

who_can_apply: Age 16 and up for construction sites, even with a parent or guardian. Ages 16 to 18 bring a signed minor waiver. Age 15 and under can help with fundraising, flyers or lunch for site volunteers.
how_to_apply: The page gives no online sign-up link; there is usually a volunteer kiosk on site. Call 866-450-4432 or email Volunteer@HabitatEBSV.org. Groups of 5 or more use the group pages.
notes: Hands-on building experience for age 16 and up. Specific build sites were not listed on the page; ask which are near you.
pay_detail: No volunteer fee mentioned on the page

who_can_apply: At least 16 to volunteer on a job site. The page lists no age minimum for the ReStore and no special rules for 16 and 17 year olds. No experience needed.
how_to_apply: Make a VolunteerHub account (sachabitat.volunteerhub.com), register for and attend a one hour HabiTour orientation, then sign up for shifts. Email volunteers@habitatgreatersac.org or call (916) 440-1215.
notes: Ask whether under-18 volunteers need a parent signature or waiver, since the page does not say. Group volunteering contact: gcabral@habitatgreatersac.org. Office: 819 North 10th St, Sacramento.
duration: Shifts Tue to Sat (times not listed)

who_can_apply: Monthly projects: filter the calendar by age to see which are open to you. HandsOn Tomorrow and the Youth Volunteer Council are for Bay Area high school students; the Council requires finishing HandsOn Tomorrow first.
how_to_apply: Use the Community Calendar at handsonbayarea.org/calendar and filter by age. Email info@handsonbayarea.org or call 415-541-9616.
notes: HandsOn Tomorrow, a 2-week summer program (up to 40 hours), will not be running in summer 2026. The page does not say when it returns and does not use the word paused. The Youth Volunteer Council needs HandsOn Tomorrow first, so for now the monthly calendar projects are the way in. Age limits vary by project.
duration: Monthly projects; HandsOn Tomorrow was 2 weeks
pay_detail: No cost or pay stated on the pages

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 17. Animal handling, public speaking or working-with-children experience helps. It is not required.
how_to_apply: Download the volunteer application, write a 1-page cover letter about your interests and goals, and send both by mail, email, fax or in person to 1300 Senter Road, San Jose. Selected applicants interview. Phone (408) 794-6425.
notes: Minimum 48 hours a year (about 4 hours a month). Not everyone is picked, but you can reapply the next season.
duration: At least 48 hours a year (about 4 hours a month)
pay_detail: Unpaid; no cost stated on the page

who_can_apply: The page says ambitious high school students, including rising juniors, may enroll. No age range or grade rule is listed.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply page of the Summer Session site. You send a registration application with a transcript and pay fees before the course starts.
notes: Costs money and the courses are college level. Check the site in winter for 2027 dates and prices.
duration: 2026 Session I began May 26 and Session II began June 15
pay_detail: Tuition is $4,250 per 3-credit course and $5,000 per 4-credit course (2026 prices). Financial aid on the page is only for Harvey Mudd students.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 16 or older. The program page has no separate teen track.
how_to_apply: Email the education office or call the museum and ask to volunteer. You log your hours online after you start.
notes: The program page does not describe orientation, training or required hours. Phone: 510-581-0223, extension 161. The internships on the same page are for college and graduate students, not high school.
pay_detail: Volunteer. The program page does not list pay or service hours.

who_can_apply: Each job lists its own age. Lifeguard: at least 15. Program Aide (Mobile Recreation): 16 and up. Lead Lifeguard: at least 17. Many other district jobs are 18 and up. If you are under 18 you need a work permit from your school.
how_to_apply: Go to the job openings link on the H.A.R.D. Employment page and apply online. You can also make a profile to be considered for future openings. Questions: Human Resources, (510) 881-6708.
notes: Lifeguards need a lifeguard card, a CPR card for lifeguards and a first aid card. They also need a TB test that comes back clear. Program Aides get first aid and CPR training in their first two weeks. Workers 18 and up are fingerprinted. Camp and swim teacher jobs for summer go up in spring. A 2026 summer flyer (not on the district's site) said 15 and a half and up, so check each job's age. Pool upkeep, nature, ropes course and gym coach jobs are for 18 and up.
duration: Part time. The Program Aide job is up to 12 hours a week on Saturdays and Sundays, year-round. Lifeguard shifts can include weekends, early mornings, evenings and holidays.
pay_detail: Lifeguard: $18.63 to $25.14 per hour. Program Aide: $17.74 to $23.94 per hour. Lead Lifeguard: $21.61 to $29.17 per hour.

who_can_apply: Ages 12 and up. Some jobs have their own age rules, listed on each opportunity. Volunteers under 18 need a parent or guardian to sign the volunteer agreement.
how_to_apply: Create a volunteer profile, then register for a one-time event or submit an interest form for a service project. Service projects need a background check and TB risk assessment before starting.
notes: This page lists many volunteer roles, not one program, so each role's own age rule applies. Verification of service hours is emailed on request. Volunteers with court orders should follow the district process (info@haywardrec.org).
duration: One-time events, or service projects that run 6 months or longer.

who_can_apply: The current page does not state ages or grades. The 2023 city notice said students entering grades 8 to 12.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application linked on the Youth Academy page. Your spot is not confirmed until staff contact you and send a confirmation email. Class size is limited. Questions: (510) 293-1043.
notes: The 2026 class met at Fire Station 6 Training Center, 1401 W. Winton Ave. The page warns the course may include simulated firearms and graphic subject matter. The 2026 application link (research.net/r/HPDYA-2026) is for last year, so wait for the 2027 link.
duration: One week, 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. daily (2026: July 6 to 10).
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17. Library service hours cannot be used for community service required by a judge or court.
how_to_apply: Use the APPLY TO VOLUNTEER online interest form linked from the library page. Questions go to hpl.teens@hayward-ca.gov.
notes: The page says the roles are subject to change, so check the online interest form for current openings. The Just for Teens page describes its events for grades 9-12, while the volunteer page says ages 13-17; the volunteer page is the one used here. An older 2023 city notice describes a monthly Teen Advisory Group meeting (1st Wednesday, Downtown Library, ages 13-17, no commitment). That notice was not re-checked for 2026, so ask hpl.teens@hayward-ca.gov whether it still meets.
duration: Flexible. Volunteers sign up for 1-hour shifts.

who_can_apply: Hayward Unified students in grades 10, 11 or 12. You need a work permit and a 2.0 GPA or higher. You also need a letter from someone at school. Bring a California ID and a Social Security card, or other proof you can work.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online registration form on the HUSD page. Qualified students are invited to a group interview, then may be placed at a school site.
notes: Only for HUSD students. The 2026-27 window has passed, so ask the YEP office if late spots open. Contact: Larry Ewings, YEP Operations Supervisor, (510) 723-3857 ext. 34157. Students who turn 18 and graduate can apply to be a YEP Program Leader (starting at $28.98 per hour).
duration: School year, after school. Hours are not stated on the page.
pay_detail: Paid internship. The intern pay rate is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Students ages 13 to 20 who live in the City of Hayward or within the Hayward Unified School District boundaries. Applicants under 18 need a parent or guardian consent form.
how_to_apply: Get the application and the Parent Agreement and Contact Information form from the City of Hayward website, or call the City Clerk at (510) 583-4400, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. weekdays. Applicants are interviewed by a panel.
notes: The official Youth Commission page returned 404. The newest notice read is from April 2025. The 2021 notice said meetings were on the first and third Mondays, so the meeting schedule may have changed. Confirm the 2026 cycle with the City Clerk before applying.
duration: Meetings at Hayward City Hall, September to June (meeting day not confirmed; the 2021 notice said first and third Mondays). The 2021 notice said two-year terms.

who_can_apply: Black male students entering grades 9, 10 or 11. No coding experience needed. Must commit to the full 15 months.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the Immersion Program page on hiddengeniusproject.org.
notes: The apply page says OUR 2027 APPLICATION IS NOW OPEN and lists no closing date. The immersion page still shows the old Feb 21, 2025 deadline. The immersion page lists Oakland and Richmond among its sites.
duration: 15 months
pay_detail: Free to join; no stipend listed

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18. Application, interview, orientation and hands-on training.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Flight Teen application online, then expect a call to schedule an interview, attend volunteer orientation, and train with an active volunteer.
notes: Year-round, ongoing applications. Weekend shifts only. Interview timing and training length are not stated.
duration: Alternating Saturdays or Sundays (1st and 3rd, or 2nd and 4th), plus an extra shift on a 5th weekend some months
pay_detail: Unpaid; no cost stated on the page

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24 living in the City of Los Angeles. The checklist PDF (2024 version) lists the other rules on who can join. Check the current one.
how_to_apply: Create an application on the Hire LA site, then bring or upload proof of age, right-to-work (I-9) documents, City of LA residency and the family income form.
notes: Cycle dates are not confirmed, so check with EWDD before you count on a summer 2027 spot. The home page Youth section says ages 14 to 30. That does not match the 14 to 24 overview used here, so check the current age range. The same city department runs 14 free YouthSource Centers for ages 14 to 24. They offer school help, job readiness and some paid internships. Ask at your nearest center, for example Boyle Heights 323-526-5800 or South LA 323-903-6926. Under 18 you need a California work permit. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps. Checked 2026-10-10: the home page still says "Accepting Applications for" with no year or dates, so left unconfirmed.
duration: Varies. Student to Student Success is up to 140 hours in one school semester (20 hours of training, up to 120 hours of service).
pay_detail: Paid. The home page does not state an hourly rate.

who_can_apply: Local students ages 16 to 18. No grade level is stated.
how_to_apply: The page lists no application or interest form for this program. Call the Volunteer Office to ask when interest will be taken again.
notes: Not offered: summer, short-term, hands-on patient care, shadowing or observation. Volunteer Office phones: Newport Beach (949) 764-8264, Irvine (949) 517-3152. The page does not state the weekly hours.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: On-site animal care volunteers must be 18 or older. Students under 18 can foster with a parent or guardian's support or make fleece blankets.
how_to_apply: Email volunteer@hssv.org or see the student opportunities page for fostering and blanket instructions.
notes: No hands-on shelter work until 18. Service hours: 2 fleece blankets = 1 hour (0.5 hour each); fostering is counted by care time. Email for a service hour verification letter.
pay_detail: Unpaid; no cost stated. HSSV provides foster supplies.

who_can_apply: Restoration days are for ages 8 to adult. Kids under 14 need an adult with them. Age rules for long-term volunteer roles are not stated on the pages.
how_to_apply: Come to a restoration day (wear closed-toe shoes and bring water) or sign up for the monthly volunteer training. A waiver form is on the volunteer page. Contact Kenny at 714-846-1114.
notes: The Conservancy internships are unpaid. They need a related degree or college enrollment, so they are not for high schoolers.
duration: Restoration events are the last Saturday of each month, 9 a.m. to noon. Long-term volunteers start with a monthly 3 hour training.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Most roles are ages 13 to 17 (18-year-olds still in high school can also join). Teen Tech Volunteer is ages 15 to 17, Chess Club Volunteer is ages 15 to 18 in high school, and Helen Murphy toy cleaning is 13 and up. D&D Club volunteers must have attended a club meeting in the past six months.
how_to_apply: Use the online application for the role you want (several library roles share one application link, so check which one). Seats for club roles are first-come, first-served, and staff email next steps. The Main Street Branch also accepts a printed teen application dropped off at the branch.
notes: Contact: Teen Services Librarian Katelyn Wong (Katelyn.Wong@surfcity-hb.org) or the library at 714-842-4481. The page also lists other Huntington Beach volunteer groups for teens, with their own age rules. They are Bolsa Chica Conservancy, Bolsa Chica Land Trust, Shipley Nature Center and OC Coastkeeper cleanups. Some entries on the page look copy-pasted, so confirm details with staff.
duration: Varies by role: weekly or monthly sessions of 1 to 3 hours
pay_detail: Unpaid. Sessions earn 1 to 3 volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: You must be 17 years old by July 1 of the year you are hired, with proof. You must pass a 1,000-yard pool swim in under 15 minutes and an 1,800-yard ocean run-swim-run.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the city job site before the exam. Pass the exam and go to an interview. The best scorers join the paid training academy.
notes: A 16-year-old can apply only if they were a Huntington Beach Junior Guard last summer. Marine Safety must also back them. New hires get a uniform, fins, sunglasses and a beach parking pass. Check the city job board for the 2027 posting. Paid work under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work.
duration: Seasonal, as-needed work with weekends and holidays
pay_detail: $22.50 to $27.50 an hour in the 2026 posting. Lifeguards are paid during the academy.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 through 20. The page also says the maximum age to apply is 19. Ask the department which age applies to you. You must be in high school or a graduate. Keep a 2.0 GPA. Pass a medical exam and a background check. You cannot have a felony conviction.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form. An advisor emails you. Go to an information meeting. Turn in the application and a Hold Harmless form. Pass a medical exam. Then take an agility test, an oral interview and a background check.
notes: The agility test has a 1-mile run, sit-ups, push-ups and a flex arm hang. The city also runs a Fire Explorer program.
duration: Monthly training on the 2nd and 4th Thursday of each month. Volunteer at least 4 hours a month.
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Local high school students. These are HB Union High School District students. They also include Huntington Beach residents who go to private school or are homeschooled.
how_to_apply: The page says applications are now available. It links the word Applications to its Notice of Vacancies page. No deadline is listed. For questions, contact the city staff liaison, Molly Uemura. She is at the Community and Library Services Department. The email is on the page.
notes: Application dates and the form are not on the page. Confirm with the city first.
duration: 1 year term, from the start of the school year to May. Members can reapply until graduation.
pay_detail: Not stated; this is a volunteer board

who_can_apply: Students who are chosen as student reps from local high schools. The page lists 2026-27 reps from Beckman, Portola, Irvine, University, Northwood and Woodbridge high schools. It lists no grade or eligibility rules.
how_to_apply: The page says to look for HSYAT at your school through the Campus Clubs page. No application form is listed.
notes: The page lists no grade rules, application dates or phone number for this program. Check your school's Campus Clubs page.
duration: School year; follow the team on Instagram for events
pay_detail: Not stated

who_can_apply: High school students ages 14 and over (program assistance and toy cleaning are ages 14 to 17). Teen Summer Reading volunteers are students in grades 8 to 11. Each library has up to 20 TAG memberships.
how_to_apply: Submit the Teen Volunteer Application on the library's volunteer system at www.volgistics.com/appform/337674493. A required orientation comes before the summer program.
notes: The page lists no library contact; it points to the volunteer coordinator, and the City of Irvine main number is 949-724-6000. The page writes the Teen Volunteer Application link as volgistics.com/appform/337674493 and links it over https, so apply_url uses https.
duration: Summer Reading volunteers work a weekly two-hour shift. Other roles vary.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18, or finished 8th grade and going into 9th. You must live in Irvine or go to school there. Keep a C or better in every class. You cannot have criminal convictions or serious traffic offenses.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Interest Form on the program page. Interest cards are due January 1 for winter or June 1 for summer. Email ipdexplorers@cityofirvine.org with questions.
notes: The Orange County Explorer Academy is held twice a year. It is a hard 5-day program. You must finish it within a year of joining. The group also takes trips, such as a weekend in Sacramento for the Peace Officers' Memorial.
duration: Most Explorers stay until high school graduation
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page calls it a volunteer program.

who_can_apply: High school students who will graduate in 2027 or 2028. The page also describes 11th or 12th grade in Fall 2026. You need an unweighted GPA of 3.0 or higher in college prep classes. You need a strong reason to take one UCI course.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Enrollment Form. Send it to the Summer Session office. Add a copy of your latest high school transcript.
notes: This is real college credit and costs real money. The grade stays on a college record. The page names two grade groups (graduating 2027 or 2028; and 11th or 12th grade in Fall 2026), so check which one fits you. The fee page says 2026 Summer Session fees were pending the state budget and may change.
duration: One summer course (Summer Session sessions)
pay_detail: The fee page lists high school students under visiting non-UC students: $400 per unit plus a $296 campus fee and $5.50 per unit tech fee. Some courses add materials fees.

who_can_apply: Grades 9 to 12 need parent and principal consent. Grades K to 8 also need instructor approval. You must meet each class prerequisite. There must be open seats.
how_to_apply: Find a class in the IVC schedule, write down its CRN, then complete the General Enrollment Form steps with parent and school approvals. The Director of Dual Enrollment is listed on the page.
notes: Checked 2026-10-13 against the general dual enrollment page: per-unit enrollment fees are waived for grades 9 to 12 and not for K to 8, grades 9 to 12 need parent and principal consent, and K to 8 also need instructor approval. The page says enrollment is ongoing, on a space-available basis, with no deadline. IVC/IUSD Summer College is for grades 9 to 11 at seven Irvine high schools: Creekside, Irvine, Northwood, Portola, San Joaquin, University and Woodbridge. The Early College Pathway is for some students admitted before grade 9, at Beckman and San Joaquin.
duration: By semester or summer session
pay_detail: Per-unit enrollment fees are waived for grades 9 to 12 (not for K to 8). You pay the college health fee and buy textbooks.

who_can_apply: High school students of all backgrounds can apply. Irvine residents get priority. Priority also goes to youth who are low-income or out of school. It also goes to youth in foster care and first-generation college students.
how_to_apply: The page gives no application link or contact for this summer program. It says to check back in February 2027.
notes: This program is part of a California Volunteers Youth Service Corps grant. The same page lists an adult job program for ages 18 to 30. That one is not for high school students. Training covers job search, interviewing, leadership, customer service and financial literacy.
duration: About 20 hours a week. Shifts run 7 a.m. to 10 p.m., weekdays and weekends.
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the program page. The page calls the roles jobs ("hiring").

who_can_apply: Students in Northern California; grade levels not stated. The center is not open yet.
how_to_apply: No sign-up steps yet. Call JA of Northern California at (925) 465-1070.
notes: Not open yet, and the page lists no registration steps or opening date. Watch for it in early 2027. The contact on the page is for sponsors and partners.
pay_detail: Free to students (page says programs are delivered at no cost)

who_can_apply: High school students whose school or group requests a program. The page does not say whether individual teens can sign up. JA Finance Park is the Los Angeles area only.
how_to_apply: Ask your school to request a program using the form on the JA high school page. The page does not say who should fill it in. Contact: info@jasocal.org or 323-957-1818.
notes: The page does not say whether teens can sign up alone. Bring the page to a teacher. JA Company Program ends with the JA Student Entrepreneurship Challenge pitch contest.
duration: Varies by program
pay_detail: No pay. The page says programs are offered at little or no cost to educators.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 who are low income and meet citizenship, residency or other approved status rules, plus background checks (per the national Job Corps site). Mostly fits teens who are out of school or want a different path. Housing is on campus.
how_to_apply: Apply at enroll.jobcorps.gov or call 800-733-JOBS (800-733-5627).
notes: Residential, so you live on campus at 3100 Meadowview Rd, Sacramento. The Sacramento page lists the trades (building construction, carpentry, cement masonry, Certified Nurse Assistant) but not the age or income rules, which come from jobcorps.gov. A federal settlement reported Aug 12, 2026 kept all 99 centers open, but that article does not name Sacramento, so confirm the center is enrolling.
pay_detail: Free tuition, housing, meals and basic medical care, plus a monthly living allowance (amount not stated).

who_can_apply: Local high school students interested in a healthcare career. Must be at least 14.5 years old, at least a second-semester freshman, with a minimum 3.0 GPA. Must attend a Saturday orientation with a parent or guardian and complete required training. Students apply through a partner high school, which interviews and screens its own candidates.
how_to_apply: Apply through your high school. Contact the career, college or community service office at a partner school listed on the page. The school interviews and screens its own student candidates.
notes: Read on the official John Muir Health page 2026-10-07. Not stated on that page: application window or deadline, TB test or immunization requirements. It is an unpaid volunteer role, so no work permit is listed. Region is east-bay because Walnut Creek is in Contra Costa County, not Oakland. The Auxiliary at Walnut Creek Medical Center offers selective scholarships to high school seniors and college students who volunteered in this program. A separate Concord Medical Center high school program is not onboarding this summer; its page says to check back in March 2027. An older third-party listing said seniors are not accepted, which conflicts with the official page; confirm with the program before applying. Minimum age is listed as 14.5 on the page, stored here as 14.
duration: One 3-hour shift per week, year-round, committed through the end of senior year
pay_detail: Volunteer role; no pay stated on the page

who_can_apply: High school programs are delivered through schools and teachers, who request them. The site does not list a way for a student to sign up alone, so ask your school or call JA.
how_to_apply: Ask your teacher or counselor to request a JA program, or contact JA at (925) 465-1070 or info@janorcal.org.
notes: JA reached 27,947 students in 128 schools in 2025-26, mostly through schools. JA Launchpad (Silicon Valley) is listed as opening early 2027. Job shadow and internship details were not on the pages, so ask JA.
duration: Varies
pay_detail: No student fee stated. JA says programs are little to no cost to educators.

who_can_apply: Be 16 to 19 by June 1, 2027, live in a Northern California Kaiser Permanente service area, have proof of legal US work eligibility, and be free Monday to Friday about 8am to 5pm. Priority goes to juniors and seniors. Children of Kaiser employees or physicians cannot apply. The program aims at students who lack resources to explore health careers.
how_to_apply: Apply only on the KP LAUNCH online portal during the window (email submissions are not reviewed). You need a resume and a personal statement of up to 750 words. Questions: KP.LAUNCH@kp.org.
notes: Full-time hours, so no summer school or camp overlap. Competitive. A Kaiser story reportedly cited about 3,300 applicants for 318 spots, which is not confirmed here. Placement sites vary, so check that your area is offered. Kaiser may ask for COVID vaccine proof.
duration: 7 weeks, June 14 to July 30, 2027
pay_detail: $25 per hour minimum, paid every two weeks, up to 40 hours a week

who_can_apply: High school students 16 years or older (the kp.org page says ages 16 to 17). Applications open only when shifts are available. One-year commitment.
how_to_apply: When it opens again, sign up on the Kaiser volunteer site under Redwood City. You need one or two references from a teacher, coach or tutor. Then you do a video interview. Next is a health check where you bring your shot records. A parent must come. Last are online trainings and an in person orientation. Phone: 650-299-3135.
notes: Read on Kaiser's volunteer site and the kp.org Redwood City page on 2026-10-16. The two pages do not agree. kp.org says 4 hours a week for 6 months. The volunteer site says one year for high school students. Plan on one year. Kaiser does not offer job shadowing. The kp.org page also lists roles like the ER, art, pet visits and surgery. These differ by site.
duration: One year

who_can_apply: Must be 16 years or older to apply. The time commitment is one year. One or two professional references from a teacher, coach, tutor or similar are required.
how_to_apply: When it opens again, apply on the Kaiser volunteer site under San Jose. You need one or two references. Then you do a video interview. Next is a health check where you bring your shot records. Bring a parent. Last are online trainings and an in person orientation. Volunteer office: 408-972-7230.
notes: Read on Kaiser Permanente's volunteer site on 2026-10-16. The high school program is full. Check the page every few weeks, since minors are taken only when shifts are free. Kaiser does not offer job or clinical shadowing (physician, nursing, radiology, PT or OT). The kp.org page still links to volunteer-ncal.kaiserpermanente.org, which no longer works; use kpvolunteer.samaritan.com.
duration: One year

who_can_apply: Volunteers 16 years and older. The page lists separate steps for 16 and 17 year olds. You must give at least one 4-hour shift each week, Monday to Friday between 8 am and 6 pm, for a planned one year commitment.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the Kaiser volunteer site. Look under High School Programs at Santa Clara Homestead. Then do a video interview. Next is a health check where you bring your shot records. A parent must come with you. Last are online trainings and an in person orientation. Volunteer office: 408-851-1717.
notes: Read on Kaiser's volunteer site on 2026-10-16. The kp.org Santa Clara page links to it at kpvolunteer.samaritan.com. Shifts are on weekdays only, 8 am to 6 pm. Most students would need a free period, a late afternoon or summer days. A background check with a Social Security number is only for people over 18. The page asks for shot records. It does not say which shots, if you need a TB test, or if there are fees. Kaiser does not offer job shadowing.
duration: One 4-hour weekday shift a week for a planned one year

who_can_apply: High school students 16 years or older (the kp.org page says ages 16 to 17). Commit to one 4-hour shift a week, same day and time. The time commitment spans your high school career.
how_to_apply: Call Volunteer Services at 650-742-2678. Ask when high school spots will open. Then apply on the Kaiser volunteer site under South San Francisco.
notes: Read on Kaiser Permanente's volunteer site and the kp.org page on 2026-10-16. The kp.org page says a few hours a week for a few months, but the volunteer site says the high school commitment spans your high school career; plan on the longer one. The Daly City Medical Offices page has the same high school rules. Kaiser does not offer job or clinical shadowing. The page does not list vaccine, TB test or fee rules.
duration: One 4-hour shift a week, for the rest of high school

who_can_apply: High school students age 15 or older. You must give one 3 to 4 hour shift a week on the same day and time, and stay in the program for your whole high school career. The high school track is at Walnut Creek Medical Center only.
how_to_apply: Go to the Kaiser volunteer site. Open High School Programs at Walnut Creek and click Apply. You will log in or sign up as a new volunteer. Questions? Call 925-295-5487.
notes: Read on Kaiser's volunteer site on 2026-10-16. kp.org links to it at kpvolunteer.samaritan.com. This is a long commitment. The page says it lasts all through high school. The page does not list shots, a TB test or fees. It does not say if a parent must sign. Kaiser does not offer job shadowing. Adult volunteers here also cover nearby offices. The high school track is at Walnut Creek only. Kaiser's old volunteer link no longer works, so use kpvolunteer.samaritan.com. The Pleasanton and San Ramon offices said on 2026-10-16 that they are not taking high school students right now.
duration: One 3 to 4 hour shift a week, for the rest of high school

who_can_apply: Currently enrolled high school students ages 16 to 17. Must be 16 or older when you apply.
how_to_apply: Apply online. You need a self-portrait photo, proof of COVID-19 vaccination and a questionnaire. Recommenders email letters to volunteer@med.usc.edu by April 30. If accepted, you do an interview. Then you get a health screening with a TB test, an orientation and a tour. Phone (323) 442-8436.
notes: Check the page in January for the next year's dates.
duration: 8 weeks, at least 8 hours a week and 60 hours total
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Rising public high school seniors (entering senior year in fall 2027) who attend a public high school in LA County and live or go to school within 10 miles of the worksite. Must be able to work legally in the U.S. and bring a school ID and proof of work eligibility. No age rule is listed.
how_to_apply: Apply for a listed internship when applications open in March 2027. Questions: BAI@arts.lacounty.gov.
notes: Schedule may change. You cannot be a current or former employee of the worksite or related to its staff. The 2026 internship positions list is on the Department's site. The page does not mention work permits. California requires a permit for paid work under 18.
duration: 8 weeks, June 14 to August 6, 2027. Optional paid extension from September 2027 to April 2028 (22 weeks).
pay_detail: Paid. The hourly rate is not stated. Program Day participants also get a stipend for 90% participation, plus transportation help and lunch.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 20 with at least a 2.0 GPA. You can read, write and understand training materials in English. You can work on a team.
how_to_apply: Send in the Explorer Program Interest Card to hear about the next cycle. Add the program's email to your safe senders. Then apply during open enrollment. Accepted applicants get a uniform fitting and a family meeting. They also go to a two-day orientation.
notes: The page lists 12 posts. They are Vernon, Carson, Whittier, Industry, Azusa, Lancaster, Fairfax, Santa Clarita, La Canada Flintridge, El Monte, Agoura Hills and Pomona. But its sign-up form lists Posts 1 to 22. Confirm your post with the department.
duration: Ongoing after a two-day orientation; twice-monthly meetings
pay_detail: No cost or pay is stated on the page

who_can_apply: Youth ages 9 to 17 in LA County. New participants must pass a 100-yard freestyle swim test (1:30.00 for ages 14 to 17). Cadets must be 16 or 17 as of July 1 with at least two years in the program, one as an A.
