how_to_apply: Register online when the season opens, usually in February or March. New participants must pass a swim test. They must bring a birth certificate or passport. Cadet and Life Saving Team applications are separate. They are posted later.
notes: The page calls the $635 an estimated operating cost and says the fee schedule is under review. Costs money and is mainly for younger kids; teens 16 to 17 can reach Cadets. Not every beach offers afternoon sessions or Session 2. Refund rules and absence limits are on the page. The registration site (juniorlifeguards.fire.lacounty.gov) was not loading on October 18, 2026; use the link on the program page when 2027 registration opens.
duration: Two 4-week sessions in 2026: June 15 to July 10 and July 13 to August 7
pay_detail: About $635 per child for Summer 2026 (the page says the fee schedule was under review). Financial aid needs a federal tax return.

who_can_apply: Anyone 14 and older can volunteer. Teen Advisory Boards are open to teens at libraries that have one.
how_to_apply: Contact your local LA County Library branch to ask about volunteer openings and whether it has a Teen Advisory Board.
notes: This covers LA County Library branches (unincorporated areas and many cities), not the City of Los Angeles library system (see the LAPL card). Tasks vary by branch and season.
duration: Varies by library
pay_detail: Unpaid; students can earn school service credit.

who_can_apply: LA County residents who are 14 to 24 when they enroll and have the legal right to work in the U.S. The county gives priority to youth with high needs, such as current or former foster youth, youth touched by the justice system, youth who are or were homeless, and LGBTQ+ youth.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth Interest Form on the Youth@Work page. AJCC staff reach out within 48 hours to check eligibility and match you with an employer.
notes: The county released a Youth@Work Program Review and Redesign Report on August 25, 2026, so rules and pay for 2027 may change. Under 18 you need a California work permit before the first day. The pay figure is the 2025 summer rate from the county's own news release, not a 2027 promise. Long Beach youth can also use the City of Long Beach center (see the LBWIN card).
duration: About 160 hours in all: up to 140 hours of paid work plus 20 hours of job-readiness class
pay_detail: Paid work experience for about 140 hours plus a class. The page does not state an hourly wage.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 26. You live in LA County. You were hurt by COVID-19. You can go to all six weeks.
how_to_apply: Fill out the intake form on the academy page to join the waitlist. Questions: (844) 432-4900 or emi@opportunity.lacounty.gov.
notes: The COVID-19 impact rule is on the page, so confirm you qualify. Schedule, cost and meeting place are not listed. Confirm first.
duration: 6 weeks per cohort
pay_detail: Cost and stipend are not listed.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 17. The 2026 council has 27 members from nine areas, including the San Gabriel Valley, Central Los Angeles and the South Bay. No other rules are listed.
how_to_apply: The page has no application. Use the update sign-up form, email metroyouthcouncil@metro.net or call 213.922.2852.
notes: Check the page for the next recruitment. The page does not say how often the council meets.
duration: 1-year term, January to December
pay_detail: The page does not mention a stipend or pay

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 14 years old and able to finish the required training. No upper age limit is stated.
how_to_apply: Join the waitlist on the Zoo's volunteer page. When applications open, go to an info meeting and an interview. You are invited to these. Then finish online and in-person training. You must also pass a fingerprint background check.
notes: Applications were closed when this page was read. A negative tuberculosis test may be needed for some advanced roles. Phone: (323) 644-4200.
duration: 25 hours per year for students (50 hours per year for other volunteers)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Los Angeles County residents, 16 to 18, who will be juniors or seniors in the 2027 school year and are interested in art, museums or community events.
how_to_apply: Online application during the open window (last year July 1 to Aug 21). Questions go to teens@lacma.org.
notes: Next year's dates are not posted. Watch for a July opening. LACMA also offers NexGenLA, a free membership for LA County youth 17 and under (free museum entry plus one guest). Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.
duration: 10 sessions on select Sundays, 10 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., Oct 2026 to Feb 2027
pay_detail: Selected teens receive a stipend. The amount is not stated.

who_can_apply: Anyone 16 or older. Those 18 and over also pass a background check and need a valid Social Security number. You commit to 150 hours a year.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application form (PDF on the page). Email it to the volunteer office, addressed to Julia Lieberman. Then go to a Volunteer Services orientation. You also need 2 TB tests and the required seasonal flu shot. The page does not mention an interview.
notes: Volunteer Office: (949) 452-3728, 24451 Health Center Dr, Laguna Hills. The application PDF is labeled an adult form; ask the office which form teens use.
duration: 150 hours per year
pay_detail: Unpaid. You buy a volunteer uniform jacket ($25) and pay $5 in dues.

who_can_apply: Oakland residents only. The City of Oakland MSYEP page lists youth from 14 through 21 in general, and some providers serve narrower groups. This card shows 16 through 21, which the pages checked did not confirm, so ask the provider.
how_to_apply: Call (510) 533-8850 or 1 (833) 532-3674, or use the Contact Us form at lfcd.org.
notes: LFCD's own employment page does not describe this youth program, so provider details were not confirmed there. Hours and minimum-wage pay come from the City of Oakland MSYEP page. Under-18 workers need a work permit.
duration: Up to about 100 hours
pay_detail: At least Oakland's minimum wage (MSYEP rule); exact rate not posted

who_can_apply: Teen Volunteer and Teens Leading Change are for ages 14 to 19. Teen Council is for ages 11 to 19. Volunteers fill out a Teen Volunteer Intake Form and a parent or guardian signs a waiver.
how_to_apply: Contact the Young Adult Librarian or Senior Librarian at your nearest library, then complete the intake form and parent waiver. Questions: Volunteer Engagement, 213-228-7490.
notes: LAPL hosts over 2,600 teen volunteers a year across 73 branches. Openings differ by branch. Some branches also have volunteer slots listed at volunteer.lapl.org.
duration: Varies by branch; Teen Council members complete at least 20 community service hours
pay_detail: Unpaid; you earn community service hours.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 and up. Younger kids can help only if the event lead says yes ahead of time. If you are under 18, a parent must sign the online youth waiver.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer form. Use a personal email, since school emails do not work. Then log in to MyImpactPage. Open the Opportunities tab and sign up for shifts.
notes: This is the year-round list. The separate Summer Youth Volunteer Program (ages 13 to 17) has its own card. Phone 925-373-5700. Office: 4444 East Ave, Livermore.
duration: One-time event shifts and recurring work days. The page does not set a minimum.

who_can_apply: Ages 11 to 14. You do not need lifesaving or first aid skills. The program page asks you to be comfortable in the water and have basic swim skills.
how_to_apply: Pick a session on the program page. Use the register link for that session. The page does not give sign up dates.
notes: Sessions run Monday to Thursday, 1 to 4 p.m. This is a class, not a job. The program page footer says 2026, and the course numbers end in 26. It does not state the camp year. Phone 925-373-5700.
duration: 4 days, 3 hours a day
pay_detail: $100 for Livermore residents and $120 for non-residents.

who_can_apply: Lifeguard I: 16 or older when hired, with a Red Cross lifeguard card. Swim Instructor I: 16 by your first shift, with a Starfish swim teacher card and a CPR, first aid and AED card. Recreation Leader I: 16 or older when hired. No past work is needed.
how_to_apply: Apply online only, through the job openings links on the LARPD jobs page. The district does not take general applications for jobs it is not hiring for. You must pass a fingerprint background check and a TB test. Workers under 18 need a work permit before the first day.
notes: Recreation Leader I must finish First Aid, CPR and AED training within six months of hire. Lifeguard I may also work the front desk and collect money. Check back before summer, when pools usually hire, but no date is posted. The job description PDFs were read with firecrawl. Phone: 925-373-5700.
duration: Part-time staff are hired as needed. Shifts can include early mornings, evenings, weekends and holidays.
pay_detail: Paid hourly. Pay is not stated on the jobs page or the job descriptions; each posting should list it.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17. Volunteers under 18 need a parent or guardian to sign the Youth Volunteer Waiver. Students must attend a Summer Youth Volunteer orientation. Some roles have extra rules: Summer Nature Camp requires the Counselor in Training (CIT) program, and Open Space Jr. Docents require age 16 or older.
how_to_apply: Create a LARPD volunteer account by submitting the General Volunteer Application (use a personal email, not a school email). Attend a Summer Youth Volunteer orientation at the Robert Livermore Community Center. Then sign up for shifts through MyImpactPage. Questions: volunteer@larpd.org.
notes: The 2026 cycle is closed. Watch larpd.org/volunteer and the orientation pages for the 2027 dates; the district's pages were not all updated to the same year. The FAQ says the opportunity list may change each year. The orientation and FAQ pages list volunteer@larpd.org as the contact. Not a paid job, so no California work permit is needed.
duration: Summer weekly shifts. The 2026 FAQ says sign-ups start with a maximum of 2 weeks, with more weeks added later.
pay_detail: Volunteer position. Earn community service hours; no wage is listed.

who_can_apply: High school students in partner districts: Dublin, Livermore, Pleasanton and Tri-Valley, plus San Ramon Valley USD (welding) and TUSD (fire safety training). Residency and citizenship rules apply; ask Admissions & Records.
how_to_apply: Sign the CCAP Dual Enrollment form with your school counselor. You sign it once for all of high school. Questions: lpc-dualenrollment@laspositascollege.edu.
notes: Offered during and after the school day. Ages are not stated on the page.
duration: Per term
pay_detail: Free; tuition and fees waived and required materials provided (parking may cost extra for classes at LPC)

who_can_apply: Grades 10 and 11. Public school students in Alameda, San Francisco and Contra Costa counties are prioritized; nearby counties are encouraged to apply. In person at Berkeley Lab at least 4 days a week for 6 weeks.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the Berkeley Lab K-12 page when it opens (the 2026 application ran through apply.mykaleidoscope.com).
notes: Whether students are paid is not stated. Finishing students can join later workshops and possible lab internships in following summers.
duration: June 16 to July 24, 2026 (6 weeks, 4 days a week)
pay_detail: Not stated on the page (no stipend listed)

who_can_apply: Grades 10 to 12 in Northern California, at least 16 by the program start. Students within 30 miles of the lab are prioritized. You can do the program only once.
how_to_apply: Apply online during the window and pick your top three projects. Do not contact mentors directly. Oakland Unified students also complete the ECCCO common application.
notes: The page still says 'at least 16 by June 16, 2025', so check the age date when it reopens. Some 2026 projects were hybrid or virtual. Under-18 interns need a work permit.
duration: 6 weeks (June 15 to July 24 in 2026)
pay_detail: $500 per week for 30 to 35 hours

who_can_apply: English-learning, native Spanish-speaking bilingual students.
how_to_apply: Watch the Berkeley Lab K-12 high school programs page.
notes: Grades and ages are not listed on the page. The 2026 camp is over and no 2027 camp is posted, so it is not confirmed to repeat. Page says it can lead to summer internship chances.
duration: April 8 to 11, 2026 (spring break)
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: The center serves ages 14 to 30. Youth@Work is for ages 14 to 24 and WIOA-funded services are listed for out-of-school youth ages 16 to 30. WIOA funding focuses on out-of-school youth with barriers such as low income, foster care, homelessness, juvenile justice involvement, parenting, or a disability. A Long Beach residency rule is not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Complete the Youth Interest Form on the city's Youth Services page. Partner agencies can also refer youth through the Unite Us platform.
notes: Because most WIOA funding targets youth facing barriers, a teen still in school may be steered to Youth@Work or a school-to-career program instead. Under 18 you need a California work permit for any paid placement. The city's Youth Opportunities page also lists teen volunteering at Long Beach libraries and at Parks, Recreation and Marine (ages 13 and up).
duration: Varies by program
pay_detail: Paid internships and Youth@Work (about 160 hours of paid work experience). Pay rates are not stated. Workshops and career help are free.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17. The page does not state a residency rule for volunteers.
how_to_apply: Use the Register to Volunteer link for the teen volunteer call on the League site, or email lov@lov.org. Phone (510) 793-5683.
notes: The teen call on the homepage is for summer 2026. Confirm with the League whether it recruits again for 2027. Serves the Tri-Cities (Fremont, Newark and Union City).
duration: The 2026 summer recreation program ran July 6 to July 30, 2026, Monday to Thursday, 10 a.m. to 2 p.m., at Mayhews Landing Park in Newark.

who_can_apply: California high school sophomores, juniors and seniors. A select number are chosen.
how_to_apply: Apply through the LegiSchool website application. Join their mailing list for contest, town hall and internship news.
notes: The application link and 2027 dates are not on the page. The stipend amount is not stated. LegiSchool also runs Town Hall meetings in downtown Sacramento. It also runs video and essay contests for California high school students.
duration: 4 weeks, Mon/Wed/Fri afternoons (2026: starts June 22)
pay_detail: Stipend paid after the program. The amount is not posted.

who_can_apply: Students entering 11th or 12th grade. You must be able to work full time all summer. You must go to May Saturday trainings.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Lawrence Hall of Science teen internship page when it reopens; questions to lhscamps@berkeley.edu.
notes: The page URL says 2024 but the content is the 2026 posting. The page says to apply next summer; 2027 dates are not posted. Mid-January is the 2026 pattern only.
duration: June 1 to Aug 7, 2026, Monday to Friday 8:30 am to 4:30 pm; Saturday trainings in May
pay_detail: $3,500 for the full summer ($72 deducted per missed day)

who_can_apply: Page lists teens entering 9th grade or above, or at least 14 years old, who are not current volunteers. The age wording is tied to June 1, 2024 and may be outdated. No current rules posted.
how_to_apply: Check the Lawrence Hall of Science teen volunteer page; call 510-642-5132 or mail/deliver forms to the Volunteer Program, attention Veronica Urdaneta, 1 Centennial Drive, Berkeley, CA 94720. The page lists no youth volunteer email.
notes: The page says recruiting is paused and a re-imagined program is planned for 2026, with no dates. Its Apply Today teen link conflicts with the pause notice, so do not treat it as active. Call to ask whether the program has launched. The age rules come from 2024 wording, so the age fields are blank. The email veronicau@berkeley.edu was removed because neither page lists it.
duration: Summer minimum 21 hours; school year two 3-hour shifts a month

who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12 who live in Livermore or go to a school in Livermore. The council has 20 members.
how_to_apply: Fill out the paper form. It asks three short questions: why you want to join, how you help in your town, and what else you want to share. A parent must sign. Turn it in at the front desk of the Civic Center Library, or email it to njbrumley@livermoreca.gov. If picked, you get a talk with staff.
notes: This used to be the Livermore Area Youth Advisory Commission. The city's youth page now calls it the Livermore Youth Council. If you miss three meetings in one school year, you are out. Adults and some members read the forms and talk with each teen. A city staff member makes the final pick. Contact: Nathan Brumley, 925-373-5572.
duration: A new term starts each school year. Members serve 2-year terms, then say if they want to keep serving. Meetings are the first Monday of each month at 7 p.m., plus subcommittee meetings and events.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 6 to 12 in the 2026-27 school year. You must live in Livermore. Each applicant needs a separate account and email.
how_to_apply: Click Fill in an application on the volunteer page. If you already have an account on the library volunteer portal, log in. You must go to an orientation and log your hours in your account.
notes: The program page does not give start and end dates, orientation details or the number of hours. Ask the library before you apply. The listing is for summer 2026, so look for the next summer posting.
pay_detail: Volunteer. The program page does not mention community service hours.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 21 with a real interest in a fire service career. You must commit time to training and community service.
how_to_apply: Fill out and sign the Explorer application on the LPFD Explorers page. Information left off the application will not be considered. A resume is welcome but does not replace the application. Questions: explorers@lpfire.org or (925) 454-2361.
notes: Scouting America has run this with the fire department since 1999. Explorers must come often, act like pros and help the town. Each training builds on the last one, so try not to miss any. The fire department serves both Livermore and Pleasanton. Its office is at 3560 Nevada Street, Pleasanton.
duration: Full-day training on the 2nd and 4th Sundays of each month (8 a.m. to 5 p.m. per the brochure) at the LPFD Training Center and fire stations.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 (and done with 8th grade) to 21. Your application must arrive before your 19th birthday. You must be in school with at least a 2.0 GPA, have good moral character and no felony convictions, and be interested in a law enforcement career.
how_to_apply: Get the form from the police Explorer page, fill it out and send it in. Questions? Email lpd-explorer@livermoreca.gov.
notes: The police page also says you must not have a health problem that could put you or others in danger on a task. The library's youth list says to live or go to school in Livermore. The police page does not say that, so ask. This card does not cover what the form itself asks.
duration: Ongoing. The page does not list a meeting schedule.

who_can_apply: Teens 14 to 18 years old by June 1. No experience needed. You must be friendly and professional with guests.
how_to_apply: Fill out the ZooTeen application online (link on the page), then go to orientation. Phone: 760-346-5694.
notes: Requires attending ZooTeen orientation. Address: 47900 Portola Avenue, Palm Desert, CA 92260.
duration: Two shifts a month and monthly meetings; a 4-year program, and you can serve one year or all four
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. Cost not mentioned.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 11 or 12 at a Northern California high school (public, charter, private or homeschool). Must be 16 or older at the start. GPA 3.3 or higher and science GPA 3.5 or higher. Must have finished Biology and Chemistry (or Integrated Science I and II). Students 18 at the start must be U.S. citizens.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Send your latest high school grades (a copy is fine). Give the name and email of your biology or chemistry teacher. That teacher sends a letter for you.
notes: Competitive, and space is limited. You must be allowed to enter the Lab under federal law (2025 NDAA Section 3112), which blocks some foreign nationals. Bring your own laptop and get your own ride. Contact: stem-education@llnl.gov.
duration: Two weeks. In 2026: weekdays July 13 to 24, 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m.
pay_detail: Free to attend. Lunch is not provided.

who_can_apply: Must be 16 or older at the start of the workshop. No GPA requirement and no experience needed. Students 18 at the start must be U.S. citizens. You must be allowed to enter the Lab under federal law (2025 NDAA).
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. That is all. You do not need a letter from a teacher.
notes: The page does not list a grade level or a region rule. Competitive and space is limited. Bring your own laptop and transportation. The 2025 NDAA rule generally blocks citizens of China, Russia, Iran and North Korea who do not also hold U.S. citizenship. Contact: stem-education@llnl.gov.
duration: Three days. In 2026: June 29 to July 1, 8:30 a.m. to 3 p.m.
pay_detail: Free to attend. Lunch and snacks provided.

who_can_apply: Current 9th to 11th graders at a Northern California public high school, ages 14 to 17 and under 18 at camp time. A GPA above 3.5 is preferred.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Ask a teacher, coach or other adult who knows you to write you a letter. In 2026 there was an online info talk in February.
notes: Competitive. Public school students only. The page said 'Not accepting applications' on Oct 16, 2026. Contact: stem-education@llnl.gov. The Livermore library list mentions proof of COVID vaccination, but the LLNL page does not, so that may be out of date.
duration: One week. The 2026 camp was June 8 to 12.
pay_detail: Free to attend.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 10 to 12 in the fall, at least 15 by the start, with a cumulative GPA of 3.3 or higher. Students 18 at the start must be U.S. citizens. You must be allowed to enter the Lab under federal law (2025 NDAA Section 3112).
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Send your latest high school grades. A copy is fine.
notes: Bring your own laptop and smartphone, and arrange your own ride. The page does not list a region rule. Contact: stem-education@llnl.gov; allow 2 to 3 business days for a reply.
duration: One week. In 2026: weekdays July 6 to 10, 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m.
pay_detail: Free to attend. Lunch and snacks provided.

who_can_apply: High school students in 9th through 12th grade in the Inland Empire who are interested in health sciences. Students 17 and a half or older may be invited to an optional shadowing week.
how_to_apply: Submit the application form, a recommendation form from a teacher or clergy member, a 200-word essay on your interest in health sciences, and the $30 fee or a waiver request.
notes: Closed until the next cycle opens. Loma Linda University is a Seventh-day Adventist institution.
duration: 2 weeks (2026: July 12 to July 24), plus optional shadowing week
pay_detail: $30 non-refundable application fee (fee waiver available for financial need). The page does not list a program cost.

who_can_apply: Active middle or high school students who meet each course's prerequisites. No minimum GPA is listed.
how_to_apply: Apply free on OPENCCC. You get your Viking ID by email. Then turn in the High School Dual Enrollment Form with all signatures. Finish New Student Orientation with a score of 80% or higher on the final test. Then register once Admissions confirms your form.
notes: Students who stop attending for two main terms must reapply. Taking college classes does not affect Long Beach College Promise eligibility. To take extra units, file the Unit Max Petition.
duration: By term
pay_detail: Tuition and enrollment fees are free. Course material fees, textbooks and supplies are not covered (a Textbook Loan Program exists for hardship).

who_can_apply: Two seats are for youth under 19 at the time of appointment. Each youth is picked by their district councilmember and appointed by the Mayor.
how_to_apply: The page has no application. Ask your district councilmember's office or the city contacts listed on the page.
notes: Only two youth seats exist. Meeting location was listed as to be decided. Contacts on the page include ashleigh.griset@longbeach.gov and erika.Medrano@longbeach.gov.
duration: 2-year terms (up to 4 terms); meets every other 3rd Wednesday at 6 p.m.
pay_detail: No pay is stated

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 17. Must be at least 15 by July 1, 2027. Capped at 15 cadets.
how_to_apply: Sign up with the Cadet Tryouts Sign Up form on the page. Bring a resume. Pass a physical tryout: a 1000m open water swim in about 20 minutes and a run-swim-run in about 10 minutes. Then do an interview. Questions: LBJG@longbeach.gov.
notes: Very physical. Tryout date and calendar may change, so email to confirm. LBUSD students with at least one year of cadet experience can apply for a separate LBUSD Cadet Internship (details not on this page). The page header says the tryout date is not set but lists April 26.
duration: Summer; the 2026 cadet calendar is listed as not set
pay_detail: Cost or pay is not stated on the page

who_can_apply: People ages 13 and over.
how_to_apply: Use the online 'Apply to Volunteer' link. It is in the BetterImpact portal. For questions, call (562) 570-3226 or write to prmvolunteers@longbeach.gov.
notes: The page does not list hours or what each role does. Ask which sites take 13 year olds.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Must be at least 16 years old. If under 18, you must have a valid permit to work.
how_to_apply: Use the 'Apply Here for Recreation Jobs' link, which goes to governmentjobs.com (search for recreation). Tech help: (877) 204-4442.
notes: Pay rates are as posted on the page (the page does not date them). Under-18 applicants need a valid permit to work. Ask the department which level a first-time worker starts at. Accommodation requests: (562) 570-3188.
duration: Temporary; hours vary by week and may reach 40 per week June through August
pay_detail: Hourly by level: $16.76 (Specialist III), $17.31 (IV), $18.09 (V), $20.87 (VII). The level depends on your qualifications.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Volunteer Interest Form linked on the library's volunteer page. Questions: lbpl_volunteers@lbpl.org.
notes: Hours, locations and training are not listed on the page. Ask by email.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18 as of February 27, 2027, and living in the City of Long Beach during the program year.
how_to_apply: Apply online. You answer five short questions. You also send a CV of up to 4 pages, a bio of up to 100 words and 5 poems (up to 10 pages). Paper applications go to LS-YPL@longbeach.gov or Teen Services at the Billie Jean King Main Library. Info sessions are Saturdays, Dec 12, 2026 and Jan 23, 2027, 12:30 to 2:00 PM at the Main Library. To reserve, email LS-YPL@longbeach.gov. Walk-ins are welcome.
notes: Poets must also take part in the National Youth Poet Laureate program and attend most monthly workshops. Mailed packets must be postmarked by Feb 27, 2027. Prize is a scholarship, not wages.
duration: May 2027 to April 2028
pay_detail: $1,500 scholarship for the Youth Poet Laureate; $500 scholarship for each of 4 Youth Poet Ambassadors

who_can_apply: Anyone at least 14. Volunteers under 18 need a parental permission form. The city takes individuals, groups, and families, one time or ongoing.
how_to_apply: Print the volunteer form and fill it out. Bring it to the Los Altos Community Center (97 Hillview Ave), or email it to rec-info@losaltosca.gov. You can also mail or fax it. Staff will reach out to you. Ask Bridget Matheson: bmatheson@losaltosca.gov.
notes: The city's teen page sends teens ages 14 to 18 here. The Teen Center (grades 6 to 12, weekdays 3 to 6 p.m.) is a free place to hang out. It is not a volunteer job.
duration: One-time or ongoing shifts. Adult 50+ Program hours are weekdays, 9 a.m. to 2 p.m.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 15. No experience with children is needed. Acceptance is not guaranteed. Los Altos residents pay a lower fee, but others can apply.
how_to_apply: Sign up with the city's online sign-up link on the program page. Staff will email you to say if you got in. Ask Sarah Carrico: SCarrico@losaltosca.gov.
notes: This costs money; it is not a paid job. The page shows dates without a year; the weekdays match 2026. Only 14 and 15 year olds in high school fit the age range, so this suits younger high schoolers.
duration: Weekly camp sessions in summer, after two required training days.
pay_detail: You pay a weekly fee. Half day: $125 for Los Altos residents, $148 for others. Full day: $250 for residents, $296 for others.

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students who live in Los Altos Hills. Up to 20 members.
how_to_apply: Fill out the town's form for joining a group. You fill out a form and talk with the Youth Commission and staff. Then the Town Council talks with you and votes to add you.
notes: Meets at 7 p.m. on the 1st and 3rd Tuesday of each month. Members lose their seat after missing 3 meetings in a row or going below 75% attendance in a year. The June 2026 council recap says candidates must first attend at least one meeting and volunteer at town events. After that meeting there were 17 members, so a few seats may be open.
duration: One-year term. Members can be reappointed for up to 7 terms.

who_can_apply: High school students who are in school during the 2026-27 year.
how_to_apply: Online Teen Docent Program application, linked from the museum site (closed for 2026-27). A 2024 article says selected applicants are called in for a brief interview.
notes: Phone 650.948.9427; the page gives no email address. Pay is not stated on the current official page, so we list it as unpaid based on a 2024 article; confirm with the museum. The lahstalon.org article is a 2024 news piece, used only for the interview and volunteer details. The museum's adult docent roles are separate and not for teens.
duration: August 2026 through June 2027, at least 4 hours per month. Two-day training on August 8 and 9 for accepted applicants.
pay_detail: Not stated on the current page. A 2024 article describes volunteer hours and work experience.

who_can_apply: Not stated on the page. The 2026-27 members are high school students from Los Altos High, Menlo, Nueva, Mountain View High, and Crystal Springs Uplands. Ask the City Clerk about grade and residency rules.
how_to_apply: Watch the city page in April 2027, when sign-ups open. Ask the City Clerk, Melissa Thurman, at mthurman@losaltosca.gov. Or ask Taylor Brown at tbrown@losaltosca.gov.
notes: In 2025 the old Los Altos Youth Commission became this academy. Meetings are at 5:30 p.m. at the Los Altos Community Chambers, 1 N. San Antonio Rd. The 2027 mock council meeting is set for Monday, May 3, 2027, and will be on the city's YouTube channel. Meetings are open to the public, so you can visit one first.
duration: School year, with about one Monday meeting a month from September to May. Current member seats expire in June 2027 or June 2028.

who_can_apply: High school students. Ages and grades are not stated.
how_to_apply: Use the Learn More and Apply link on the Craft Contemporary teens page. You can also call 323-937-4230. Or email info@craftcontemporary.org.
notes: Ask about ages, the application date and whether any stipend is paid. The permit field is false only because it is described as a free program, not a job.
duration: Dates not on the program pages
pay_detail: The page calls it a free program.

who_can_apply: Youth who were in foster care at any time from age 16 to 18, or who meet a few guardianship rules. An ILP coordinator checks that you qualify.
how_to_apply: Call the Transition Aged Youth helpline at 877-694-5741 or email youthds@dcfs.lacounty.gov. Ask for an ILP coordinator.
notes: Call first to ask what you qualify for. Foster Youth Helpline: 877-846-1602. If you are in danger right now, call 911. The page does not mention the ETV college voucher; ask your coordinator about it.
pay_detail: Not a job. The page does not list a cost.

who_can_apply: Young people ages 12 through 24.
how_to_apply: Call 323-908-0011 or 1-888-YOUTH-50, or email info@myfriendsplace.org to ask about hours and how to start.
notes: This is a support center, not a job. Details on its education and job help are not on the program pages, so call. If you are in danger right now, call 911.
pay_detail: The site describes its resources as free.

who_can_apply: The page header says ages 13 to 19 and the FAQ says ages 15 to 19, so ask which applies. Sign-up is required and seats are limited.
how_to_apply: Fill out the sign-up form on the Teen Auto Workshop page when a date is posted. Adults who bring a teen under 18 must stay in the museum.
notes: A one-day workshop, not a job. Check the page for the next date.
duration: One session on select Saturdays, 10 am to 2 pm
pay_detail: Free to join. Museum admission is required.

who_can_apply: Youth experiencing or at risk of homelessness. The age range is not stated on the program pages.
how_to_apply: Call 310-902-2283 or email info@safeplaceforyouth.org. The site is at 2471 Lincoln Blvd, Suite 101, Los Angeles. General hours are Mon to Thu 9:15 to 7:00, Fri 9:15 to 6:15, Sat and Sun 9:30 to 3:30.
notes: Ask when you call what ages they serve, because the pages do not say. If you are in danger right now, call 911.
pay_detail: A paid internship through the Community Garden is mentioned. The pay rate is not stated. Cost to join is not stated.

who_can_apply: High school students who have finished at least 9th grade by the start and take a rigorous course load. Domestic and international students may apply.
how_to_apply: Apply online with a 300 to 500 word essay, a teacher or counselor recommendation, a transcript and the application fee. You can rank up to three courses but you take one. Join the email update list for 2027 news.
notes: Expensive. Prices and deadlines above are the summer 2026 numbers; the 2027 numbers may change. The pages did not give an age limit.
duration: Four weeks (Summer 2027: June 21 to July 15)
pay_detail: Summer 2026 prices: tuition $7,401, materials $300, program fee $325, health center $104. Total $8,130 commuter or $11,570 residential, plus an $85 application fee. No financial aid was mentioned. 2027 prices not posted.

who_can_apply: 11th and 12th graders at a high school in the program. The page names the AUSD, LUHSD and PUSD districts. You need a signed Dual Enrollment Authorization form from a parent and your counselor. Your principal must recommend you. You do not need to be in a special program.
how_to_apply: Go to your high school counselor for the form and the steps. Get the signatures from a parent and your counselor. Your principal must recommend you.
notes: The page says it was last updated 3/15/22, so ask your counselor to confirm the steps. Grades from these classes go on your college transcript. You can also take other Los Medanos classes on your own time as a concurrent student, with principal approval. You pay all fees and costs for those concurrent classes.
duration: By semester
pay_detail: Free. The page says there are no course costs and no textbook costs. Your school district pays for textbooks.

who_can_apply: At least 14 years old or already started ninth grade. Needs a parent or guardian signature and a recommendation from your high school principal.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school counselor, pick the Los Rios college that offers the class, apply at that college as a dual enrollment student (parent signature and principal recommendation needed), then register.
notes: Credits go on a permanent college transcript. Whether you also get high school credit depends on your school, so ask your counselor. Your school does not need a CCAP agreement for you to take a college class. Application deadlines are by college term.
duration: Per semester
pay_detail: Tuition is free. Other fees may apply, such as the student representation fee. Books may cost extra.

who_can_apply: Young volunteers who go to school. The application asks about your school schedule and clubs. A parent must sign if you are under 18. No minimum age is stated.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Junior Docent Application PDF (link on the volunteer page), with a short bio. Call 951-902-5949 or email volunteerinfo@marchfield.org.
notes: Museum address: 22550 Van Buren Blvd, Riverside. Ask the volunteer office about the youngest age they accept.
duration: You pick 1 to 6 days a week or 1 to 7 days a month; shifts are Tue to Sun, 9 AM to 4 PM
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: High school students, college students, teachers and recent graduates can join. Students under 18 need a signed permission slip from a parent or guardian to go on the in-person tour. Say in your application if you are under 18.
how_to_apply: Join the mailing list with the form on the program page. You will get an email when the next session is announced.
notes: The program is free to join. In-person events are optional, because you can take part fully online. Central San works with Contra Costa Water District on the program. Central San is at 5019 Imhoff Place, Martinez.
duration: In 2026: four partial days over two weeks in February
pay_detail: Unpaid. You pay for your own travel and meals.

who_can_apply: Students who are 16 or older and are in school now or going back in the fall. If you have not graduated from high school, a work permit must be obtained.
how_to_apply: Apply in the first two weeks of March. The page does not say where to apply, so ask Central San. If you have not graduated from high school, a work permit must be obtained.
notes: Summer students are at-will, short-term workers. They do not get benefits or a promise of a regular job. When school is not in session, a minor can work up to 8 hours a day and 40 hours a week. Central San is at 5019 Imhoff Place, Martinez. The internship programs on the same page are for college students.
duration: Up to four months
pay_detail: $30 per hour

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18. Must be 16 by Sept 1.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Here link on the page when applications reopen. The page suggests joining an information session. Questions: mya@mednet.ucla.edu.
notes: Fundraising cannot start until you are accepted. It cannot take place on hospital or clinic grounds. Two excused absences are allowed.
duration: Cohort 8 runs 2027 to 2028. Meetings are Wednesdays 3:30 to 4:30 PM, virtual; weekly in summer, monthly in the school year.
pay_detail: You pay nothing, but you must raise $1,250 for the hospital to earn an awards package. There is no pay.

who_can_apply: 11th and 12th grade students from San Diego. The page says the group draws teens from across San Diego County. Limited to 25 students.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application (one per student). Invited students get an acceptance email and onboarding documents. Questions: education@mcasd.org.
notes: Closed for 2026-2027. The program is supported in part by the California Arts Council.
duration: Sept 8, 2026 to June 2027; meets the 2nd and 4th Tuesday of each month, 5 to 7 p.m.
pay_detail: No stipend or cost mentioned on the page.

who_can_apply: Mt. Diablo Unified students who are interested and eligible. In 2026-2027 class capacity will be 60 juniors and 60 seniors. Talk to your high school counselor about the rules.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school counselor. Then fill out the College Now student application on the program page. A recommendation form is also on the page. Go to the parent night if you can.
notes: The program started in fall 2016. The 2026 parent night was Wed, Feb 4, 2026. Staff phone on the page: 925-969-2512. The DVC page also lists a related program called Diamante Scholars for Mt. Diablo seniors.
duration: Junior and senior years
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the College Now page. DVC says its dual enrollment classes are free.

who_can_apply: Current Mt. Diablo Unified students who will be in 11th or 12th grade in the year they serve. You need at least a 2.0 grade point average and must be enrolled in 20 credits.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Student Board Member Application when the district posts it. For 2026-2027 it was sent by email to Laura Juranek at juranekl@mdusd.org, due May 29, 2026.
notes: Board meetings are usually on the second and fourth Wednesday of the month, starting at 6:00 PM. The Student Advisory Committee advises the Student Board Member. Its 2025-26 meetings were at Concord High School. The district is at 1936 Carlotta Drive, Concord.
duration: One school year, July 1 to June 30
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 16 to 24 who live in Central Contra Costa County or Bay Point. You must be able to work in the U.S. and show proof of low income. Priority goes to McKinney-Vento (HOPE) youth, foster youth, and justice-involved youth in Bay Point and on the Monument Corridor. Being pregnant or parenting, an English learner, or having an IEP or 504 plan can also help you qualify.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Refer a Youth form on the program page. A coordinator then works with you. Questions: Anna Ramos, 925-685-1011, extension 62028.
notes: The Workforce Development Board of Contra Costa County funds and supports this WIOA grant. For East or West Contra Costa County, the page points to the County Office of Education. The page lists 14 required program elements, including leadership development and financial literacy education.
pay_detail: The page lists paid and unpaid work experience. Pay is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Students in high school grades 9 to 12. No age range is stated.
how_to_apply: Watch the page for the next application. Accepted students get an email. Then they send shot records (varicella, MMR) and a TB test within 6 months. They also go to a required orientation by invitation only.
notes: The page covers Long Beach Medical Center only. It does not mention an Emergency Room volunteer role or its age rule.
duration: 8-week session; 2026 ran June 29 to August 21
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 21. You must be in school with at least a 2.0 GPA and no failing grades, be in good physical condition (with exceptions), and should not have a criminal record. A parent or guardian must sign the application. The page does not list a residency rule.
how_to_apply: Fill out an application and have a parent or guardian sign it. The page does not link the form, so email Eric Mijangos at explorer109@menlofire.gov to ask for one. District office: 170 Middlefield Road, Menlo Park, 650-688-8400.
notes: You need reliable transportation, and you will be tested to show you learned the skills. The page says bi-monthly meetings but does not give days or times. Exploring is part of Learning for Life. The district's separate Fire Cadet program is not for high schoolers (it needs EMT and Firefighter I training).
duration: Ongoing. The page says training happens at bi-monthly meetings and Explorers must attend all Explorer events.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program. The page does not list any cost.

who_can_apply: Applicants should be in grades 7-12. The page does not state a residency requirement.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application linked from the library's Teen services page. Questions to David Jimenez, Librarian I, 650-330-2528 or djimenez@menlopark.gov.
notes: Meets the 1st and 3rd Thursdays, 4:30-5:30 pm, at Menlo Park Library (800 Alma St.), and the 1st and 3rd Wednesdays, 4-5 pm, at Belle Haven Library (100 Terminal Ave.). Members may attend one or both. The page is undated and is the only source; older M-A Chronicle articles describe pandemic-era activities and a different meeting pattern, so confirm the schedule with the librarian before the first meeting.
pay_detail: Volunteer. Members earn volunteer hours; the page does not say how many.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 21. You can start applying at 13 and a half. You must keep a 2.0 GPA, pass a background check and pass an oral board interview. The page does not list a residency rule.
how_to_apply: Fill out the cadet form and the agreement from the page. Mail them to Attn: Police Cadet Program, 701 Laurel St., Menlo Park, CA 94025. Ask Corporal Galen Fliege: gpfliege@menlopark.gov or 650-330-6300.
notes: You must finish a cadet training course. The 2019 form says it is eight Sundays at College of San Mateo and one Saturday at Huddart Park. You must pass tests at 70 percent and get your own ride. It also lists one evening meeting a month. The page now says Police Cadets, but the forms still say Explorer Post 844. The form asks for your Social Security number and driver license number for a background check. A parent must sign if you are under 18. The page lists no meeting times or dates.
duration: Ongoing. Volunteer at least 10 hours a month. The page says it is meant to be a long-term commitment, and cadets age out at 21.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program. A 2019 participation form on the page lists a $55 academy fee and a uniform that costs about $150 to $200. The current page does not list costs, so confirm them.

who_can_apply: Lifeguard, Swim Instructor and Front Desk jobs say you must be at least 15. Lifeguards must pass a swim test (150 yards, 2 minutes treading with no hands, then 50 more). Swim instructors need a clean background check. Front Desk asks for 1 year of customer service work.
how_to_apply: Go to the Menlo Swim and Sport careers page and click through to the Team Sheeper job board. Pick a job and apply online. Questions: customerservice@menloswim.com or 650-781-5525.
notes: The city does not hire its own pool staff. The city's aquatics page says Menlo Swim and Sport runs both swim centers under contract, and its careers page links to the Team Sheeper, Inc. job board. You do not need to be a certified lifeguard to apply, they train you. The swim instructor posting says active employees get free lifeguard certification and calls the job good for high school students. Front Desk asks for experience, so it is harder for a first job.
duration: Year-round and summer jobs. The swim instructor posting says shifts fit around school, sports and other jobs.
pay_detail: Lifeguard: $20 to $26 per hour. Swim Instructor: $23 to $28 per hour. Front Desk Associate: $20 to $26.25 per hour. Training is paid.

who_can_apply: Must be a City of Menlo Park resident and be entering grades 9-12 for the upcoming academic year and committee term.
how_to_apply: Submit the YAC application form and supplemental questionnaire to the Library and Community Services Department. Staff review applications, schedule interviews and make the final selection.
notes: Competitive, and closed now. Members must attend at least 75 percent of meetings. Contact Da'Shawn Williams, Recreation Coordinator, 650-330-2248. The page lists two email addresses (dlwilliams@menlopark.org and dlwilliams@menlopark.gov); confirm which is current. An older city notice said about 8 hours per month; the current page says about 6. The page does not mention pay, so we list it as unpaid; confirm with the city.
duration: One-year term, September through May. About 6 hours per month for meetings and events.
pay_detail: Not stated on the page. Treated as unpaid committee service; confirm with the city.

who_can_apply: High school youth from 9th grade through 19 years old. Teen staff are picked through an application and an interview.
how_to_apply: Fill out the 2027 Camp Staff Application from the Merced 4-H Camps page and turn it in by the deadline. Then you have an interview. Questions: Merced County 4-H Office, (209) 385-7418.
notes: The page gives the deadline as November 9 with no year, next to the June 2027 camp dates and the 2027 application form. It does not say whether teen staff must be enrolled 4-H members, so ask the 4-H office.
duration: Camp runs June 14 to June 18, 2027
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: The squadron welcomes all community members ages 12 to 18. They join its cadet program.
how_to_apply: Fill in the contact box on the squadron's Join Us page with your contact information and a short description of your interests. Email: christopher.ince@cawgcap.org. The squadron meets at 3515 Hardstand Ave, Atwater, CA 95301.
notes: Confirm first: the squadron pages do not list meeting times, dues or the first visit steps. The national Civil Air Patrol cadet page says cadets can join at ages 12 through 18.
duration: Ongoing. Nationally the ideal time is a weekly meeting of about two hours, one Saturday event a month and a week long summer encampment. The squadron's meeting day and time are not listed.
pay_detail: Civil Air Patrol says annual dues are $25 to $50 depending on location, and a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year (minus financial help). The squadron page does not state its own dues.

who_can_apply: Students at high schools that offer Merced College CCAP courses. Grade levels and partner schools are not listed. Ask your counselor.
how_to_apply: Apply online with the CCAP link. A parent fills out the Dual Enrollment Parent Consent Form. Pick classes with your counselor. Then give the K-12 Permit PDF to your high school CCAP counselor.
notes: The Dual Enrollment Coordinator is Jourdan L. French. Her number is 209-384-6189. For classes taken on campus, see the separate Merced College K-12 concurrent enrollment card.
pay_detail: No tuition and no books.

who_can_apply: K-12 students. Ask your high school counselor if you are eligible. English C1000 is only open to eligible 11th and 12th graders. K-8 students need a written recommendation from their principal or designee. They also need current transcripts.
how_to_apply: 1) Apply for admission for the semester you want. 2) Turn in the Dual Enrollment Parent Consent Form once during high school, after you get your 7 digit Merced College ID. 3) Complete the K-12 Permit form for your school level. 4) Wait for the email that lets you register in the MC Portal. 5) Pay fees online or at the Student Fees Office. Phone for the Merced campus: 209-384-6000.
notes: This is the college's own concurrent enrollment page. Merced Union High School District also has its own dual enrollment partnership with Merced College (see that separate card). Kinesiology courses with a physical activity part are capped at 10 percent of K-12 seats.
duration: By semester, including summer
pay_detail: K-12 students can enroll in Merced College classes tuition free (limitations may apply). Some physical activity courses need an extra K-12 Permit, and some fees may still apply.

who_can_apply: You can join if you are 9 by December 31 of the program year. Groups are Junior (9 to 10), Intermediate (11 to 13) and Senior (14 to 19). You can stay until December 31 of the year you turn 19. Kids 5 and up can join as Primary members.
how_to_apply: Contact a club leader first, since some clubs have limited space. Then enroll online in the 4-H enrollment system linked on the New Youth Member page, picking at least one club and one project, and pay your club leader or pay online. Questions: (209) 385-7418.
notes: The club list is on the Merced County 4-H Clubs tab of the site. Teens can also apply to be 4-H camp teen staff (see the Merced 4-H Camp Teen Staff card).
duration: 2026 to 2027 program year
pay_detail: The youth fee is $70 for 2026 to 2027. It includes accident and illness insurance. You may be able to get the fee waived or lowered.

who_can_apply: Out-of-school youth ages 16 to 21 (for example, youth without a high school diploma). Teens 16 to 18 qualify only if they are out of school.
how_to_apply: Use the Click here to apply form on the EMPOWER page, or call 209-381-5926. The office is at 658 W. Main Street, Merced.
notes: Prospero (the Merced County workforce board, formerly WorkNet) lists EMPOWER as its main youth program for out-of-school youth. Prospero Youth Team: 209-724-2036. Confirm first: the page gives no start dates or wage.
duration: Not stated; follow-up services for at least 12 months after the program
pay_detail: Paid and/or unpaid work experience; wages are not stated.

who_can_apply: High school students across Merced County. The page lists the ROP at Delhi, Dos Palos, Gustine, Hilmar, Le Grand, Los Banos and Pacheco high schools. It also lists Merced Scholars Charter School. It also lists Valley Community School in Atwater and in Los Banos. Grade rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: The page does not explain how to enroll. Ask your school counselor, or contact Dora Robles, Staff Secretary, at (209) 381-6684 or drobles@mcoe.org.
notes: Confirm first. The page does not list the courses, grades, cost or how to enroll. The MCOE college and career page also lists the EMPOWER program (see the separate EMPOWER card). It also lists Cal-SOAP for college and financial aid information.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Cost, pay and credit are not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Age 16 or older. Mercy Medical Center in Merced is a listed place to volunteer.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer interest form. The volunteer team then contacts you about an interview and orientation. You also need a background check and shots.
notes: This is the Central California system volunteer page. It lists no phone number, so use the contact page at commonspirit.org/dignity-health-central-cal-contact-us. The page does not say whether applications are open, so ask before you plan on it.

who_can_apply: Students in good academic standing at a Merced Union High School District school (Atwater, Buhach Colony, El Capitan, Golden Valley, Livingston, Merced, Sequoia, Yosemite). Complete the Merced College application, a parent consent form and a High School Permit.
how_to_apply: Apply to Merced College, submit the parent consent form and High School Permit, and talk to your school's Pathway Counselor.
notes: College privacy law applies once you enroll: parents do not get progress updates from Merced College. A college GPA below 2.0 can affect future college eligibility and financial aid.
duration: By semester
pay_detail: Free: students can take college courses at no cost, up to 11 units a semester. Textbook fees are waived for CCAP classes; textbook fees apply for concurrent enrollment.

who_can_apply: Current 11th or 12th graders who go to school in Merced County and have active Medi-Cal. You answer personal questions about your interest in health careers.
how_to_apply: Apply online at ucm.edu/chapply. Questions: pace@ucmerced.edu.
notes: Only for teens with Medi-Cal who attend school in Merced County. Ages are not stated, only grades 11 and 12. Check the page each fall for the next round.
duration: Spring certificate course, then 60 hours of team projects in summer 2026
pay_detail: $1,400 stipend, plus project funding, a $150 gas card and a program polo (per the flyer).

who_can_apply: City of Merced residents ages 13 to 19. Seats are split by Measure C district: two from each of three districts and one at large.
how_to_apply: Fill out the form on the city page. Then the current members interview you. City staff then make a pick for the City Council. You and a parent sign an agreement.
notes: Meetings are the second Thursday of each month at 6 p.m. in the City Council Chambers, 678 W. 18th Street. Members may miss only two meetings a year without an excuse. There are required trainings and trips. The council can also add non-voting junior high or high school helpers.
duration: Two-year term, up to two terms. At least 8 hours a month.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 18. Other rules are not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Call the Milpitas Fire Department at 408-586-2800 to get involved or ask questions.
notes: The page is short and gives no meeting times, requirements or application form. Call first to ask if the program is active and taking new Explorers.
duration: Not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: At least 15 at the time of hire. You must pass a swim skills test through a Lifeguard Academy before you are hired. Experience with kids and adults is preferred, not required.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the Milpitas city job board. Before you are hired, you must pass a swim test at a Lifeguard Academy.
notes: This posting first opened Sep 3, 2024 and is still listed as continuous. Its application questions still mention 2024-25 shifts, so call 408-586-3090 to check current hiring. A TB test is required. Fingerprints are only required if you are 18 or older.
duration: Part-time, year-round and seasonal. Shifts are usually 4 hours. August to June: Monday to Saturday, 5:30 am to 8:30 pm. Summer: daily, 5:30 am to 9 pm.
pay_detail: $18.50 to $25.77 per hour

who_can_apply: The city page says ages 14 to 20 in one place and 16 to 20 in another, so ask. You need at least a 2.0 GPA, no major criminal convictions, and no substance abuse. You do not have to live in Milpitas.
how_to_apply: Get the Explorer form, the history form and the health form from the page. Or pick up a form at the police station, 1275 N Milpitas Blvd. You must pass a talk with officers and a background check. Call 408-586-2400 with questions.
notes: The info sheet on the page is from 2010. It still names the Boy Scouts as a sponsor. Call 408-586-2400 to check that the program takes new members.
duration: Ongoing, with meetings twice a month.

who_can_apply: At least 16 at the time of hire. You must have some experience working with elementary school age kids.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the Milpitas city job board. Or mail a paper form and a resume to the Milpitas Community Center, 457 E Calaveras Blvd. Call 408-586-3210 with questions.
notes: You need a TB test and Red Cross First Aid and CPR within 60 days of hire. Fingerprints are only required if you are 18 or older. Perks include a free Milpitas Sports Center membership and paid sick leave after 90 days.
duration: Part-time, year-round and seasonal. Usually Monday to Friday, 2 to 6 pm, with some nights, weekends and holidays. Up to 1,000 hours a year.
pay_detail: $18.50 to $25.77 per hour

who_can_apply: All ages. Volunteers under 14 need a parent or adult with them. Some jobs have their own rules. Volunteers 18 and older need fingerprint clearance for some jobs.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer form. You do not need a form for park cleanups. Call 408-586-3210 or email volunteers@milpitas.gov with questions.
notes: The Alviso Adobe likes high school helpers, but most tours are on school day mornings. Teen Center tutoring is on weekdays from 4 to 7 pm. The page's list of events and cleanups looks old (the last cleanup shown is from January 2024). Watch the monthly emails for new ones.
duration: Ongoing. Some jobs are one day, others are longer projects.

who_can_apply: Commissioners must be in grades 7 through 12 and live in Milpitas. Applicants also complete the Youth Advisory Commission supplemental questionnaire.
how_to_apply: Submit a commission application online, by email, by mail, or in person, with the Youth Advisory Commission supplemental questionnaire. Questions go to the City Clerk's Office at cityclerk@milpitas.gov or 408-586-3001.
notes: Regular meetings at 6 p.m. on the second Thursday of every month, Milpitas Teen Center, Rooms 140/141, 40 N Milpitas Boulevard. Founded April 1996. The page lists current members with terms ending September 2028. Pay is not mentioned on the page, so it is listed as unpaid. The supplemental questionnaire PDF could not be read, so its questions are not summarized here.
duration: Three-year terms (seven commissioners and two alternates)

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 17, entering 10th or 11th grade in fall 2026, and attending a San Diego County high school.
how_to_apply: Online application, then a mandatory in-person interview and group interview if advanced. Contact the museum's Education Specialist or see the program PDF on the page.
notes: Closed for the 2026-2027 cohort. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.
duration: 15 sessions, twice a month on Wednesdays 4:30 to 6:30 p.m., October to May
pay_detail: $750 for full participation

who_can_apply: High school students prepared for college-level work. Students in 9th grade or below need special approval from the Director of Outreach and Student Development. English and math placement rules apply. No GPA rule stated.
how_to_apply: Apply through OpenCCC, do the placement assessment, submit the Dual Enrollment Form (parent and school counselor signatures, 2 to 3 business days), meet prerequisites, then register in the My Mission portal. Phone (408) 855-5007.
notes: Unit limits: up to 8 in fall or spring (non-MECHS students), 6 in winter, 9 in summer; more needs a petition. Undocumented students are welcome. Getting to campus is on you.
duration: By term (fall, winter, spring, summer)
pay_detail: Enrollment fees waived; you pay only for textbooks and materials (many courses have no textbook cost)

who_can_apply: You must attend a local high school. You must be a freshman, sophomore or junior when you apply. You must turn 15 by February 1 of the following year.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form for the 2027 group. The link is on the program page. Add two recommendation letters: one from a teacher and one from a coach, mentor or supervisor. Add a resume with no photo. Add a personal statement of at least 300 words. Answer the short essay questions. Some students then get an interview.
notes: Chosen students need a TB test and proof of vaccines. They also go to registration, orientation, training and shadowing shifts. The earliest start is usually March. Shifts are Monday to Friday 4 to 8 p.m., or on weekends. There are no summer-only spots. Email MHAuxiliary@providence.org or call 949-364-1400 ext. 7944.
duration: One 4-hour shift a week, year round, until you graduate
pay_detail: Unpaid. You pay a one-time $125 membership fee for an ID badge, polo shirt and jacket. You also buy black khakis and shoes.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors. MOCA aims for a group with different school, area and arts-access backgrounds.
how_to_apply: Not open now. See mocateens.org and the MOCA Teens page for the next call.
notes: Competitive. Check the page in summer for the next cycle.
duration: 2026-27 group starts mid-September 2026
pay_detail: Teens are paid. The page does not give an amount.

who_can_apply: In 2026, Future Leaders was for age 12 or 13. Counselors in Training was for age 14. Ages were counted on June 8, 2026. You must go to a required orientation and a week of training. You must also interview, and an interview does not promise a spot.
how_to_apply: Sign up for an interview time in the Moraga Parks and Recreation online catalog. The link is on the program page. An interview does not promise you a spot. If chosen, you pick the weeks you can come.
notes: In 2026 the orientation was May 7 and training was June 8 to 12. The page says CITs gain hands-on experience that prepares them for possible future jobs with Moraga Parks and Recreation. The town website also has a Summer Jobs page.
duration: 4-week blocks with weekly AM or PM shifts; most weeks have one full day, 9:00 AM to 3:00 PM
pay_detail: $250 per session for Moraga residents. $270 per session for non-residents.

who_can_apply: U.S. citizens ages 16 to 22 who are in high school or college with a 2.5 GPA or better. You need a valid California driver license and a good driving record. You must pass an oral board and a background check. You must volunteer at least 4 hours a week.
how_to_apply: Contact Lt. Steve Borbely at 925-888-7052 to ask about the Police Cadet Program and how to apply.
notes: The cadet program is on the town employment page, below the police officer and reserve officer jobs. Good character and good health are also on the list. Ask the department if it is taking cadets now.
duration: At least 4 hours per week
pay_detail: Community service role. You volunteer at least 4 hours a week.

who_can_apply: The page does not list ages, grades or a residency rule. Ask the Parks and Recreation office before you apply.
how_to_apply: Applications for the 2027-2028 term will be available in July 2027. Contact Jasmine Bateson at the email link on the program page to ask how to apply.
notes: The committee meets at 7 PM on the 2nd Thursday of every month at the Hacienda de las Flores, 2100 Donald Drive, Moraga. Its service projects change each year.
duration: Not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Teens; the page says age limits vary by program but does not list them. Minimum time: Junior Leaders 1 week, Junior Lifeguards 2 weeks, Deer Hollow Farm interns 3 weeks.
how_to_apply: Follow the application steps on the city page (online account, email, or mail/drop-off at Mountain View Community Center, 201 S. Rengstorff Ave). Questions: TheViewTeenCenter@mountainview.gov.
notes: Age limits are not listed on the page, so email The View Teen Center to check yours. Shifts are weekdays (Junior Lifeguards also Saturdays). Transport to Deer Hollow Farm is provided from the Community Center.
duration: 1 to 3 weeks minimum, depending on role
pay_detail: Free to participants; unpaid

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students who represent Mountain View teens. The committee has fifteen members plus members-at-large. Residency or school rules are not spelled out on the page.
how_to_apply: Use the application link on the city YAC page. Questions: yac@mountainview.gov or 650-903-6331.
notes: Meets twice a month, August to June, at 4:30 p.m. in person at The View Teen Center, 263 Escuela Ave. Email to ask whether 2026-27 seats are still open. Re-check on 2026-10-10 returned HTTP 403 (page could not be read), so status and verified_on were left as they were.
duration: School year, August to June
pay_detail: Unpaid; no cost stated

who_can_apply: Bay Area residents who attend a local high school, are at least 15 and have finished 9th grade before it starts. Parent or guardian permission is needed under 18. GPA is not considered.
how_to_apply: Contact Academy@BayAreaMetro.Gov or 415-778-5207. The page does not detail the application steps.
notes: MTC's older 'High School Internship Program' pages date to 2018. The high school program MTC lists now is this Academy. It is mostly virtual evening sessions. It is not a job placement.
duration: 2026: virtual Thursday evening sessions in July plus a final in-person session at Bay Area Metro Center, San Francisco (July 31, 2026)
pay_detail: Stipend paid after completion; amount not stated

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 14. Under 18 you fill out an extra section and a parent or guardian must sign. All volunteers must clear Live Scan fingerprinting.
how_to_apply: Fill out and sign the Volunteer Application (PDF). The form does not say where to return it, so ask at the Murrieta library (8 Town Square).
notes: The form lists the Teen Advisory Council as one option but gives no details about it. Confirm first how to return the form.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Teens who live in the City of Murrieta and are in 9th to 12th grade at a Murrieta Valley Unified School District school. You need two references.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application with five short answers and two references. Turn it in at the Murrieta Youth Center (40644 California Oaks Rd) or email it to the city contact on the sheet. Questions: Community Services at (951) 304-PARK, ext. 6117.
notes: Confirm first: the only sheet found is for the 2024-25 term. Members must go to all mandatory city events. Meetings were on the 1st and 3rd Tuesday evenings.
duration: Nine months, October to May, with an optional extended summer term; meetings in the evening
pay_detail: Unpaid. No stipend is stated.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 21. You must live in or go to school in Orange County and have finished 9th grade. You should want to learn about fire and emergency careers.
how_to_apply: Email the fire department using the contact link on the program page. Ask for the program application. Ride-along forms for minors are posted on the page.
notes: This program used to be Explorer Post 309. You learn what school you need for fire careers. You also get tips on how to get ready.
duration: Weekly program
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Youth volunteers must be in 7th through 12th grade and age 12 to 18. The Young Adult Advisory Council (YAAC) is only for teens who live in Newport Beach.
how_to_apply: Teens fill out the online application themselves on the library's volunteer portal (application form number 2) and lead communication with staff. You must attend volunteer training before starting.
notes: Volunteers age 15 and up must complete fingerprinting and a background check. Applying does not guarantee a spot. Questions go to the library's Teen Services team through the email link on the page.
duration: 20 hours of service per year. Children's Department shifts are 1 to 2 hours a week. YAAC also meets monthly.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: You must be 16 years old on or before March 30, 2027. No lifeguard experience is needed. You must pass a 1000-meter ocean swim and a 1000-meter run-swim-run tryout.
how_to_apply: Apply online for the Lifeguard Trainee job. If you qualify, you are invited to a tryout. Top finishers get an interview. You must also pass the Basic Lifeguard Academy.
notes: Practice workout schedule is on the program page. Dates can change with weather. The tryout has no wetsuits or fins. The info night is at Lifeguard Headquarters, 70 Newport Pier, in person or on Zoom, and is not required. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work.
duration: Training academy, then seasonal work
pay_detail: Paid training is $16.90 an hour. Lifeguard I pay is $25.50 to $31.02 an hour.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 15. The page does not state a residency rule.
how_to_apply: Submit a Teen Leader Application. Qualified applicants may be interviewed and the top candidates are chosen. Selected teens pass a background check, register online and pay the fee. Contact Recreation and Senior Services at (949) 644-3151.
notes: This is a volunteer role with a fee, not a paid job. The same page lists the Mayor's Youth Council (an unpaid internship that runs October 2026 to August 2027, applications May 15 to Sept 4, 2026), but it does not state an age or grade, so it is not listed as its own card.
duration: The 2026 session; exact length not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid. Selected teens pay a $206 program fee for 2026.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors who live in or attend high school in Boyle Heights. A work permit and proof of authorization to work in the U.S. are required.
how_to_apply: Online application. The link and deadline are posted on the page each February.
notes: Narrow: ten spots a year (eight new interns and two returning peer mentors) for Boyle Heights students. Transportation is provided.
duration: Spring: select Saturdays in April and May (about 10 a.m. to 1:30 p.m.). Summer: six weeks in June and July, 24 hours a week.
pay_detail: Interns are paid museum employees. The hourly rate is not stated.

who_can_apply: Ages 17 to 24 who live in San Mateo County or in Cupertino, Los Altos, Milpitas, Mountain View, Palo Alto, Santa Clara or Sunnyvale. High school students who live outside the area qualify if their school is inside it. In-school youth 17 to 21 need low household income. They also need one of these: justice involvement, being unhoused or a runaway, or foster care (in it now or aged out).
how_to_apply: Fill out the short interest form on the NOVAworks Young Adults page, then meet a Career Advisor. You can also email youngadults@novaworks.org, call 408-730-7640 or text 408-568-7776.
notes: Narrow eligibility. The FAQ says internships are 18 and up, so a 17 year old gets coaching and training first. Teens under 17 do not qualify. In-school applicants need income under the program limits plus a barrier; the page's out-of-school barrier list is broader.
duration: 4 to 5 weeks of career readiness first, then an internship (most interns work 10 to 20 hours a week)
pay_detail: Coaching is free. Paid internships start at $19.50 per hour (Sunnyvale minimum wage), at least $7,800 for 400 hours. Internships are for ages 18 and up.

who_can_apply: Must live in Oakland. No work experience needed. Free. Partner groups set their own ages (for example YEP 14 to 18, Youth UpRising 14 to 21, Lao Family 16 to 21).
how_to_apply: Pick a partner from the City list (YEP, Youth UpRising, Lao Family, Trybe, Rising Sun, Destiny Arts, Soccer Without Borders, YouthBeat, Alameda County Office of Education GCGI-GET) and apply on that group's site or by phone.
notes: City Council approved more than $3.1 million for 2026 and 2027 summer youth jobs, so a 2027 round is expected. Another City page lists ages 16 to 21, so check each partner's own age rule. Under-18 workers need a work permit (OUSD Linked Learning can help OUSD students).
duration: Up to 100 paid hours (varies by partner)
pay_detail: At least Oakland's minimum wage; exact rate set by each partner

who_can_apply: Oakland youth ages 16 to 21, per this City page.
how_to_apply: Contact Lao Family Community Development (510) 533-8850, Youth Employment Partnership (510) 533-3447, or Trybe (510) 985-9915. OWDB email: OWDB@oaklandca.gov.
notes: This City page is older than the MSYEP page (which lists partners with other ages, such as YEP 14 to 18 and Lao Family 16 to 21). Treat 16 to 21 as the safe range and confirm with the partner.
pay_detail: Not stated on this page; the City's MSYEP page says at least Oakland's minimum wage

who_can_apply: The City is hiring for its recreation jobs. The page does not state a minimum age. It strongly encourages people who speak Spanish, Cantonese and Mandarin to apply.
how_to_apply: Apply at governmentjobs.com/careers/oaklandca. Questions: parksandrec@oaklandca.gov or (510) 238-7275.
notes: The hiring process takes several months, so apply early. Check each posting for minimum age and pay. The governmentjobs.com/careers/oaklandca portal showed 0 openings on Oct 7, 2026. If you cannot find the posting, call (510) 238-7275.
duration: Varies by posting; mostly seasonal
pay_detail: Paid job. Not posted on the page; see each job posting

who_can_apply: Teens who join through the library teen volunteer application: ages 13 to 17, or 18 and still in high school. The TAB page itself states no age rule.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer Application and choose 'leadership', or ask your branch teen librarian.
notes: Meets monthly at Main (TeenZone), 81st Ave, Asian, Cesar Chavez, Dimond and Rockridge. The same page also covers the Oakland Youth Poet Laureate program.
duration: One meeting a month

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 17, or 18 and still in high school. Also takes teens with court-ordered service hours.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Teen Volunteer Application, or stop by a branch.
notes: The library cannot promise a spot at a specific branch. About two thirds of library volunteers are teens, per the page.
duration: Shifts when the library is open; the form asks for morning and afternoon or evening availability, any day of the week

who_can_apply: Students entering 11th or 12th grade interested in animal care or environmental education.
how_to_apply: Online form with a cover letter (500 words max) and resume or transcript, then an interview.
notes: Up to 6 interns, so it is likely competitive. No stipend is listed; ask. Financial aid is available for the $50 fee.
duration: About 200 hours over 7 weeks (June 10 to July 28 or Aug 1 in 2026); shifts 9 am to 4:30 pm, Sunday to Wednesday or Wednesday to Saturday
pay_detail: $50 non-refundable fee when selected (aid available). No stipend is listed.

who_can_apply: Must be 13 or turning 13 in the application season.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application, interview, then attend both mandatory training days.
notes: Unpaid, and teens pay a small fee (aid available). Must be 13 or turn 13 in the application season.
duration: School year: every other weekend. Summer: about once a week. Shifts 9:30 am to 4 pm.
pay_detail: $50 first year, then $25 a year; financial aid on request

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12 for Teen Assistant (no experience needed). Paid Teacher and Administrative Intern roles are for grades 11 to 12 with previous camp experience and one letter of recommendation. All roles need at least 3 one-week sessions.
how_to_apply: Each role has its own online application (Volgistics link on the Oakland Zoo page). Interns also need one recommendation letter. A required training day is held in May.
notes: Great first step: be a Teen Assistant, then apply to be a paid intern. The 2026 info meetings were in March and the 2026 training was Sunday May 17; expect similar timing for 2027.
duration: 1-week sessions, Mon to Fri, June 1 to Aug 7 (2026); at least 3 sessions (Administrative Intern: 3 sessions in a row)
pay_detail: Teen Assistant unpaid (community service hours). Interns: $400 per week stipend, assuming full attendance.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 6 to 12. The page does not list a city residency rule.
how_to_apply: Email Alicia, the city staff contact named on the program page. Use the email link on that page. Ask how to join.
notes: Meetings are at the Oakley Recreation Center, 1250 O'Hara Avenue. The Teen page also mentions CORE Camp, a six-week summer camp that mixes camp games with community service. The Teen page does not give ages or dates for CORE Camp.
duration: Meets monthly, August to May
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: You must be at least 16 to work at the annual OC Fair. Some jobs require 18 or older. Applicants 17 and under must provide a valid work permit, available through their school, unless they have already graduated from high school. You must show documents proving identity and work eligibility in the U.S.
how_to_apply: Read the Fair's jobs page, then contact Human Resources at (714) 708-1563 or humanresources@ocfair.com. The page lists no application link.
notes: The page does not describe an application link or a pay rate, so call or email HR to ask when summer 2027 hiring opens. Applicants 18 and older must pass a background screening.
duration: The OC Fair runs for a few weeks in summer. Fairgrounds also hosts 150+ events a year.
pay_detail: Pay not stated on the page

who_can_apply: Teens are typically 12 to 17, but each branch sets its own age range, so check with your local branch. Court-ordered community service is not offered.
