how_to_apply: Contact your local branch to confirm there is an opening. Once a spot is confirmed, fill out the OCCR Volunteer Registration Form, print it, and drop it off at the branch.
notes: The registration form is shared by several county agencies, so some questions may not apply to you. Ask your branch what it needs. Arrive on time and tell the branch as early as you can if you miss a shift. OC Public Libraries points teens who need court-ordered hours to the OneOC Court Referral Program.
duration: Flexible shifts, set by the branch
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: You must be 14 years old or entering 9th grade. You need basic sailing skills and should enjoy working with children.
how_to_apply: Check the class list and sign up online. For a scholarship, you must meet the eligibility requirements. Scholarship details are given at your interview. Call 949-645-9412 with questions.
notes: You can choose to take the written test for a Small Powerboat Certification. The program is at the OCC Waterfront Campus, 1801 West Coast Hwy, Newport Beach.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: The fee is $525. Scholarships are available.

who_can_apply: High school students, freshman through senior. You must apply before you can register.
how_to_apply: Fill out the CIT application on the program page. Then register for a session after you are accepted.
notes: This is a program you pay for. It is not a paid job. The same page lists a week-long Marine Science Careers and Internship Academy for ages 14 to 17.
duration: 3 weeks, 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
pay_detail: $400, plus a 3% registration fee at checkout. Members at the Family level or above get 10% off.

who_can_apply: High school students and college students. You must be able to get to the Ocean Institute each week.
how_to_apply: Watch the program page for the summer 2027 opening. Then apply online. Last year, interviews ran from August 17 to September 4.
notes: Interns must go to all required workshops, the May poster session and the June showcase. They do not have to work on holiday weeks. Some projects need you to board the research vessel Sea Explorer on weekends.
duration: September to June, one 4-hour shift a week
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Public Programs Docents must be 14 or older. Maritime Education Docents must be 16 or older. Other roles on the page are for ages 18 and up.
how_to_apply: When applications reopen, use the online form on the program page. Forms are reviewed three times a year. Then you have an interview and training.
notes: Public Programs Docents work at least two shifts a month on Saturday and Sunday, 9:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. or 12:00 to 3:00 p.m. Maritime Education Docents work shifts between 10 a.m. and 2 p.m., any day. If you get no confirmation email, submit the application again.
duration: At least 6 hours a month for at least one year
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer roles.

who_can_apply: Students age 15 or older and adults. You must volunteer for 6 months or more. No summer-only volunteering.
how_to_apply: Apply online, then email the volunteer reference form to OCHVolunteer@hhs.sccgov.org. You will be contacted within two weeks for an interview. Then a 2-hour orientation, background check, health screening clearance and badging. Phone: 408-947-2830.
notes: Read on the official O'Connor Hospital page on 2026-10-16. Health screening asks for proof of a COVID-19 vaccine or booster, a yearly flu shot, immunity to measles, mumps, rubella and varicella, a Tdap shot, and a TB test within the past 3 months (then yearly). Start gathering shot records early. The page does not state weekly shift length or any fee. O'Connor is a sister hospital of Santa Clara Valley Medical Center. The email link on the page has a typo, so type OCHVolunteer@hhs.sccgov.org by hand.
duration: 6 months or more

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 21. You must keep a 2.0 GPA or higher and be in good standing with school administrators. You cannot have arrests or convictions and cannot be on probation. You cannot have a severe mental or physical limit.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Explorer Interest Form on the program page. Or call 714-566-2711 to learn more.
notes: The first police Explorer post in the US began in Santa Ana in 1959. The Sheriff also runs a Teen Academy for ages 16 to 18.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid. Explorers are volunteers.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 16 to 18.
how_to_apply: To join the interest list, email TeenAcademy@ocsheriff.gov. In 2026, the flyer said to email your form to the same address.
notes: Space is limited. The service hours can count toward high school graduation rules. The flyer lists Community Engagement at 714-647-4141 for questions.
duration: 5 days, 8 a.m. to 12 p.m.
pay_detail: Free. You earn community service hours.

who_can_apply: In-school young adults ages 14 to 21 who are low income (free or reduced-price lunch counts) and have at least one barrier: basic skills deficient or English learner, offender, homeless/runaway/foster, pregnant or parenting, or disabled. Out-of-school youth ages 16 to 24 who are not in school (adult education is allowed) and have a barrier such as dropout, offender, homeless/runaway/foster, pregnant or parenting, or disabled.
how_to_apply: Fill out the READY S.E.T. OC interest form (Interest and Eligibility Assessment) linked on the page. Services are delivered by a network of regional providers, which the page does not name.
notes: Federal WIOA program, so eligibility rules apply (income and barriers). Cost to the student is not stated on the page. Questions: County Directory Assistance 855-886-5400. Many teens will not qualify, so read the eligibility list first.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Work experience can be paid or unpaid. Wage not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Students in high school, college, grad school or medical school who are interested in health care and innovation. You must be at least a high school freshman. You need to be on site 40 hours a week.
how_to_apply: Apply on the CHOC website when the form opens. Interviews are rolling, so apply early. You are admitted by form and interview.
notes: The page links to a CHOC volunteer page but does not state its age rule here. Hospital and outpatient shadowing rotations are 18 and up. Business casual dress is expected.
duration: About 8 weeks, June 15 to Aug 7 (2026 dates). Monday to Thursday plus Friday field trips.
pay_detail: No cost to join. Pay is not mentioned on the page. Meals, housing and travel are on you; help for low-income students may be available.

who_can_apply: Girls in 9th to 12th grade. The four-week externship is for 11th grade girls.
how_to_apply: The page has a Contact Us link. Ask the Girls Inc. Programs Team how girls sign up.
notes: For girls only. Past host companies named on the page include PepsiCo, Edwards Lifesciences and Disneyland Resort. Confirm dates with Girls Inc. first. The 2026 host flyer says girls get a minimum of 50 hours of training; the page says up to 40, so ask Girls Inc. which is current.
duration: Four-month program with a four-week externship (the 2026 externship was in July)
pay_detail: Free to join. The page does not say the externship is paid.

who_can_apply: Current high school students. You need a parent consent form and one Dual Enrollment Release Form. Concurrent students also submit a Concurrent Enrollment Release Form from their high school every term. High school students cannot register for a college class without a valid release form on file.
how_to_apply: Apply to Golden West College (new students create an Open CCC account) and write down your CCCID number. Then turn in the consent forms and get your high school's approval. Dual enrollment classes are taught at your high school, so your counselor adds you to the roster. Concurrent students use a Concurrent Enrollment Release Form and register in MyGWC. Questions: dualenrollment@gwc.cccd.edu.
notes: The consent form also covers Coastline College and Orange Coast College in the same district. Only one parent consent form is needed for all high school years. The page says tuition is free, but students may still owe college fees and course costs. It offers a Foundation financial aid form and a possible fee waiver. Re-check 2026-10-10: the page says it is now accepting applications and consent forms for Fall 2026, with no closing date posted. Fetched by curl after a certificate error.
duration: By term: fall, winter/spring and summer
pay_detail: Tuition is free. Dual enrollment classes taught at a high school are free; concurrent students pay college fees and books unless their district covers them. A limited number of help grants are offered.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors from anywhere in Orange County. The 2025-26 group came from 9 school districts and was chosen from over 100 applicants.
how_to_apply: Application steps are not listed on the pages. Email langsonteens@uci.edu to ask.
notes: The museum is named UC Irvine Langson Orange County Museum of Art on the page. Confirm dates and any stipend with the museum first.
duration: One school year; the 2025-26 exhibition opens in June 2026
pay_detail: Not stated on the program pages

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 18, or 16 with parent permission. You must pass a background check and give at least 36 hours a year. The page does not give a separate age rule for OC Zoo roles.
how_to_apply: Complete the brief interest form linked from the OC Parks Volunteers page and tell them the work that interests you. Pass a background check and attend training. For short term opportunities, search the activity listing. Questions: volunteer@ocparks.com.
notes: Volunteers 16 with parent permission (the page does not mention 17). The page lists historic docent, backcountry patrol and OC Zoo roles. It lists others too. Re-check 2026-10-10: the page gives no sign-up deadline and does not say sign-up is ongoing, so status is unconfirmed, not rolling.
duration: Long term; at least 36 hours a year. The page also lists short term volunteer opportunities.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12 who want to take their leadership to the next level. The page does not list other eligibility rules.
how_to_apply: Apply in spring. The page does not link a form, so email Nadia Khodadadi at OC Pathways (address on the page) to ask how to apply.
notes: Ask your school CTE teacher or counselor too. Confirm the spring dates with OC Pathways.
duration: One school year, built around a year-long Impact Project
pay_detail: Not stated

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 21 with a 2.0 GPA or higher, no arrests or convictions, and fire-safe grooming. Anyone over 18 also does a background check.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Cadet Interest Form on the OCFA site to join the interest list. Later, people on the list are asked to finish a longer form.
notes: OCFA serves many Orange County cities. Ask which cadet post is nearest to you.
duration: 10 week Fire Cadet Trainee Academy (9 weeks at cadet posts, final exam in week 10)
pay_detail: Not stated; described as a community-based youth program

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 21 who live in Orange County. You must be in foster care, extended foster care or Kin-GAP. That means a current or past Orange County dependent. Young adults on probation may also qualify.
how_to_apply: Ask your social worker for an ILP referral. You can also call Orangewood at 714-619-0200 or visit the Orangewood Resource Center, 1575 E. 17th Street, Santa Ana.
notes: Orangewood's Lyon Workforce Academy is a separate program, so it is not listed here. The OC Social Services Agency pays for part of the program. Call to ask about cost.
duration: Nine months of case management
pay_detail: Not a job. Workshops may earn gift card incentives. The page does not say whether the program is free.

who_can_apply: High school students, called special admit students. Students in grades K to 8 need approval from a Santa Ana College dean.
how_to_apply: Use the New Students page on the Dual Enrollment site. Contact the Dual Enrollment Office at dualenrollment@sac.edu or (714) 564-6931.
notes: If you go over the unit limit you pay the enrollment fee for all units, not only the extra ones. The office is closed on Fridays in summer. Re-check 2026-10-10: the page says the program is active. It gives no term dates, no deadline, and no word that applications are taken on an ongoing basis. So the status is unconfirmed, not rolling.
duration: By semester
pay_detail: The enrollment fee is waived for part-time special admit students (under 12 units, or 15 units or fewer from partner schools). Other costs are not stated on this page.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 19. The page says there are no exceptions to the age rule. A parent or guardian must consent if you are under 18.
how_to_apply: Check the County of Orange volunteer page in spring 2027 and apply there. Questions: SSATeenVolunteers@ssa.ocgov.com.
notes: You must dress in neat business clothes. There are several office sites. The addresses are on the application form. Volunteers sign a promise to keep client facts private.
duration: About 6 weeks, roughly June to August, up to 20 hours a week
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer work experience.

who_can_apply: High school students (special admit students). Students in grades K to 8 need approval from an SCC division dean. High school students sign up through the SCC Dual Enrollment Portal.
how_to_apply: Apply to SCC. Make your dual enrollment profile in the portal with your SCC student email. Send a course request. Then confirm your enrollment. Phone (714) 628-4764 or earlycollege@sccollege.edu.
notes: SCC is phasing out the paper Special Admit Form for high school dual enrollment. It now goes through the portal.
duration: By semester
pay_detail: The page says free transferable college units. Fees for books or other costs are not listed on the page.

who_can_apply: High school students and young creatives ages 14.5 to 19. No grade level is listed.
how_to_apply: Use Register Now on the Summer of Art page. Questions: soa@otis.edu or 310-665-6850. Scholarships have their own application.
notes: The page says ages 14.5 to 19; min_age is entered as 14 because the field takes whole years. Costs money. Prices shown are the 2026 numbers. In 2026 the early discount deadline was April 25. The April 16, 2027 date is the scholarship deadline, not the registration deadline.
duration: 4 weeks in July 2027. The main page says July 7 to 30; the dates page says orientation July 6, classes July 8 to July 30.
pay_detail: 2026 prices as posted: $4,390 full program (3 college credits) or $2,690 per individual class; $7,315 or $5,615 with housing. A $150 health center fee applies. 2027 prices are not posted.

who_can_apply: OUSD students (the page also says Alameda County high school students for the Peralta Summer Institute). Some internships are open to all; others go through your career pathway.
how_to_apply: Fill out the district Summer Internship Common Application. It is a Google Form linked on the OUSD page. For school-year internships, ask your pathway lead teacher or your school's work-based learning lead.
notes: The OUSD page still shows Summer 2024 forms, so look for a new form in January 2027. Not every internship is open to every student.
duration: Varies by employer
pay_detail: Summer internships are paid; amounts vary by employer (see the district list). The district's 2024 listing said Peralta Summer Institute students got a stipend; the current Peralta page only says classes are free.

who_can_apply: OUSD high school students.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's Linked Learning or pathway coordinator, or call the district at (510) 879-8000. The office also processes work permits for students.
notes: The office handles work permits (needed for any paid job under 18). Check the pathways pages on the OUSD site to find work-based learning at your school.
pay_detail: Rate not posted (checked 2026-10-07)

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 17 for two roles. They are Junior Docent and Junior Outreach Assistant.
how_to_apply: Use Apply Now for the Junior Docent or Junior Outreach Assistant role. The center reviews forms and then gets back to you.
notes: The page says most volunteer roles are for ages 18 and up. Use the Contact Us button on the page for questions.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer roles.

who_can_apply: Current high school students who live in the Northeast San Fernando Valley. It is hard to get in. A parent or guardian must come to a required orientation.
how_to_apply: Not open now. If you have questions, write to aguau@pacoimabeautiful.org or call 818-899-2454.
notes: Pacoima Beautiful also lists Bee Wise, Agua Academy and YUTEP on its youth page. No details were posted for them.
duration: 4 weeks, Monday to Friday 9:00 AM to 1:00 PM, 20 sessions (2026: June 15 to July 10)
pay_detail: The page does not mention pay. It says students earn community service hours.

who_can_apply: Current high school students in the Northeast San Fernando Valley with a 2.0 GPA or higher. Returning participants are not eligible. No age range is listed.
how_to_apply: Not open now. Selected students must provide a valid high school work permit. Questions: jfr@pacoimabeautiful.org or 818-899-2454.
notes: Classes run 8:00 AM to 2:30 PM and field days 8:00 AM to 1:00 PM. Dates may change each year.
duration: 6 weeks. 2026 ran with a June 5 orientation and a culmination on July 10, 2026.
pay_detail: Paid opportunity with up to 70 working hours. The pay rate is not stated.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 17. Morning or afternoon sessions.
how_to_apply: Register for a CIT or Lead CIT spot when Enjoy! summer camp registration opens on Feb 4, 2027. To get on the teen volunteer email list, email rebecca.passarello@paloalto.gov.
notes: Same page lists the Ceramics Apprentice Program (16 and older, 2 years of Art Center ceramics or instructor approval, 2 hours a week, one training session). Spots may fill fast once registration opens.
duration: At least 1 week

who_can_apply: Grades 8 to 12. Rising 8th graders can join in summer. You must live or go to school in Palo Alto, Menlo Park, Mountain View, Los Altos, Los Altos Hills, Portola Valley or East Palo Alto.
how_to_apply: Submit the TLAB volunteer application in Better Impact, finish the paperwork in Docusign, then go to an in-person Livescan fingerprint appointment. Contact libraryteens@paloalto.gov.
notes: Fingerprinting is required. Log your hours in Better Impact or the library cannot confirm them.
duration: Fall (Sept to Dec), Winter/Spring (Jan to May) and Summer (June to Aug) terms

who_can_apply: High school students. Needs an online application, a letter of recommendation (returning members are exempt), an intro video and an interview with a nominating committee. Residency rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application, recommendation letter and intro video by the deadline, then interview with the nominating committee.
notes: Check the current deadline with Mitchell Park Teen Services (3700 Middlefield Rd, or @mpteenservices on Instagram and Facebook). Pay is not mentioned on the page; treat as unpaid until confirmed.

who_can_apply: High school students. Needs an online application, a letter of recommendation (returning members are exempt), an intro video and an interview with a nominating committee. Residency rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Online application, recommendation letter, intro video, then an interview with the nominating committee, once applications open.
notes: Pay is not mentioned on the page; treat as unpaid until confirmed. Term length is not stated. Contact Mitchell Park Teen Services (3700 Middlefield Rd).

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students. Dual enrollment is only at partner schools. These are in the Arcadia, El Monte Union (Rosemead High), La Canada, Pasadena, San Gabriel, San Marino, South Pasadena and Temple City districts. Grade and age rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Apply at OpenCCCApply. Pick courses with your counselor. Then send the Recommendation form. A counselor and a parent sign it. If you are under 18, send the Medical Consent form too. Send your latest unofficial transcript as well. Then turn on your LancerPoint account and register. Questions: outreach@pasadena.edu.
notes: Do not email documents to the outreach address; upload them as the page says. Check with your counselor which classes your school offers.
duration: By term. Fall 2026 runs 8/24/26 to 12/13/26.
pay_detail: Fees and fee waivers are not stated on the program pages. Ask outreach@pasadena.edu.

who_can_apply: Volunteer jobs are for ages 15 and over. Ambassador is open at 14 with a parent or guardian. Anyone under 15 must have a parent or guardian who also volunteers at all times.
how_to_apply: Sign up for a coming virtual orientation on the volunteer page. Then go to the training for each job you pick.
notes: The page does not say which roles are only for adults. Kids ages 6 to 14 have separate roles (Shelter Greeter, Boredom Busters). Those need a parent who volunteers too.
duration: At least 2 hours a month for at least 12 weeks
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Students ages 13 and up who live or go to school in Pasadena.
how_to_apply: Send your writing or art to the teen librarian (email on the page). To help with the magazine, fill out the library's Teen Volunteer Application. Limits: poetry up to 40 lines, short fiction up to 1,000 words, book reviews 250 to 500 words.
notes: The library page does not say the age rule for the Teen Volunteer Application, so ask the teen librarian. Teen librarian contact is on the page. The page does not say whether contributors are paid.
duration: Ongoing; the library publishes issues from time to time (Spring 2026 was Issue 1)
pay_detail: Unpaid. You are published, not paid.

who_can_apply: The page does not give a minimum age for individual volunteers. It says people under 16 may take part on site but must have an adult with them the whole time.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application on the PVI website. Staff will contact you with open roles. Phone: 650-326-0665. Address: 800 Middle Avenue, Menlo Park.
notes: Weekday daytime hours make this hard during the school year, so summer or school breaks fit best. The under-16 rule appears in the group volunteering section of the page. Idealist listings for PVI say volunteers must be at least 16, but the PVI page itself does not say that, so ask PVI about the age rule before you apply.
duration: Ongoing. Volunteer hours are usually Monday to Friday, and most in-person volunteering ends by 3 p.m.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer work.

who_can_apply: High school students from Oakland, Berkeley and Alameda. You need counselor and parent or guardian signatures on the High School Special Enrollment Form.
how_to_apply: Meet your counselor. Apply to a Peralta college. Turn in the High School Special Enrollment Form, a transcript and photo ID. Meet a college counselor. Then register.
notes: Peralta also runs a free Summer Institute for Bay Area high schoolers, including incoming 9th graders. The 2026 dates were June 22 to July 31. No application deadline is posted. The old OUSD page mentions a stipend. The Peralta page does not.
duration: Per term (fall, spring, summer)
pay_detail: Tuition and fees excused. Unit caps: CCAP 15 units fall or spring; other dual enrollment 11 units fall or spring; 9 units in summer.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 20 when you are appointed. You must live in Pittsburg city limits. The commission needs at least 3 middle school students, 4 high school students and 2 college students, unless nobody applies.
how_to_apply: Fill out the city application. Then the City Council interviews you and picks the members. Ask Pittsburg City Hall for the form and the dates.
notes: The facts come from the city code, Chapter 2.80, adopted in 2020. Check pittsburgca.gov or City Hall for the current application and meeting dates. The commission meets at least 10 times a year. Members can serve no more than two terms in a row.
duration: Two-year term, August 1 to May 31
pay_detail: Members get no pay. The city may repay approved costs.

who_can_apply: No age or grade rule is stated. The program focuses on youth facing challenges such as hunger or homelessness and aims to keep them in school.
how_to_apply: Email your resume to jobs@plantingjustice.org. Or call the East Oakland Nursery at 510-756-6965.
notes: Ages, season and hours are not stated, so call and ask. Pay is from the page and may change.
pay_detail: $17.50 per hour (page says 40+ paid internships)

who_can_apply: Age 16 or older. No other rule is stated for teens on the employment page.
how_to_apply: Download the job application on the employment page. Fill it out. Email it to Ainsley Pearce, the Human Resources Admin. Her email link is on that page.
notes: The same page lists sports referee jobs for age 18 or older. Listings change, so check the page for the current jobs. A job description link is on the page.
duration: Part time, nights and weekends
pay_detail: $18.00 to $19.85 per hour, depending on experience

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 6 to 12. The page does not list a residency or school rule.
how_to_apply: Stop by the Pleasant Hill Teen Center. Or email the Youth Services Manager, Katrina Hunn. Her email link is on the program page.
notes: Meetings are on the 1st and 3rd Mondays of the month, 7:00 to 8:00 PM, at the Pleasant Hill Teen Center. The council does not meet on holidays.
duration: Meets September to June
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Ages 12 and up. You go to an orientation and get your fingerprints taken. Junior Lifeguards must also take a Red Cross class first.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer application online. Sign up for an orientation and a fingerprint visit. Junior Lifeguards also sign up for the training class on the city recreation site. Then pick your shifts online.
notes: Junior Lifeguards do not make rescues and do not get a lifeguard card. The 2026 class ran April 6 to 10 and June 15 to 19, 9am to 3pm. Swim Instructor sessions ran Monday to Thursday. Saturday shifts are daily sign-ups with no commitment. Both jobs prepare volunteers to become lifeguards or water safety instructors at age 15. For the fingerprint form, bring an approved photo ID and know your Social Security number. Contact: Katelyn DiGiosaffatte, Recreation Coordinator, kdigiosaffatte@cityofpleasantonca.gov.
duration: Junior Swim Instructor: 8 day sessions. Junior Lifeguard: shifts June 9 to August 2 in 2026.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The Junior Lifeguard training class costs $145 for Pleasanton residents and $181 for non-residents. Every volunteer pays $25 on site for fingerprints.

who_can_apply: Students going into 9th or 10th grade in the fall. You must help for at least two weeks in a row in June or July. You must go to a meeting in April and a summer training. You must also be fingerprinted.
how_to_apply: Check the city page in January 2027 for the form. Ask Francesca Kelly (FKelly@cityofpleasantonca.gov) or call the teen office at (925) 931-3435.
notes: The page does not mention a fee or pay. It does not say if you must live in Pleasanton. Last year's application window was not posted, so the January 2027 note is the only timing clue.
duration: At least 2 weeks of volunteering in June to July. Day length varies by program area.

who_can_apply: Teen Academy: high school students ages 14 to 18. Explorers: ages 14 to 20 when you apply, with at least a C average. You must go to school in Pleasanton, live there, or have family who works for the city. You must finish the Teen Academy first.
how_to_apply: For the Teen Academy, call the police at (925) 931-5100. For Explorers, fill out the form (you can print it). Then pass a talk with officers and a background check.
notes: Explorers need good moral character and no history of negative police contacts or poor conduct (the page lists running away and poor school attendance). The page also links an Explorer brochure PDF. Its details are not on this card, so check it before you apply. The city's Behind the Badge and V.I.P.S. programs are 18+ only. The Police Cadet job on the city job board is for college students 18+.
duration: Teen Academy: one week. Explorers: ongoing, with meetings twice a month.
pay_detail: The Teen Academy is free.

who_can_apply: Must reside within Pleasanton city limits. Seats are set aside by grade: middle school, 9th grade, and 11th grade (fall 2026 ad: 3 seats each).
how_to_apply: Apply online through the City of Pleasanton boards and commissions page (link at the bottom of the page, per the recruitment ad). Questions: Office of the City Clerk, 925-931-5027.
notes: The next recruitment date is not posted in the ad; deadline_confidence is last-year-pattern because the most recent cycle was fall 2026. The recruitment ad describes city commissions in general; the Youth Commission's own duties and term length were not on any official page for it, so what_you_do is based on the ad's general description.
pay_detail: Volunteer appointed seat. No pay is stated in the recruitment ad.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 20 at appointment, enrolled in high school or college with a C average or better. Needs a valid government ID (CA ID, driver license or US passport), parent consent if under 18, and a background check.
how_to_apply: Email the completed application to joinsmpd@cityofsanmateo.org or call the Recruiting Unit at 650-522-7629.
notes: Training classes are on the 1st and 3rd Thursday, 5 to 7 p.m. Hours count toward school service requirements. You need a flexible schedule for weekdays and weekends. FAQ is at cityofsanmateo.org/4720.
duration: 9 week academy plus monthly service

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 19 (not yet 19 and a half), full-time student, 2.5 GPA, must pass a background check.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application, or contact the coordinator at 510-293-5060 or Explorers@hayward-ca.gov.
notes: The page gives no closing dates, so check at the start of each window. Meetings are Wednesday nights 5 to 7pm plus training and some weekend events.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 21, currently enrolled in school with a C average or better. No felony or certain misdemeanor convictions, no pending criminal cases, and you must agree to fingerprinting for a background check.
how_to_apply: Email the Explorer application PDF to MHPD_Explorers@morganhill.ca.gov, then complete an oral board interview.
notes: Free to join, but you may need to buy a uniform and gear. Financial help is available. Expected to attend all meetings, trainings and events. Meeting times are not on the page.
pay_detail: Free; you may buy your own uniform (help available)

who_can_apply: High school students at least 14.5 years old, 2.0 GPA, average or better attendance and discipline, no felony or serious misdemeanor.
how_to_apply: Email Explorer Coordinator Officer Charles Stone at cstone@oaklandca.gov, or Oakland PAL (Officer Jumaal Hill) at 510-615-5758 or oaklandpal@oaklandpal.org.
notes: The page gives a minimum age of 14.5 and no upper limit. The page does not give meeting times or dates, so ask the coordinator. Oakland PD also runs the Police Activities League.

who_can_apply: Current 9th graders who live or attend high school in Los Angeles, Orange, Riverside, San Bernardino or Ventura County. First-generation, low-income, or Geometry/Integrated Math II students are considered but not required. About 30 students are admitted each year.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online New Student Application. Add two essays of up to 500 words each, this year's transcript and two recommendations. One must come from a core subject teacher. Some applicants get an interview. Contact PAYS@pomona.edu or (909) 607-1810.
notes: Checked 2026-10-13 on the apply page: it lists the 2026-2027 dates and the June 20 to July 16, 2027 residential dates. Its list of application materials still says 2025-2026. The program admits about 30 students each year. Contact the program if the form is not up by Nov 9.
duration: 4-week residential summer (2027: June 20 to July 16), then 3 years of involvement
pay_detail: Free. Pomona College covers housing, food, activities and field-trip transportation. No stipend mentioned.

who_can_apply: Students currently in 9th, 10th or 11th grade. The page does not list an age rule.
how_to_apply: The page has a link to its application site for high school volunteers. Use that link only to check whether high school applications are open. The page lists no phone number or email to ask about it.
notes: CONFIRM FIRST: the page offers a high school application link but also says only adult applications are being accepted right now. Scheduled Monday to Friday shifts.
duration: At least 1 year; one 3-hour shift a week (up to 3 shifts)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Pomona youth. Each City Council member appoints one youth from their district, and the Mayor appoints two youth at large. The page gives no age range for youth members.
how_to_apply: The page does not explain how to apply. Youth members are appointed by their City Council member or the Mayor, so contact your council member's office or the Department of Children and Youth.
notes: Confirm first: the page has no application, age range or term length. The department serves children and youth from birth through age 24.
duration: Term length not stated
pay_detail: Pay or stipend not stated.

who_can_apply: People who can play or understand the music area they help with and enjoy working with kids. The posting does not list a minimum age.
how_to_apply: Apply on the city's job site, or ask music staff to refer you. Then meet staff and show your skills. Sign a release form. If you work with kids, you need a background check.
notes: Confirm first: the posting does not say whether teens can apply, so call the city at (909) 620-2291 before you apply. Volunteers help instructors and do not lead rehearsals or teach alone. Instruments include brass, strings, percussion and woodwinds, plus choir.
duration: No minimum hours. School year: weekday afternoons and evenings, some Saturdays for shows. Summer schedule varies.
pay_detail: Unpaid. You may earn community service hours.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 12 or older. The TeensTeach and TeensTable teen programs are for ages 13 to 19.
how_to_apply: Volunteers: create an account and submit the individual application, read the handbook, finish the online orientation and quiz, then sign up for training. Teen programs: submit an idea through the page. Staff pick programs that fit the museum's mission and email chosen applicants.
notes: Address: 29 Hubble, Irvine, CA 92618. Volunteer questions: volunteer@pretendcity.org or 949-428-3900. The page also links a Youth Leadership Board but does not describe it.
duration: At least 3 hours a month and 15 hours a year before you sign up for training (volunteers). TeensTeach and TeensTable length is set by you.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page lists no fees.

who_can_apply: Lifeguarding: at least 15 years old by the last day of class, plus a swim test (swim, tread water, timed event). Water Safety Instructor and Basic Swim Instructor: at least 15 by the end of the course.
how_to_apply: Use Find a Class on the Red Cross lifeguarding page to pick a pool or YMCA class near you, and check the fee.
notes: Final test is a 50-question exam with an 80% pass mark. Certificate lasts 2 years. Before the update this file said Water Safety Instructor needs age 16; the Red Cross page says 15. For lifeguard jobs, check each employer's page for pay and work permit rules.
duration: Lifeguarding: about 27 hours in person, or about 6 hours online plus about 21.5 hours in person
pay_detail: Course fees are set by each provider and are not listed on the program pages.

who_can_apply: In-person teen volunteers must be at least 16. You send a City of Redlands volunteer application and a liability waiver. If you are 18 or older you also need a LiveScan.
how_to_apply: Email yrr@akspl.org to ask what is open. They send details after you write. Youth Services phone: (909) 798-7674.
notes: The Youth Services volunteer rules say volunteers must commit at least one month and follow the City dress code. The Teens page also lists a Teen Makers and Helpers Lab for ages 13 to 18 with a sign-up form, but gives no details.
duration: Fall, winter/spring and summer sessions; length not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid. Community service hours available.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 15 to 18 with a reference from a teacher or school counselor. You must commit for one year.
how_to_apply: The page lists these steps for all volunteers: a volunteer application, an in-person interview, health requirements, a background screening, General Orientation and training. It shows no junior application link or contact, so ask the hospital volunteer office.
notes: Confirm first: no contact or junior application link on the page. The page says the commitment is one year and that junior recruitment opens periodically.
duration: One-year commitment, 2-hour shift at least once a week
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 15; you must be 13 by the first training day. Written application, then an interview if selected. At most 20 L.I.T.s per session. Redwood City camps.
how_to_apply: Download the L.I.T. application and email it to tbrent@redwoodcity.org by the deadline. If chosen you interview, then get camp placement and payment instructions. Phone 650-780-5929.
notes: Teens pay a fee to take part (2026: $88, $98, $98 or $49 depending on session). The fee is due after a successful interview. Placement depends on camp needs. A mandatory Saturday training is required. 2027 dates are not posted, so expect a similar April to May window and watch the page.
duration: 1 to 2 weeks per session
pay_detail: 2026 fees: $88 for session 1, $98 for sessions 2 and 3, $49 for session 4

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 17. You must give at least one 3 to 4 hour shift each week, for at least 144 hours and 12 months in a row. No summer-only or school-break-only volunteering. Spanish and Vietnamese skills are a plus.
how_to_apply: Apply online between Jan 1 and Jan 7, 2027. Send the reference form to RMCVolunteer@hhs.sccgov.org. If you are a good fit, you get a phone interview. Then you do an online orientation, a health check, a background check and training at the hospital.
notes: Read on the official Regional Medical Center page on 2026-10-16. You must be fully vaccinated and upload immunization records and a TB test for the health clearance. After 6 months and 100 hours you may qualify for shadowing. Have your reference form ready before Jan 1 since the window is only one week. Benefits include free parking and a free flu shot after one year.
duration: At least 12 consecutive months and 144 hours

who_can_apply: People who live in Richmond or North Richmond and are 15 or older. If you are 15 to 17, a parent or guardian must approve. Some seats are set aside for youth who are 15 to 24 years old. You must be able to go to at least 6 meetings a year and give at least 50 hours.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Oversight Board Application, a PDF on the city page. A parent or guardian signs it if you are under 18. Email it to the City Clerk or mail it to the City Clerk's office at the address on the form.
notes: The board meets every first Monday at 6:00 PM in the Richmond City Council Chamber, 440 Civic Center Plaza. City Council members and the Mayor pick the members. The application says you can learn more at richmondyouth.org or by calling 510-620-6523. Having work or school experience is not required.
duration: One-year term if you are under 24
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page. The application says members get training, childcare, meals and translation help at meetings.

who_can_apply: Richmond youth ages 16 to 21. Must attend required workshops and training to be guaranteed an internship.
how_to_apply: Submit the online Work Experience Program application (2026-2027 form linked on the city page). The team contacts you for an intake. Phone (510) 412-2044.
notes: The page refers to Richmond youth but does not spell out a residency rule. Ask about the hourly wage and your start date at intake.
duration: Up to 100 hours
pay_detail: Paid internship; the hourly rate is not stated on the page

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 24 living in Alameda, Contra Costa, Fresno, Merced, Madera, Napa, San Francisco, San Joaquin, Santa Clara, Sonoma or Tulare county. Must commit to four days a week.
how_to_apply: Apply through the links on the job posts at risingsunopp.org/jobs/. Phone (510) 665-1501.
notes: As of Oct 10, 2026 the jobs page lists three staff postings: two Central Valley coordinator roles and a Bay Area Senior Program Manager. No Bay Area summer Energy Specialist posting is listed. Pay shown is the 2026 rate. The City of Oakland summer jobs list also includes Rising Sun.
duration: Summer; four days a week
pay_detail: 2026: up to $20.50 per hour for Energy Specialists (up to $22.50 during externship); drivers up to $21.50

who_can_apply: Teens at branches that have a board. The page states no age range, so ask your branch.
how_to_apply: Contact your local branch. The page describes no teen application; its online application is for adult volunteers.
notes: Not every branch has a board. The page gives no ages, hours or sign-up steps for teens, so call the branch first. Separate from the City of Riverside Public Library.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 in Riverside County. You must be low income and have at least one of six barriers to work. The program mostly serves youth who are not in school.
how_to_apply: Call or visit the nearest Youth Opportunity Center. They are in Indio, Hemet, Lake Elsinore, Moreno Valley, Perris and Rubidoux. Staff check if you qualify.
notes: This is a federal WIOA program, so you have to qualify. Centers are open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Phone numbers: Indio (760) 802-6059, Hemet (951) 765-0917, Moreno Valley (951) 653-1311, Perris (951) 657-7105, Rubidoux (951) 683-9622. Do not email your Social Security number. Paid work under 18 in California needs a work permit.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Some work experience is paid and some is unpaid. The page does not list a wage.

who_can_apply: High school students enrolled in a Riverside County high school. You must be able to go to meetings every other week and to service events.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form on the Join Us page. Or contact the youth council coordinator for your supervisor district. Contacts for all five districts are on the home page.
notes: There are five councils, one per supervisor district. Students elect officers, and each council's Commissioner joins the county Youth Commission. Commission meetings are public, in the Board Chambers in Riverside. The paid Legislative Intern jobs that run the councils are for college students only.
duration: School year. Council meetings every other week. Youth Commission meetings every two months.
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn community service hours.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors. The city recruits through local school districts, colleges and universities.
how_to_apply: The page gives no application steps. Ask your school counselor or the City of Riverside.
notes: Confirm first. This comes from a city news release about the first group, which had 15 students. Employment is not guaranteed.
duration: 20 weeks, 120 hours of training
pay_detail: The first group was paid. The pay rate is not stated.

who_can_apply: The center serves ages 14 to 22. Teens in Action serves ages 13 to 18. The youngest age at this site is 13, for Teens in Action.
how_to_apply: No sign-up steps are posted. Call the center at (951) 826-2272 (Teens in Action: 951-826-2000).
notes: Center at 2060 University Ave, Riverside. Hours: Mon to Thu noon to 7, Fri noon to 6. The page says the center aims to give youth an opportunity to gain employment, but it lists no specific job training or paid programs.
duration: Teens in Action runs Mon to Fri, 3 to 6 PM
pay_detail: Teens in Action is free. Costs of other programs are not stated. No pay.

who_can_apply: Teens 14 to 18. An 18-year-old can join if still in high school, but must be fingerprinted before turning 18. You must be free at least 8 and at most 40 hours a week.
how_to_apply: Call (951) 826-2272 to ask about joining. No online form is listed.
notes: Office: 6927 Magnolia Ave, Riverside, open Mon to Fri 9 to 5. The 8 to 40 hours a week is a lot, so ask if a school-year schedule is possible.
duration: 8 to 40 hours per week; length not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role. Possible chance to be hired later; no pay rate stated.

who_can_apply: Anyone at least 14 years old who can pass a Department of Justice background check. The library cannot accept court-ordered volunteers.
how_to_apply: Create an account at riversideca.cervistech.com, find a Library opportunity, click 'Apply to participate', then wait for an email or call. If approved you book a processing appointment with Human Resources at City Hall and get cleared by background check.
notes: This is the City of Riverside library, not the Riverside County Library System. The page does not describe teen-specific roles; it applies to all volunteers ages 14 and up.
duration: At least 30 total hours at one library before switching
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Ages 13 and up. Spots are limited and not every applicant is chosen.
how_to_apply: Send the interest application and a letter of recommendation to Megan Eaton, meaton@roseville.ca.us, by the deadline. Selected applicants are interviewed, placed at a program site, then pay the course fee.
notes: The page does not say what day applications opened, only the May 5, 2027 deadline. You pay the course fee only after you are chosen. A separate LDP information sheet is linked on the page.
duration: 10 hours of training plus up to 50 hours of job experience training; starts in June
pay_detail: Participants pay a course fee (amount not posted). Includes t-shirt and name tag.

who_can_apply: Must be 13 or older.
how_to_apply: Complete the online Volunteer Form and a staff member will contact you. (916) 774-5221
notes: The page lists no parent permission rule, tasks, or hours. Call (916) 774-5221 or ask the staff member who contacts you.

who_can_apply: Young people ages 13 to 21. Membership is free.
how_to_apply: Register for an enrollment session at rysecenter.org/for-youth. Then watch each cohort's application. Phone (510) 374-3401.
notes: Per the cohort page: Food Justice, Public Health, Health and Wellness Career Exploration and STAY FLY TAY Law applications are listed as releasing December 2026; Mock Trial January 2027; Roots to RYSE (summer) Spring 2027; YOUTHBRIDGE internship May 2027. Pay and ages for each cohort are not stated. The cohort page does not say any internship is paid; pay_detail was not changed in this check.
pay_detail: RYSE staff set up some paid performance and art show chances as they come up. Internship pay is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Age 12 to 17. Ages 12 to 15 must volunteer beside a parent or guardian who also registers and trains.
how_to_apply: Do the online orientation and sign the volunteer agreement, make an online account and fill out the volunteer application, attend the Shelter Basics 101 on-site training, then sign up for shifts.
notes: Log hours online and also sign in and out in the paper student binder. Court-ordered hours use a separate page.
duration: Needing school hours: at least 30 hours of shifts over about 3 months. No school requirement: at least 12 hours on site.

who_can_apply: Enrolled high school seniors who can get a work permit if under 18, are low income, and meet at least one barrier (for example disability, English learner, foster or homeless, justice-involved, parenting, or struggling academically).
how_to_apply: Download the application from the page and email or hand it in, or pick up a paper copy at Belle Cooledge Community Center (9:30 am to 4:30 pm). WIOA@cityofsacramento.org
notes: Only for low-income students with at least one listed barrier. You can qualify as low-income through free or reduced lunch, SNAP or TANF, or a qualifying ZIP code. Work experience must start at age 18 or younger.
pay_detail: Wage not posted on the page.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 18 still in high school (16 by the end of the program) who live in Sacramento city limits. May complete up to two times.
how_to_apply: Make a parent or guardian ActiveNet account and register your teen for the next session. jrrecaide@cityofsacramento.org
notes: Only one absence allowed because of the stipend. Waitlist spots are filled until the second week. Classes are in person at a community center. Youth who are 18 must show proof of school attendance. The page says sessions are held throughout the year.
duration: 8 weeks (winter 2026: Jan 26 to Mar 18, Mon and Wed 4:30 to 7:00 pm)
pay_detail: $425 stipend and certificate for meeting attendance and goals.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 17 living inside Sacramento city limits. Interview and work permit needed.
how_to_apply: Apply online only during a recruitment window using the Apply link on the L&L page. Selected applicants get an in-person interview, then hiring steps including a work permit. landscapeandlearning@cityofsacramento.org
notes: Fills fast because the window closes at 350 applications. Applications are online only during a recruitment window. Hiring includes getting a work permit. The page also lists a Crew Leader job ($21.83 per hour) that includes driving city vehicles. It states no age rule, so do not assume it is for teens.
duration: Fall 2026 runs Sept 12 to Nov 22
pay_detail: $16.90 per hour. Fall 2026 shifts: Sat and Sun 8:00 to 2:30.

who_can_apply: Youth 13 to 18 who live in one of eight listed North Natomas apartment complexes (address checked in week one).
how_to_apply: Register through ActiveNet using the Register Here button when a session is open. NNworkforce@cityofsacramento.org
notes: Only for residents of the eight eligible apartment complexes (Atrium Court, Natomas Park, Terracina Gold, Terracina Meadows, The Lofts, Valencia Point, Westview Ranch, Willow Glen). You must meet the age rule by the session start date. Only one absence is allowed or you may lose the stipend. Only one session is open for registration at a time.
duration: 6 weeks (fall 2025 sessions shown)
pay_detail: $350 stipend ($400 with optional workshops). $25 gift card for bonus workshops.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18, in middle or high school, living in Sacramento city limits. 18-year-olds need a school transcript. May complete up to two times.
how_to_apply: Make a parent or guardian ActiveNet account and register. Teen and parent must attend a mandatory orientation. PrimeTimeTeen@cityofsacramento.org
notes: Fall sessions are at Evelyn Moore (Mon and Wed) and Clunie (Tue and Thu) Community Centers, 4:30 to 7:00 pm. You must be 13 on the first day. Only one absence is allowed. Graduated high school seniors who are in college do not qualify.
duration: 8 weeks (fall 2026: Evelyn Moore Mon and Wed, Sept 14 to Nov 4; Clunie Tue and Thu, Sept 15 to Nov 5; 4:30 to 7 pm)
pay_detail: $325 stipend and certificate.

who_can_apply: Teens can volunteer. A parent or guardian must sign the application before you start. The page does not state ages; ask your branch.
how_to_apply: Submit the online volunteer application. Teens who need school hours can ask about drop-in volunteering at a branch.
notes: Many people apply, so a spot is not guaranteed. Drop-in is the quickest way to start; scheduled volunteering needs a longer onboarding. Court-ordered hours are not accepted.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 7 to 12. Academies are sorted into 7th to 10th and 9th to 12th grade groups.
how_to_apply: Choose an academy once the 2027 schedule is posted, then register online starting March 1, 2027.
notes: Offerings change each year; the page lists 2026 courses as examples. Some academies are online and some are in person, and the same course may have an online and an in-person section. Open to students entering grades 7 to 12.
duration: 1 week each (2026: June 22 to July 31)
pay_detail: Estimated cost $205 to $520 per academy.

who_can_apply: Current freshmen, sophomores and juniors who attend a Sacramento City, Twin Rivers or Natomas high school or live in Sacramento city limits.
how_to_apply: Use the Register link on the page when the window opens. Email summeratcityhall@cityofsacramento.org with questions.
notes: Dates are tentative. The city also runs Semester @ City Hall, a 6-week spring and fall version open to any high school student who lives or goes to school in Sacramento city limits; its dates are not posted yet.
duration: 6 weeks (2027 start June 14)
pay_detail: $500 stipend plus 5 high school elective credits (letter of completion for other schools).

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 22 at the time of appointment. You must live in Sacramento city limits or go to school there for your whole term. City employees cannot serve.
how_to_apply: Apply online for an open seat. The city clerk reviews it, then there is an orientation and a supplemental application. The Mayor nominates and the City Council approves.
notes: Appointed by the Mayor and City Council, so not every applicant is picked. The FAQ says the $50 stipend applies to the 1st and 3rd monthly meetings. No experience needed. Seats open at different times; check the Become a Commissioner page. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.
duration: 2-year term (up to 2 terms in a row). Up to 10 hours a month. Meets the 1st Monday of the month, 5:30 to 7:30 pm, in person.
pay_detail: $50 per meeting attended, according to the FAQ.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 19, 2.75 GPA (proof needed), letter of recommendation, interview, $35 program fee, mandatory in-person training Jan 10, 2027.
how_to_apply: Apply online (the form opened Oct 10), send a recommendation letter and proof of GPA, then interview with the volunteer coordinator.
notes: Mandatory in-person training Jan 10, 2027. The Summer Camp Counselor teen role (ages 15 to 19) is closed for 2026; check back next year. Animal Care Volunteers must be 18 or older.
duration: Jan to April 2027. 3-hour weekend shifts, at least 2 shifts (6 hours) per month
pay_detail: Unpaid. Cost to you: $35 program fee.

who_can_apply: Age 10 and up. Ages 10 to 15 need an adult chaperone; ages 16 to 17 need parent permission (waiver emailed after sign-up).
how_to_apply: Sign up for a shift on the online calendar; groups of 5 or more email volunteer@sacramentofoodbank.org. Phone 916-456-1980.
notes: Closed-toe shoes that cover your whole foot are required. Full shifts do not appear on the calendar, so check back. People who received food bank services in the past 12 months cannot volunteer there. Groups of 5 or more email volunteer@sacramentofoodbank.org.
duration: Shifts of a few hours

who_can_apply: The page says programs are typically ages 14 to 20 and often need a 2.0 GPA, high school enrollment and parent consent under 18. Each program has its own rules.
how_to_apply: Use the links on the Metro Fire page and contact each program directly.
notes: Details from the programs' own pages: Sacramento Firefighter Youth Academy is free, ages 14 to 17, 9 months of Saturdays 8 am to 2 pm starting end of July, 35 spots, applications open in spring. Cosumnes Fire Explorers are ages 15 to 18 (juniors and seniors), 2.0 GPA, and applications for next school year open in spring 2027.

who_can_apply: Regular volunteers must be 18. Students and scouts can do community service projects without direct animal care. The page states no youth age range.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Community Service Application, or take the online New Volunteer Orientation. Questions: rmaier@sspca.org, 916-504-2807.
notes: You can become a regular volunteer at 18. Court-ordered hours are not offered. You will not get a confirmation after you send the application; you may start a project any time.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 16 to 24 served by Sacramento Works Youth Programs. Ask a Job Center whether you qualify.
how_to_apply: Visit a Sacramento Works Job Center (find one on the Sacramento Works site). Staff at each center help youth access services.
notes: The page says Sacramento Works Youth Programs serve all youth ages 16 to 24. Work experience is one of several services in a case-managed plan, not an open job board. Ages 16 to 24 are served, so this is mostly for older teens.
pay_detail: Paid work experience is one service. Wage not posted on the page.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 24. The page gives no other rules.
how_to_apply: Use the Register buttons on the Programs page, call 916-248-1081, or use the contact form.
notes: Open Mon to Sat, 12 to 6 pm, at 1901 Del Paso Blvd. The Cafe Paso job training cafe is marked temporarily closed, so ask whether job training spots are open. Pay is not stated.
pay_detail: Cost and pay are not stated on the program pages. Ask the center whether classes cost anything and whether job training pays.

who_can_apply: High school students can take the courses marked as open to high school students. The page shows three courses with that mark for 2026.
how_to_apply: If you are not a Saint Mary's student, register with the form linked on the Summer Session page. Ask the Business Office about payment.
notes: The courses open to high school students are marked on the page. The page says high schools are among the students who can enroll. Check that a course is marked open to high school students before you sign up. Saint Mary's is in Moraga. The page shows a different price for Saint Mary's students. The printing course listed an extra fee of $110.
duration: 2026 sessions: June 1 to July 2 and July 6 to Aug 7; some classes are shorter
pay_detail: The page does not give a price for non-Saint Mary's students. Ask the Business Office. Some courses have an extra fee.

who_can_apply: San Diego County residents who finished their most recent semester at a San Diego County high school, are 16 by June 14, 2027, have a 2.75 GPA or higher and have finished at least one high school biology class.
how_to_apply: Online application with a resume (PDF or Word), unofficial transcript and short-answer responses. Questions: community@salk.edu.
notes: Applicants under 18 must get a work permit from their school if hired. Preferred but not required: one high school chemistry class and your own transportation.
duration: 8 weeks, June 14 to Aug 6, 2027 (30 to 40 hours a week)
pay_detail: Paid internship; the page does not state the rate. Transit stipends are available if you lack reliable transportation.

who_can_apply: High school students at least 15 years old who are starting 9th, 10th, 11th or 12th grade in the 2026-2027 school year. Spots are limited and applicants are interviewed.
how_to_apply: Online application when the window opens, then an interview. Contact Kimberly Morrow, Volunteer Coordinator, 909-579-6794 (8 a.m. to 4 p.m.).
notes: Closed now. The page lists a July 30, 2026 deadline and a June 1, 2027 opening for the next cycle. Non-graduating volunteers who finish 100 hours can return the next school year.
duration: At least 100 hours in the school year; 1 to 3 shifts of 3 hours per week
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 anywhere in San Bernardino County. LTLP is required for all teen volunteers at the county's 32 branches.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer Application and turn it in at your local branch library. Then attend one meeting a month at Apple Valley, Chino Hills, Crestline, Fontana, Hesperia, Highland, Phelan or Yucca Valley.
notes: Meetings are the 2nd Thursday of the month 4 to 6 p.m. or the 3rd Saturday 10 a.m. to noon; you pick any listed date and branch. Locations may change with participation. The County Library is separate from the City of San Bernardino Public Library.
duration: One LTLP meeting a month, Aug 2026 to May 2027
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Ages 14 through 20. You must be enrolled in or graduated from high school. You need a 2.0 GPA or better. You must be a legal U.S. resident, in good health and of good moral character. You cannot have an arrest or conviction record or pending misdemeanor or felony court cases. Under 18 needs a parent or guardian to sign a liability release.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Sheriff's Volunteer Application Form and bring it to your local station or email it to the address on the form. Contact: volforces@sbcsd.org, (909) 252-4100.
notes: Members must keep current CPR and First Aid certification and finish Explorer Academy within a year. The page does not give meeting days or locations.
duration: At least 8 volunteer hours a month; monthly business meetings
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role. No fees listed.

who_can_apply: San Bernardino County residents ages 16 to 24 by the start date, legally authorized to work in the U.S., with a valid California ID card. Under 18 needs an approved work permit before day one.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the county's job site when the window opens in March, upload proof of age and residency, attend orientation, then get matched to a job.
notes: Very fast: the 2026 posting closed after 800 applications. Check hr.sbcounty.gov/spark-syep/ in early March 2027 and have proof of age, residency and a California ID ready. The county page shows a PDF on how to apply.
duration: 2026: about six weeks, June 15 to July 24, Monday to Friday
pay_detail: $16.90 per hour in 2026 (about 28 hours a week).

who_can_apply: Eligible youth ages 16 to 24. Specific eligibility rules are given by each provider.
how_to_apply: Contact one of the providers listed on the county's youth page. Openings depend on each provider's capacity.
notes: This is the year-round option when the summer SPARK program is closed. Phone numbers for each provider are on the county page. The page does not say whether 16 and 17 year olds are paid, so ask the provider about work permits.
duration: Varies by provider
pay_detail: Work experience is one of the services. Pay is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: People age 16 and up. You need two reference letters to apply and must commit to at least six months.
how_to_apply: Get two reference letters ready. Then fill out the online volunteer application. Training happens four times a year.
notes: No short-term or summer internship spots. Not good for a one-time service-hours project because of the six-month rule.
duration: At least 6 months, one 4-hour shift each week
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Group volunteering (3 to 25 people) takes volunteers age 8 and up. The page does not give an age rule for individual volunteers.
how_to_apply: For one-time or individual service, email cabr_volunteers@nps.gov. Groups use the Group volunteering page on the park website.
notes: Ask the park about age rules for each repeat role, since the page does not say.
duration: One-time service days or recurring roles
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 30 who are enrolled in an academic or training program (show proof). You must have the legal right to work in the U.S.
how_to_apply: Pick a posting on the City internship job site. Attach proof that you are enrolled in a school or training program. Then apply. The job site says to consider unpaid internships too.
notes: Interns are City employees. Hiring includes a background check, which usually takes 6 to 8 weeks. The job site says to consider unpaid internships too.
duration: Varies by posting. Hiring takes about 6 to 8 weeks.
pay_detail: $19.47 to $22.75 per hour, set by education level

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students ages 13 to 15 who can come to the meetings. You show interest in service and leadership.
how_to_apply: Fill in the online form linked from the City youth volunteer page. Questions? Write to workreadiness@sandiego.gov.
notes: Only for ages 13 to 15, so a 16 year old is too old. For older teens, see the City paid internships. Confirm the current cycle with workreadiness@sandiego.gov, the contact listed on the City page.
duration: Weekly online meeting (Mondays 5:30 to 6:30 p.m.) plus one in-person meeting a month
pay_detail: Unpaid. Gift card rewards at 40 service hours and a certificate signed by the Mayor at 80 hours.

who_can_apply: Recreation Aide: at least 15 and a half years old. Pool Guard: at least 16 at the time of application, no certification needed.
how_to_apply: Apply for 'Recreation Aide' or 'Pool Guard 1' on the City's governmentjobs.com portal. The City then sends interview and skills-test details.
notes: Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.
duration: Flexible hours that work around school and sports
pay_detail: Hourly pay is not stated on the page; see the posting on governmentjobs.com.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 25 who live in or go to school in the City of San Diego. You must be able to serve a 2 year term and go to monthly in-person meetings.
how_to_apply: Apply on the City boards website. Choose Youth Commission and your seat from the Boards and Seats menu.
notes: Seats are nominated by the Mayor and each Councilmember (2 each). Contact is the Office of Child and Youth Success. The chair's bio on the About page says she first learned of the commission through the Employ & Empower internship.
duration: 2 year term, monthly meetings (currently Saturday mornings at a public library)
pay_detail: Not stated; this is an advisory board

who_can_apply: Teens, generally ages 12 to 17. The exact age range varies by branch, so ask your branch.
how_to_apply: Ask a staff member at your San Diego County Library branch how to sign up.
notes: Run by the County library system. It is separate from the City of San Diego Public Library. The page lists no teen requirements. The background check and medical exam it mentions are for adult volunteers. Confirm your branch's age range before going.
duration: Flexible hours, weekdays and Saturdays
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn community service hours.

who_can_apply: Students now in high school, in at least 9th grade. You need high school approval and written parent approval before you apply. You can appeal if you do not meet every rule.
how_to_apply: Apply online to become a Cuyamaca student. Then get approval from your high school administrator. A parent or guardian must approve too. Do this every term, before you register.
notes: All classes make a permanent college record, so choose with care. Your high school district decides if the class counts toward graduation.
duration: By semester or session
pay_detail: Tuition is waived for concurrent enrollment. You pay minimal fees and buy textbooks.

who_can_apply: At food handouts, volunteers must be 14 or older. Anyone 15 or younger needs a chaperone over 18. The Distribution Center takes volunteers who are 6 and up.
how_to_apply: Sign up for shifts through the volunteer page on the Feeding San Diego website. Shifts are posted one month in advance.
notes: Closed-toe shoes are required. Shifts are posted one month ahead.
duration: Single shifts; you sign up for dates that work for you
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 21 with at least a 2.0 GPA. The page does not name a city residency rule.
how_to_apply: To get on the waitlist, email sdfdcadets@sandiego.gov. Give your name and date of birth, and say that you want to join.
notes: Phone on the page: 619-643-2505. Pay is not mentioned, so treat it as unpaid until the department says otherwise.
duration: Ongoing. A one week Cadet Academy is held each summer.
pay_detail: Not stated; described as a youth program

who_can_apply: Ages 11 to 15 can volunteer with a registered adult (18+). Ages 16 and up can sign up on their own. School groups from middle and high school are welcome.
how_to_apply: Create an account on the Food Bank volunteer site, then sign up for open shifts. Under 18 volunteers use the minor waiver, which guardians sign.
notes: Good for a first volunteer experience or school service hours. Shifts are at the Miramar warehouse and the North County site in Vista. Wear closed-toe shoes.
duration: One shift at a time. You can come once or on a regular basis.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Students at schools that run JA Fellows. The page lists Lincoln High and Chula Vista Learning Community Charter. One version of the page also lists Hoover High. The summer program draws from JA Fellows, ages 16 to 18.
how_to_apply: The page has no student application. Ask your school counselor if JA Fellows is offered. You can also contact Madeline Bowen at mbowen@jasandiego.org or 619-682-5155.
notes: Only a few San Diego schools host JA Fellows. Pay rate and hours not stated, so confirm first. Work permit rule not stated on the page.
duration: JA Fellows: 1 to 2 semesters, daily. Summer 2026 ran June to August.
pay_detail: Page says summer experiences are paid. No rate or hours are stated.

who_can_apply: High school students across the San Diego region. How a student or school enters is not on the page.
how_to_apply: Not on the page. Contact Marley Gang at mgang@jasandiego.org or use the Learn More event page linked from the JA San Diego site.
notes: Details are thin. The page gives no cost, sign-up steps or format. The page's email link for Marley Gang goes to a different address than the one shown, so check the address before you email. The page also lists the JA Rising Innovators Expo on Apr 29, 2027, for schools that run JA business classes.
duration: Event day Mar 18, 2027
pay_detail: Cost and prizes not listed.

who_can_apply: Junior Conservatory is for students going into grades 8 and 9. Conservatory is for students going into grades 10 to 12. To get in, you send a form and two letters of support. You also do an audition.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Have two references send letters. Then go to an in-person audition at the Playhouse. A separate scholarship form is linked from the page.
notes: The page prints 2025 in a few date lines for the 2026 program, so check dates on the page. The Playhouse has a form to get a note when 2027 applications post.
duration: 9 days (Junior) or 15 weekdays (Conservatory)
pay_detail: 2026 cost: $500 for Junior Conservatory, $850 for Conservatory. A scholarship application is offered.

who_can_apply: Any San Diego high school student who is a rising 10th to 12th grader.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Teen Council application form during the open window. Applicants were told the result by Sept 18 in 2026.
notes: The page still says applications are now open, but its own deadline of Sept 4, 2026 has passed. Questions: Gia Battista Figueroa (email on the page).
duration: One school year (2026/27 first Teen Council meeting is listed for Oct 12, 2026)
pay_detail: Pay not stated on the page

who_can_apply: Youth ages 16 to 18.
how_to_apply: See the museum's main volunteer page and Volunteer Application link, or contact the museum at 619-232-3821.
notes: The page gives no application steps beyond pointing to the volunteer application. Ask the museum about the time commitment.
duration: Summer camp season; exact dates not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page says you gain work experience and/or college credit.

who_can_apply: High school students with approval from their high school district and a parent or guardian. Students under 16 also need each instructor to sign an Under 16 form. Home-schooled students need extra forms.
how_to_apply: Get approval from your high school district and a parent. Apply online to Palomar. Fill out the K12 Special Admission Approval Form. Turn it in at Enrollment Services or email it to admissions@palomar.edu.
notes: Part-time (11 units or fewer) enrollment fee is waived. Everyone pays the mandatory Health Fee and Student Center Fee. The same page lists GEAR UP, Upward Bound and Educational Talent Search for some North County schools.
duration: Up to 7 units in fall or spring and 5 units in summer without a petition
pay_detail: The $46 per unit tuition is waived for concurrent enrollment. You pay for books and some fees. Dual enrollment at partner high schools is free.

who_can_apply: Junior volunteers are 16 and 17 years old. A parent or guardian must come to the interview, orientation and TB test. You give a school counselor contact.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Junior Volunteer application online. A parent or guardian must attend the interview, orientation and TB test. Give a school counselor or advisor contact. Screening can take up to six weeks.
notes: The processing fee pays part of the TB screen and background check. It also pays for uniforms and badge parts. You can volunteer at one site at a time, so pick Poway or Escondido, not both. Volunteers in good standing can ask for a letter of recommendation.
duration: 100 hours minimum. Juniors can do one 4-hour shift every other week.
pay_detail: Unpaid. There is a one-time processing fee; the amount is not on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Minimum age is 13. Under 13 must come with an adult. Volunteers (including 13 to 17 year olds) who work with minors, seniors or people with disabilities must be fingerprinted and cleared by state law.
how_to_apply: Register on the volunteer sign-up page, then pick events or roles. Fingerprinting is by appointment (619-236-6686) for roles that need it. Wear closed-toe shoes and bring water, a hat and sunscreen.
notes: Not every role needs fingerprints. The page lists Tecolote Nature Center and Tri-Canyon among its chances.
duration: One-time events or regular roles
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 21. You pass a 20 question multiple choice test and a background check. Then you interview with a Police Sergeant and two Cadets.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Then go to a recruiting meeting at Police Plaza (4020 Murphy Canyon Rd). Bring a government photo ID. The meeting can last up to three hours. It includes a 20 question test.
notes: The activities page describes some activities. One is minor decoy work with detectives. A parent should read the page. You must finish the Cadet Academy first. Then you can become a cadet.
duration: Ongoing. You finish a Cadet Academy first. Then there are two meetings a month at Police Plaza: a general meeting on the first Tuesday and a training session on the third Tuesday.
pay_detail: Described as a voluntary position

who_can_apply: Teenagers only. The library's general volunteer rule is that volunteers must be at least 13. Annual volunteer training is required.
how_to_apply: Open the library volunteer opportunities link, pick the Teen Team Program Assistant listing, click the information icon, then 'Fill in an Application'. Sign in or create a MyImpact account and submit. If your branch has no listing, email LibraryVolunteer@sandiego.gov.
notes: Applies to City of San Diego library branches only. San Diego County Library is a different system (see the Teen Service Learner card). The page does not say how many hours a week. Background check and mandated reporter training are listed only for volunteers 18 and older.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Students who go to school in San Diego County and will be the first in their family to graduate from a four-year college. Applicants must be eligible for free or reduced lunch and/or be considered low income. You must meet the program entry rules and reapply each year.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. You get a confirmation email and staff follow up with next steps.
notes: This is a college-prep program, not a job. It is a good fit for a teen who wants help planning for college and careers. First-generation means neither parent or guardian has a four-year U.S. degree.
duration: 3 or more hours a week after school
pay_detail: Free for students and families. Not a paid program.

who_can_apply: Southern California residents in grade 10, 11 or 12 who have finished a semester of high school. You are 16 by June 15 and have a 3.0 GPA or higher. You are college bound. You must come to the final poster session.
how_to_apply: Apply online (free). Mentors read applications and interview students. If you accept, you get a registration link and pay by the end of May unless you get a scholarship.
notes: The page calls it a volunteer internship. Pick project prerequisites carefully. Students may do only one REHS internship per summer. 2027 dates are not posted, so check the page in early 2027.
duration: 8 weeks, 10 to 20 hours a week (2026 ran June 8 to July 31)
pay_detail: Free to apply. Registration fee is $2,000 if accepted. Full and partial scholarships are available based on need.

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 11 who are at least 14, with a 3.0 GPA or higher and a written recommendation from a school counselor. The page says it is not accepting the class of 2028 now.
how_to_apply: Download and print the junior volunteer form. Fill it out and mail it to Volunteer Services. Then go to a 30 minute interview and a 2 hour orientation with a parent or guardian. You also do a TB test and health screening.
notes: The page takes applications only from grades 9 to 11. It says it is no longer accepting the high school class of 2028. Call 619-740-4175 for junior volunteer information (the page gives this number for that). The mail address is on the page (Volunteer Services, Sharp Grossmont Hospital, PO Box 158, La Mesa, CA 91944).
duration: At least 1 year, one shift a week or two a month
pay_detail: Unpaid. You buy a uniform shirt for a small cost.

who_can_apply: The page has a separate high school student application. The minimum age and any GPA rule are not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: When the form opens, submit it. Then go to an in-person info session at Sharp Memorial. After that there is an interview. Onboarding includes a background check and health clearances.
notes: Health clearances include MMR, chickenpox, Tdap, TB blood test, and flu and COVID vaccine or a declination. Check the page for when high school applications reopen.
duration: At least 1 year and 100 service hours, with 75 percent attendance
pay_detail: Unpaid. Benefits listed include a cafeteria discount, meal credit and free parking.

who_can_apply: Anyone 16 and older. You need two reference responses from people who are not friends or family. You cannot serve where you or a family member has worked.
how_to_apply: Apply online and line up two references. They must be work or school contacts, not friends or family. Then do a virtual interview. Send proof of immunity to measles, mumps, rubella and chickenpox. Also send proof of a yearly flu shot during flu season. Show TB clearance. If you are accepted, UC San Diego Health does the TB screening. Then finish online training and go to an in-person orientation and tour.
notes: You may start 2 to 3 months after applying. Questions: volsvcs@health.ucsd.edu or 619-543-6370. Applications outside the summer window will not be considered for summer-only.
duration: One 4-hour shift a week for at least 100 hours over 6 to 8 months. Summer-only option: about 12 weeks and at least 100 hours.
pay_detail: Unpaid
