pay_detail: Not stated. Dual enrollment courses earn college credit. The site links a Schedule of Fees page that was not read, so ask about costs.

who_can_apply: Teens who are 14 or older by Nov 21, 2026.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Here link on the official page (vhub.at/TeenVolunteer). Questions: volunteer@thetech.org or 408-294-8324.
notes: The Oct 7 card said applications open Oct 9 to Oct 23, 2026. On Oct 9 the official page no longer shows that window, and the apply hub page shows no dates in its HTML (its content loads with JavaScript), so the status is unconfirmed. Re-check the official page for a new window. The page lists three mandatory 3.5-hour orientation and tour sessions on Saturdays Nov 14, Nov 21 and Dec 5, 2026, 9:00 AM to 12:30 PM. Applications are reviewed after the deadline by availability and answers. The page gives no year for Jan 3. The page's email addresses are encoded and could not be re-read on Oct 9; the email is kept from the Oct 7 read.
duration: Six shifts in the peak windows: Nov 21 to 29 and Dec 19 to Jan 3

who_can_apply: Must be at least 14 and live in or near Los Angeles. You can start from fall of 9th grade through fall of 11th grade. Seniors and second-semester juniors are not accepted. Training and shifts are in person in West LA.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Then go to every training, interview and orientation session. After you are accepted, show a negative TB blood test from the last 12 months. To hear about the next round, join the Prospective Teen Line Volunteer interest list on the page.
notes: Serious role that handles hard topics. Hotline runs every evening from West LA, no remote option. Training is 65+ hours per the volunteer page (the main Teen Line page says over 100). The page lists no pay and the role earns community service hours.
duration: Training of 65+ hours (the main Teen Line page says over 100), then at least two evening shifts a month
pay_detail: Unpaid. Earns community service hours.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12.
how_to_apply: Pick up an application at the library reference desk (30600 Pauba Rd). No online form is listed. Phone 951-693-8900.
notes: The page does not say how many hours you can earn. Ask the library if late applications are taken.
duration: 2026-27 school year; meeting schedule not listed
pay_detail: Unpaid. Community service hours.

who_can_apply: No age limit. Minors need a signed parental consent form. Volunteers 15 and under (the FAQ says under 15) need an adult chaperone age 21 or older, one adult per 10 young volunteers.
how_to_apply: Sign up for an event on the TreePeople events calendar. The confirmation email has the waiver and parent consent forms. Groups can email volunteer@treepeople.org to ask if there is room.
notes: TreePeople's jobs page lists only an 18+ fellowship, so this is the way in for teens. The page gives two versions of the chaperone age rule (15 and under vs under 15), so confirm by email.
duration: Single events; calendar posted at least a month ahead
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: High school students in Dublin Unified, Livermore Valley Joint Unified or Pleasanton Unified school districts.
how_to_apply: Sign up through your high school's regular class registration; your school's College and Career Specialist finishes the ROP signup. Phone (925) 455-4800.
notes: You must arrange your own transportation to off-site classes. Classes run at six high schools and Las Positas College, during the school day and after school.
pay_detail: Free classes; you earn high school elective credit (many satisfy a-g requirements)

who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 19 in the Tri-Valley area.
how_to_apply: The program page does not say whether you must register. It says to bring several copies of your resume and to dress professionally.
notes: Location: 9300 Alcosta Blvd, San Ramon. The program page does not list which employers will come. Questions: Dublin City Hall, 100 Civic Plaza, 925-833-6650.
duration: One afternoon, 12:00 p.m. to 3:00 p.m.
pay_detail: Free to attend. This is a fair, not a job.

who_can_apply: Current rules are not posted. The 2022 posting said youth 16 and over with valid photo ID and a valid SSN or ITIN were paid; younger youth got a stipend. Confirm with the program.
how_to_apply: Call (510) 985-9915 or email info@oaklandtrybe.org. Trybe also has a Jobs/Internships page on its site.
notes: Trybe's free summer camp is for kids 0 to 14; the paid youth internship is separate and the summer page shows only a flyer with no details. Call to ask about 2027. Do not confuse oaklandtrybe.org with trybe.org.
duration: About 100 hours
pay_detail: City of Oakland's 2026 list says paid, 100 hours, at least Oakland minimum wage. Trybe's own 2022 posting said $15.06 per hour (old).

who_can_apply: High school students entering grades 9 to 12, or ages 14 to 17. You should enjoy working with people and follow rules.
how_to_apply: You cannot apply online. Turn in your packet to the Parks and Recreation Department. The packet has the form, one reference and a personal statement. Questions: 714-573-3009 or tprd@tustinca.org.
notes: CITs at Camp Tustin volunteer 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. CITs at Little Folks volunteer 8:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. A training day is required.
duration: 2 to 3 weeks, Monday to Friday, about 20 hours a week
pay_detail: Unpaid. The application calls it a non-paid position.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 21. If you are 14, you must have finished 8th grade. You must keep a 2.0 GPA, pass an oral interview and a background check, and show good judgment.
how_to_apply: Go to three meetings in a row. Take part in an oral interview at the third meeting. Call 714-573-3197 or email Explorers@tustinca.org with questions.
notes: You must finish an explorer academy in your first year. The page lists two phone numbers, 714-573-3197 and 714-573-3297. Confirm the number before you call.
duration: Meetings every Wednesday at 6 p.m.
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: High school students entering grades 9 to 12, ages 14 to 17. You need a recommendation letter. You also write 5 to 7 sentences about yourself.
how_to_apply: Fill out the form. Add a recommendation letter. It can be academic, professional or athletic. Add a personal statement of 5 to 7 sentences. Mail it, email TPRD@tustinca.org, or drop it at City Hall, 300 Centennial Way. Then go to the orientation and interview.
notes: You apply once for each school year. The application form asks if you can attend meetings on Wednesday nights. City Hall Parks and Recreation phone: 714-573-3326.
duration: Monthly evening meetings. You volunteer at least 20 hours during the program year (June to May).
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program.

who_can_apply: Must be 16 by the program start (June 15 in 2026). Two references (one must be from a school teacher, counselor, coach or similar), signed parent consent form, English fluency, proof of MMR, varicella and Tdap shots, and TB testing. The page names no upper age limit.
how_to_apply: Register in the UC Davis Health VolunTEEN portal, finish all health clearance items, and submit references. Questions: 916-734-2401 or volunteer.services@health.ucdavis.edu.
notes: Located at the Sacramento medical campus (Davis II Building, 2420 Stockton Blvd). Health clearances (MMR, varicella, Tdap, TB test) take time, so start early. Spots are limited and filled first come, first served.
duration: 8-week program, 6-week minimum (2026: June 15 to Aug 7)

who_can_apply: Students in career programs at Davis Senior High, MLK Jr. High, Da Vinci Charter Academy and Esparto High (2025 cohort). Through DJUSD, students are matched to internships by the Internship Specialist.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's CTE teacher or the DJUSD Internship Specialist (Alexha Contreras, 530-757-5400 ext 170). The DJUSD list shows an internship in the spring. It is at the UC Davis Center for Valley Fever.
notes: Based on a July 2025 UC Davis Health news story and the DJUSD CTE internship list. There is no UC Davis application page. Confirm that it runs in spring 2027.
duration: 10 weeks (2025 cohort: Mar 18 to May 22)
pay_detail: The DJUSD CTE page says its internships are unpaid. The UC Davis article does not mention pay.

who_can_apply: High-achieving high school students. No minimum GPA. Admission is first come, first served once your application is complete. No academic credit.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application, two short-answer questions, and pay the application fee. Transcript and personal statement are optional but helpful.
notes: Expensive. The program moved to a new website (discoveryprograms.ucdavis.edu), and the fee page still shows 2025 numbers, so confirm the 2027 price and deadline. Age rule differs between UC Davis pages: other UC Davis pages say ages 16 to 18. A $1,500 deposit is due at enrollment. The apply page says a decision takes about 10 business days after your application is complete.
duration: about 2 weeks per session (2025: July 7 to 18 and July 21 to Aug 1)
pay_detail: 2025 tuition was $6,985 plus a $100 application fee (includes dorm and meals). 2027 price not posted yet.

who_can_apply: High school students at partner schools in Sacramento, Solano, Shasta and Siskiyou counties who are low income or whose parents did not attend college.
how_to_apply: Get an application from the Upward Bound advisor at your school (Shasta County students ask the GO Center). Send student info and a short essay, a parent-signed eligibility form and two recommendation letters back to the advisor. Questions: eduadvising@ucdavis.edu or 530-752-5887.
notes: Only available at partner schools. Federally funded TRIO program for low-income or first-generation students. No fee or stipend is listed on the pages, so ask.
duration: school year plus summer
pay_detail: No fee listed on the page. Confirm with the program.

who_can_apply: Rising junior or senior. Must be 16 by the first day and not turn 18 before the last day. Must be a permanent US resident living and attending school in the US. Two teacher references needed (one must be a science teacher).
how_to_apply: Apply in the YSP portal between Jan 1 and Mar 1. Submit grades, activities, essays and two teacher references. Ask for a fee waiver before the deadline if you need one. Fee reduction requests are checked after you are accepted.
notes: Very competitive (about 40 students). Residential, so you live on campus. Late and incomplete applications are not accepted. Application fee waivers are given on request. Contact ysp@ucdavis.edu.
duration: 6 weeks (2026 dates: June 21 to Aug 1)
pay_detail: 2026 program cost $7,750 (housing, meals and 5 units of credit included). Application fee $45 in 2026. Fee reduction and application fee waiver available.

who_can_apply: In 2026: students entering 9th grade in fall 2026 through students graduating 12th grade in spring 2026. Students moving from 8th to 9th grade can join the high school academies.
how_to_apply: Register and pay online through the link on the Bobcat Summer STEM Academy page. If the workshop you want is full, join the waitlist. Each high school workshop had 24 seats in 2026.
notes: Lunch, snacks, supplies and a T-shirt are included. For questions, contact Mariah Gonsalez, who runs K12 outreach for CalTeach. Her email is on the page.
duration: 1 day to 1 week workshops, Monday to Friday, 8:30 am to 3:30 pm
pay_detail: 2026 fees: $160 for a week, $100 for 3 days, $70 for 2 days, $40 for 1 day. Some 2026 academies were free thanks to grants. There were no regular scholarships in 2026.

who_can_apply: Students who will be high school juniors or seniors in the fall. You need a letter from your school counselor or an administrator saying you are in good standing.
how_to_apply: Fill out the discount program application. Attach an unofficial high school transcript (a phone photo is fine) and the counselor or administrator letter. Add a college transcript if you took a needed college class. Then claim your UC Merced email and sign up for open classes.
notes: Not a job. You can only take classes with no prerequisites, or ones whose prerequisites you have finished. Pay the bill by the end of the first day of class. Questions: summersession@ucmerced.edu.
duration: One summer session course or more
pay_detail: $220 per unit. One 4-unit course costs $880. The application fee and campus fees are waived.

who_can_apply: Rising seniors registered at a California high school for the next school year, with at least a 3.0 GPA. Juniors graduating a year early with the senior class may apply. You must attend the whole week and a virtual orientation in early July.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the UC Riverside summer programs form. Apply by the first deadline to hear back by early June.
notes: In 2026 the program ran at UC Irvine, not UC Riverside, so the 2027 campus may change. No college credit, and it does not promise UC admission. Students stay in supervised dorm rooms with roommates. No remote option and no partial attendance. Questions: oep@ucop.edu.
duration: 6 days, living on campus (Aug 2 to 7 in 2026, at UC Irvine)
pay_detail: Free for students who are chosen. You arrange your own travel to the campus. Limited travel money may be available based on need.

who_can_apply: California high school students in grades 8 to 12, per the COSMOS application site. A GPA of 3.5 or above is typical.
how_to_apply: Online application with a personal statement, teacher recommendation(s), transcripts and a parent or guardian e-signature, plus the application fee. You choose one campus and cluster.
notes: Competitive. UCI's own pages still show 2026 details, so the statewide site is the source for the 2027 dates. Students must live on campus for the full program. COSMOS runs on several UC campuses. This card is the UC Irvine campus.
duration: 4 weeks, residential (2027 session dates TBA)
pay_detail: Fee-based residential program. The 2027 cost is not stated on UCI's page, so check the COSMOS site for the current fee.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 and over. Selection looks at your application, your ability to keep the weekly schedule, past community service, and your education and career interests.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe the application steps. Email ucimcvolunteer@uci.edu or call 714-456-5541 to ask when applications reopen.
notes: Requires a physician-signed medical clearance with immunity proof (measles, mumps, rubella, varicella), Tdap, hepatitis B series, COVID-19 vaccine with booster, flu shot in season, and a negative TB blood test within 90 days of your start date. Also a three-hour orientation. The page says the uniform costs $40, paid by card at orientation.
duration: One 3-hour shift a week, Monday to Friday 4 to 7 p.m., minimum 75 hours
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: High school students. The page lists no age or grade rule. No research experience is needed.
how_to_apply: Email Dr. Victoria Deguzman at Vvdeguzm@uci.edu. Attach a letter of interest, a resume and a transcript. An unofficial transcript is fine.
notes: Exact start and end dates are not posted on the program page.
duration: 8 weeks
pay_detail: Unpaid summer internship. No fee is listed.

who_can_apply: High school students, including this year's graduates, ages 15 to 19. You must be 15 by the first day of your session. You need one reference from a teacher, coach, administrator or counselor.
how_to_apply: Use the apply link on the program page. Have these ready: an unofficial transcript, your reference's name and email, and answers to three essay questions. Each essay has a 1,500-character limit.
notes: Sessions may change. Notices go out in mid-April. Your reference must email the letter by the same March 1 deadline. Scholarships are available to students with financial hardship.
duration: 5 days. Listed 2027 sessions: June 21 to 25, June 28 to July 2 and July 12 to 16.
pay_detail: Tuition is $2,000. It is due two weeks before the session and cannot be refunded. Partial and full scholarships are available for financial hardship.

who_can_apply: Rising sophomores, juniors and seniors in high school. The page lists no age or GPA rule.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application linked on the program page. The page recommends preparing your answers ahead to avoid session timeouts. Questions go to Leanna Fong at leannaf@uci.edu.
notes: The program is hybrid. The page says to prepare your answers ahead to avoid session timeouts.
duration: 6 weeks. In 2026 it ran June 15 to July 22. Weeks 2 to 5 take up to 15 hours a week.
pay_detail: The registration fee is $750. The page does not mention scholarships.

who_can_apply: High school students who are 16 or older. A parent must also sign the permission form. You must find a UC Irvine faculty sponsor on your own. The program will not match you with one.
how_to_apply: Find a lab and a UC Irvine faculty sponsor. Give your sponsor and their department the packet. It has an application, a medical form, a safety form and a parent form.
notes: Without a faculty sponsor, your application is not considered. Email Alondra Garcia at alondg19@hs.uci.edu with questions. The page also lists 949-824-5388 for general Education and Admissions.
duration: 1 month to 12 months. It runs in fall, winter, spring and summer.
pay_detail: Unpaid. It is a volunteer, non-credit program. No fee is listed.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 15 to 18 with a 3.3 unweighted GPA or higher. You should be interested in healthcare research.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Email your transcript to highschoolresearch@hs.uci.edu. An unofficial copy is fine. You then get a signed confirmation by email.
notes: For a scholarship you write an essay and give family tax information. Tax forms are due before acceptance. The page still mentions the 2025 program in its scholarship text, so ask the program to confirm the details.
duration: 3 weeks. In 2026 the sessions were June 22 to July 10 and July 13 to July 31.
pay_detail: $2,350 for each 3-week session. Limited scholarships are for low-income families at underserved Southern California high schools.

who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors ages 16 to 18. You must be 16 by the first day of the program.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Here link on the program page. Incomplete applications are not read. For a scholarship, check the scholarship box, send a transcript and answer the scholarship question.
notes: This is not an overnight program. Past students may reapply, but the page says preference goes to students who will benefit most. You get a certificate. Questions: Rachel Do, rkdo@hs.uci.edu.
duration: 5 days. In 2026 it ran July 27 to 31, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Breakfast and lunch are included.
pay_detail: Tuition is $1,550. Ten full scholarships are based on financial need and merit.

who_can_apply: Must be 16 by June 1. Grade and residency are not stated. A government photo ID and immunization proof are required.
how_to_apply: Sign up for a required Zoom info session. You get the form by email. Send it back with proof of shots (varicella, MMR, TB test). Then go to one required in-person orientation. Email studentvol@mednet.ucla.edu.
notes: Info sessions fill fast. Every slot showed FULL or CLOSED when read. The page also points to the Mattel Youth Ambassador program as another option. Santa Monica and West Valley campuses have their own student pages.
duration: At least 50 hours, finished by August 31
pay_detail: Unpaid. Parking is not free for student volunteers.

who_can_apply: High school students. The Summer Precollege Focus Series requires being at least 15 by the first day of Summer Sessions, and some programs set older ages. Regular summer courses must come from a pre-approved high school list.
how_to_apply: Apply or enroll through each page on summer.ucla.edu. California students in grades 9 to 11 can apply for Summer Scholars Support (need and merit scholarships), and 10th and 11th graders from under-resourced California communities can apply for BASE, a free 6-week online course with a UCLA mentor.
notes: Out-of-state and international students cannot receive UCLA Summer Sessions financial aid. Exact program prices were not found; use UCLA's fee calculator before applying.
duration: Focus Series: 3 weeks; other formats vary (2026 sessions ran June 22 to July 31)
pay_detail: Fee-based. Ask UCLA Summer Sessions for current fees. Scholarship programs described on the page include BASE and Summer Scholars Support.

who_can_apply: High school students. No specific grades or ages are listed.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Today form at engr.ucr.edu/form/ai-enabled-robotics-summer-camp. Email roboticssummercamp@ucr.edu.
notes: Held at Winston Chung Hall on the UCR campus. Dates and price are from the 2026 camp.
duration: 5 days, 9 AM to 4 PM (July 6 to 10 in 2026)

who_can_apply: Current high school students in the Inland Empire. No grades or ages are listed.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Register Now form on the camp page. Email stemsummercamp@ucr.edu or call the XCITE Center at (951) 827-2612.
notes: The 2026 theme was The Science of Fighting Wildfires. Location in 2026: Tomas Rivera Library, 900 University Ave, Riverside. Confirm first: no cost is stated, and the page does not say whether the theme changes each year.
duration: 5 days, 9 AM to 4 PM (June 22 to 26 in 2026)
pay_detail: Cost not listed on the camp page.

who_can_apply: High school students in the Inland Empire (Riverside and San Bernardino counties) who are older than 16 by the program start date. Southern California permanent residents in Inland Empire school districts are encouraged, especially with a referral from a STEM teacher or a UCR outreach program.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button on the STRIDE page. Email stride@engr.ucr.edu or call (951) 827-5190.
notes: Confirm first: one Apply Now button on the page points to an older 2023 form. The page says applicants must be older than 16 by the program start date and states no maximum age. No stipend or cost is stated. Funded through a CIRM grant.
duration: 5 weeks (June 22 to July 24 in 2026)
pay_detail: Pay or stipend not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Students at participating schools. Upward Bound: freshmen or sophomores at Moreno Valley, Perris, Rubidoux, Banning, Norte Vista, Ramona, Bloomington, Colton or Eisenhower High School. Talent Search: Arroyo Valley, Indian Springs, Pacific, San Bernardino or San Gorgonio High. Both need a 2.5 GPA, U.S. citizenship or permanent residency, low income and/or first generation, and interest in college.
how_to_apply: Upward Bound: fill out the interest form on the page to get an application. Talent Search: fill out the ETS application. Give it to your school's ETS contact or email ets@ucr.edu. You can also call the TRIO office at (951) 827-4865.
notes: Only students at the listed schools qualify. The page does not list grade levels for Talent Search.
duration: Year-round support; UB summer program is 6 weeks (5 weeks bused to campus, final week in residence halls)
pay_detail: Free to join. Only Upward Bound summer participants receive a stipend (amount not stated).

who_can_apply: Motivated students completing grades 8 through 12 with strong interest and achievement in math and science. In 2026 the in-person program was limited to California residents. Students can attend COSMOS only once.
how_to_apply: Online application through the COSMOS portal: choose UCSD, rank two clusters and write an essay for each, one or two online recommendations from a math or science teacher, current and prior-year transcripts, and the application fee.
notes: 2027 dates come from the statewide COSMOS site; the UCSD page still shows 2026 dates. Fees shown are for 2026. 2026 rules asked for proof of COVID vaccination and a negative test; check whether that still applies. If admitted, a non-refundable deposit of one third of tuition holds your spot.
duration: 4 weeks (2026: July 5 to July 31)
pay_detail: 2026 program cost $5,518 (housing, meals, field trips) plus a $46 application fee. Financial assistance form available for California residents. Amounts for 2027 not posted.

who_can_apply: Incoming 11th and 12th graders with a cumulative GPA of 3.3 or better who are interested in sports medicine. No application is needed; you enroll directly.
how_to_apply: Enroll directly on the Extended Studies registration page. Add the course to your cart. No application or essay is needed. Questions: precollege@ucsd.edu.
notes: Earns 3 to 6 UC pre-college units. UCSD's Research Scholars also offers life sciences and marine science courses; its older Academic Connections summer program was canceled for 2026. Marine science fall 2026 application closed Sept 17, 2026.
duration: 3 weeks, weekdays 9:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. (2026: July 6 to July 24)
pay_detail: $3,500 for the July 2026 session (commuter only; no housing or transportation). A hybrid fall session cost $2,000.

who_can_apply: Age 16 or older. You must be 18 to volunteer in pediatric inpatient units or the Emergency Department. Minimum 6 months, one 3 to 4 hour weekday shift each week.
how_to_apply: Attend a virtual info session, in-person group interview, online training and health clearance (background check if 18+). Volunteer Services (415) 502-9888.
notes: The Oct 13 opening is for Parnassus and Mt. Zion or Mission Bay programs in San Francisco, not Oakland. UCSF says it cannot take new volunteers for other roles right now. Under 18 needs a parent at the health clearance visit. No high school summer program was found on the official pages.
duration: One weekly 3 to 4 hour shift for 6 months

who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12 who live in or go to school in Union City.
how_to_apply: Submit an application between February 1 and April 1, then interview in April.
notes: Follow @UCTeens on Instagram for events, per the city page. The program runs out of the Kennedy Youth Center.
duration: August to May

who_can_apply: US citizen (the Senate application guide also mentions permanent residents; ask the office) with a Social Security number. Must be 16 or 17 at appointment, a junior (semester) or one who has completed the sophomore year (summer), with a 3.0 GPA and health forms. Needs a Senator's sponsorship. Senator Padilla sponsors California residents only.
how_to_apply: Send a cover letter, resume, recent high school transcript and two recommendation letters to Senator Padilla's office. The page lists Page_Program@padilla.senate.gov as the contact for questions and does not say where to submit, so confirm the submission address with the office. Other Senate offices have their own rules; the central Page Program does not take applications.
notes: Pages pay their own travel to and from Washington, DC. The job is in DC, so a California work permit likely does not apply; ask the office. Moving to DC for a semester is a big step for a family.
duration: Spring 2027 session: Jan 24 to June 4, 2027. Summer 2027 dates to be announced.
pay_detail: $35,360 per year, prorated

who_can_apply: High school juniors or seniors holding an elected or appointed leadership office this school year, such as student body or class officer. Must be a US citizen or green card holder and live in California. Get the application from your principal, counselor or social studies teacher, or the state contact.
how_to_apply: Ask your principal or counselor for the application, or email the California coordinator at ussyp@cde.ca.gov (California Department of Education, Sacramento).
notes: Very competitive. Clubs, debate, Model UN, jobs and self-made groups do not count as qualifying offices. The CDE page was blocked by a bot check, so the coordinator name and contact are from the USSYP site only. If you are a junior now, plan for next fall.
duration: Washington Week March 6 to 13, 2027
pay_detail: $12,500 college scholarship; travel, hotel and meals paid by the Hearst Foundations

who_can_apply: High school students who have completed ninth grade by the start of the program and are pursuing a rigorous curriculum. Domestic and international students may apply.
how_to_apply: Online application with the $85 fee. Email summer@usc.edu with questions.
notes: Expensive. The admissions page does not describe financial aid, so ask summer@usc.edu. The prices and dates above are the 2026 numbers and may change for 2027.
duration: Four weeks, 9 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. each class day (2026 classes began June 22)
pay_detail: 2026 total for domestic students: $8,130 commuter or $11,570 residential. That adds tuition $7,401, course materials $300, program fee $325 and health center $104; residential adds $3,440 room and board. Also a $85 nonrefundable application fee and a $1,000 deposit that counts toward the total.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 8 to 11 in 2026, rising grades 9 to 12. Active MESA, Mission Science and Engineering Transformer students come first. So do students at STEM Center schools. All students are considered.
how_to_apply: When it is open, send a student form and a teacher recommendation. You can use the online form or the PDF. Forms that are not complete are not considered. Contact k12summer@usc.edu.
notes: The page says in person at USC main campus. The USC Viterbi summer programs list calls it virtual. Confirm the format before you count on it.
pay_detail: Free to attend. No pay.

who_can_apply: College-bound 10th, 11th and 12th graders.
how_to_apply: The page has no application link. Email cybercenter@sandiego.edu or call (619) 260-4564 to ask about the next session.
notes: Confirm first: the page lists no dates, cost or application. Its wording speaks to parents about investing in the program, so ask whether there is a fee and whether aid is offered.
duration: 5 days, in person
pay_detail: The page does not list a cost. Daily lunch is included.

who_can_apply: Current 9th, 10th or 11th graders at Kearny High Educational Complex or Hoover High School. 8th graders who will go to Kearny or Hoover next year are encouraged to apply. Your family must meet federal income guidelines, or neither parent or guardian has a U.S. college degree.
how_to_apply: Check the rules on the Prospective Students page, then fill out the online application for your high school (Kearny or Hoover) on the Apply page. Staff follow up after you apply. Questions go to the Assistant Director for your school (emails on the Apply page).
notes: To stay in the program, go to a monthly meeting after school. Go to at least one workshop or event each fall and spring, and keep at least a 2.5 GPA. USD says it serves 120 students in the school year and 100 in summer.
duration: School year services plus a summer program where students live on campus
pay_detail: Cost and pay are not stated on the USD pages.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 and up for aircraft restoration, ship restoration, radio, community outreach and visitor services (16 and 17 year olds work with an adult). Collections: 18 and up. Docents, events, security: 21 and up.
how_to_apply: Apply at volgistics.com/appform/1737643431 or call (510) 521-8448 ext. 243.
notes: Ship work involves climbing ladders and tight spaces. Another museum page lists overnight programs for groups, but no teen intern program.
duration: Set weekly shifts, for example Wed and Sat 8:30 to noon (aircraft), Tue and Sat (ship), first Saturday monthly (radio)

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18 (18-year-olds must be enrolled in high school). Based on the 2024 flyer; check the current year's rules.
how_to_apply: 2024 flyer: application with parent signature, a 1-page essay, an availability schedule, and a virtual orientation. Contact the VA Center for Development and Civic Engagement, vhalomyouthprogram@va.gov.
notes: Closed now. The age, hours and application steps come from the 2024 flyer because the current page only says 2026 applications are closed. The 2024 flyer also required COVID vaccination or an exemption; check the current policy.
duration: 6 weeks, Monday to Friday 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. (2024: June 17 to July 26)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Free to join; volunteers over 100 hours can be considered for scholarships through community partners (2024 flyer).

who_can_apply: You must be 16 or older. Some jobs need you to be 18. These are AniMeals, customer service and events. Parent and child volunteering is not offered.
how_to_apply: Look at the open shifts and apply for one you can work. A volunteer coordinator then contacts you to set up an orientation. You also take role workshops and shadow shifts.
notes: Students can earn community service hours with the same six month, weekly shift promise. Court ordered hours are not accepted. Volunteers must be fully vaccinated, according to the FAQ. Sunday dog care is the greatest need.
duration: Most roles ask for one shift a week for six months to one year
pay_detail: Unpaid. New volunteers buy a $30 Volunteer Starter Kit with a shirt, name badge and manuals.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18, attending high school in Santa Clara County and living in the county. Able to give up to 5 hours a month for 2 years, and attend quarterly Wednesday evening meetings in person.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth Commission interest form. To apply you need to know your Valley Water board district (find your home address on the map on the page).
notes: Meetings are at Valley Water headquarters, 5700 Almaden Expressway, San Jose.
duration: 2-year term, up to 5 hours a month

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18. You must attend at least two weeks of camp. You can join more weeks if you want.
how_to_apply: Summer 2026 applications are closed. Check the Lindsay camp counselor page for the next round. Interviews were in April for 2026.
notes: The page does not say if the role is paid, a volunteer role, or has a fee. Ask Lindsay before you apply. Lindsay is at 1931 First Avenue, Walnut Creek.
duration: At least two weeks of camp
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page. The page says Lindsay offers chances for community service hours.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18 who have not graduated from high school. You must give at least 100 hours in the program year and come to a 2.5 hour shift each week. You must be willing to give public talks, lift 15 pounds, and walk safely around animal pens.
how_to_apply: The 2026-2027 application is closed. Email the youth programs team to ask when the next one opens. The email is on the program page.
notes: Youth programs email: youthprograms@lindsaywildlife.org. Lindsay is at 1931 First Avenue, Walnut Creek. The same page describes Keepers in Training (KIT), a second step for teens who complete at least one year in the OWL program. KIT teens work closely with Lindsay's Animal Encounters department and commit to a 4 hour weekly shift. Lindsay lists its wildlife hospital and exhibit volunteer jobs as ages 18 and up. The OWL program is designed for teens ages 13 to 18.
duration: One program year, at least 100 service hours
pay_detail: Annual program fee of $700. Limited scholarships may be available.

who_can_apply: Open to volunteers under 18 with rules. You need a waiver signed by a parent or guardian. You must come with your parent, guardian or chaperone. Or you can come with a school or youth group and its leader. Workdays are not drop-off programs.
how_to_apply: Pick a workday on the sign-up calendar linked on the volunteer page. You can also email the stewardship team. If you are under 18, a parent or guardian signs a waiver.
notes: The office is at 201 N. Civic Drive, Walnut Creek. Groups can fill out a group workday interest form. Group workdays are three hours long, from Wednesday through Saturday, at sites in Clayton, Concord and Pittsburg. All tools, equipment and instruction are provided. The volunteer page also lists other jobs, such as hike leader and office help. It does not give an age for them.
duration: Workdays on a calendar; group workdays are 3 hours
pay_detail: Volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Age 16 or older. Seniors are told not to apply because onboarding is long (a college program exists).
how_to_apply: Email volunteer_services@washingtonhealth.com with your name, grade, school, phone and email. They contact you only when an info session is scheduled. Phone 510-818-7465.
notes: No GPA rule or fee appears on the current page (older versions listed a GPA rule and $20 fee). Openings are limited. Office: 2500 Mowry Ave, Fremont. The page says the list is closed as of May 22, 2026, but also says you are welcome to join the list now; call to confirm.

who_can_apply: At least 15 when you start. Before you start, you need cards for Lifeguard Training, CPR for the Professional Rescuer, First Aid and Title 22. A Water Safety Instructor card is a big plus. Past lifeguard work helps, but you do not need it.
how_to_apply: Fill out the whole city job form online on NEOGOV. Add a resume. The city reads every form. The best fits go on a hiring list. The top people move to the next step.
notes: The posting does not list hours or season dates, so ask Parks and Recreation at (916) 617-4567. Get your lifeguard certificates before you apply, since they are required before you start. Paid work under 18 needs a California work permit. Teens 14 to 16 who are too young for this job can look at the city's unpaid Teen Heroes summer camp program.
pay_detail: $17.25 to $18.75 per hour (2026 posting). Temporary, extra help.

who_can_apply: At least 17 at the time of employment, with one year of experience working with youth or the public. Some assignments need CPR and First Aid certificates before you start. You must pass a fingerprint check and drug screen before you start.
how_to_apply: Fill out the whole city job form online on NEOGOV. Add a resume and answer the extra questions. The city reads every form. The top people are sent to the department.
notes: The city also has a Recreation Aide job for ages 15 and up. It paid $17.00 an hour in the 2022 job sheet. But the last Recreation Aide post on the city jobs page ran Aug 29 to Sep 19, 2018. Lead, senior and KidZone leader jobs need a high school diploma or age 18. A 17 year old still needs a California work permit for paid work.
pay_detail: $17.00 to $18.50 per hour (2026 postings). Part-time extra help.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 16, eligible West Sacramento residents. Needs proof of the hepatitis B vaccine series, fingerprinting and a background check.
how_to_apply: The page does not give application steps. Call the Club West Teen Center at (916) 373-5877 or ask City of West Sacramento Parks and Recreation.
notes: Page has no year or dates, so ask when applications open. Vaccine proof may take weeks to collect. Runs in summer.
pay_detail: Free to join, unpaid. The page does not list a stipend.

who_can_apply: Concurrent enrollment: grades 9 to 12. Middle College: juniors and seniors from LGSUHSD and CUHSD. Dual enrollment on high school campuses: CUHSD (Campbell Union High School District) students only.
how_to_apply: Start at the college's high school students page and apply through the admissions portal; the page also covers assessment, orientation and registration.
notes: Ask the college about unit limits and your counselor about credit.
pay_detail: Free (per the college page)

who_can_apply: 15 or older. You need a lifeguard card (with deep water) and CPR and AED for the Professional Rescuer. You can get them within 30 days after you are hired. First Aid for Public Safety (Title 22) is a plus. You must pass a fingerprint check and a TB skin test. You must be able to work early, late, on holidays and on weekends.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the city's NEOGOV jobs page. Answer the extra questions. One asks if you can pass the swim test. You swim 150 yards, tread water 2 minutes with only your legs and swim 50 yards. Then you bring up a 10 pound object in a timed test. Training is required.
notes: A good choice if you are not certified yet, because the city pays for the certification class. The posting window was short in 2026 (about one month), so check in January. Lifeguards are mandated reporters and must finish that training in the first two weeks. Paid work under 18 needs a California work permit.
duration: Summer pool season. Exact dates are not on the posting.
pay_detail: $18.00 to $20.00 per hour (2026 posting), starting at $18. Seasonal, no benefits. The city registers you for and pays for the certification class.

who_can_apply: Current high school students who have finished 8th grade. Partner high school classes are arranged through your counselor. Tuition is free for 11 units or fewer.
how_to_apply: Explore with your counselor, apply on CCCApply, set up your student account, submit the CCAP or High School Non-CCAP form, then register.
notes: Students may pay for books and materials. Check your counselor for term deadlines. Davis High was not on the CCAP list I saw, so a Davis student would use the non-CCAP route. Charter and homeschool students may need grade verification.
duration: Per term
pay_detail: Free up to 11 units ($46 per unit fee waived); books may cost

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17.
how_to_apply: Register online through the Woodland Community Services registration portal (linked from the Teen Programs page) or call (530) 661-2000. Email: WoodlandCSD@cityofwoodland.gov.
notes: The page gives no hours, dates or fees. Call Community Services to ask how it works and when to start.

who_can_apply: Santa Clara County residents ages 16 to 24 who are low-income and have at least one barrier to employment or education.
how_to_apply: Call the San Jose Job Center at 408-794-1101 or the Gilroy center at 408-758-3477 and ask about the young adult program.
notes: San Jose Works, a partner program, is also on the page. The page gives ages 14 to 18 for its Paid Work Experience Program and ages 16 to 29 for other city services. Income and barrier rules apply. The page does not say whether job centers are by appointment only. It does not say whether the other services are free.
pay_detail: Paid work experience; the page says you can earn up to $25 an hour.

who_can_apply: Washington Unified School District high school students who are 16 by the first day. River City HS students need a Career Technical Education course; Yolo HS and Washington Middle College students need a teacher or counselor recommendation. Everyone attends one online info session.
how_to_apply: Go to the Internships page, attend the info session, send the recommendation form if needed, then apply and interview with employers.
notes: Employers have included Center for Land Based Learning, Elica Health Centers, City of West Sacramento and others. The 2026 calendar on the page is an image, so ask for 2027 dates: wshomerun@cityofwestsacramento.org or (916) 617-4500.
duration: summer, up to 40 hours per week
pay_detail: Paid by the City of West Sacramento, up to 40 hours per week. Hourly rate not posted on the page.

who_can_apply: Students in Yolo County. Start through your school College and Career Center or counselor, or email CCR@ycoe.org. Age or grade limits were not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Tell your school College and Career Center or counselor, or email CCR@ycoe.org.
notes: B-Unbound is the online platform for finding opportunities (interviews, tours, job shadowing, projects, internships). Placement depends on available mentors, so ask early. The stipend is paid after you finish the requirements. Email: CCR@ycoe.org. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.
duration: About 60 hours
pay_detail: Stipend up to $500 on successful completion

who_can_apply: Oakland youth. YEP's job training serves ages 14 to 24. The City of Oakland's summer list shows YEP's summer program for ages 14 to 18.
how_to_apply: Use the application links on yep.org/how-you-join, or call 510-533-3447 or visit 2300 International Blvd, Oakland.
notes: The YEP page does not give pay rates. Age 14 to 18 for summer comes from the City of Oakland table; the 19 to 24 programs are for older youth.
duration: Summer: about 100 hours, June 1 to Sept 30 (City list). Afterschool jobs during the school year.
pay_detail: Paid; about 100 hours of work in the City summer program (hourly rate not posted)

who_can_apply: Rising seniors (12th grade in fall 2027). Full acceptance depends on references and an interview. No city or residency rule is stated.
how_to_apply: Starting January 1, 2027, send in the CA form on the camp's sign up site. Pay a $25 deposit, which you can get back. You need both the form and an interview.
notes: Run by YMCA of the East Bay. One line of the 2027 CA listing still says '12th grade in Fall of 2026' while its title says fall 2027; confirm with the camp. In 2026 the camp sold round-trip buses from the Oakland YMCA and the EM Downer YMCA ($150), and LITs and CAs went home Friday and Saturday nights between weeks; 2027 bus details are not posted. Teens entering 10th or 11th grade can apply to Leaders in Training (LIT) instead. Contact: clmteam@ymcaeastbay.org.
duration: Two weeks: June 20 to 25 and June 27 to July 2, 2027.
pay_detail: The full CA program cost is not stated. The application asks for a $25 refundable deposit. Campership (financial aid) applications are part of camp registration.

who_can_apply: Teens entering 10th or 11th grade. Full acceptance depends on references and an interview. No city or residency rule is stated.
how_to_apply: Starting January 1, 2027, send in the LIT form on the camp's sign up site. Pay a $25 deposit, which you can get back. To get in, you need good references and an interview.
notes: Camp Loma Mar is run by the YMCA of the East Bay, not the San Francisco Y. The only LIT price posted is the $25 deposit. So ask the camp about the full fee and aid before you apply. A regular one week camp session in 2027 costs $1,065. Rising 12th graders can apply to be a Camp Assistant instead. The camp also plans a teen weekend for future camp leaders this winter or spring. Dates are not posted yet. Contact: clmteam@ymcaeastbay.org.
duration: Two weeks: July 11 to 16 and July 18 to 23, 2027.
pay_detail: The full LIT program cost is not stated. The application asks for a $25 refundable deposit. Campership (financial aid) applications are part of camp registration, and YMCA of the East Bay members get a camp discount.

who_can_apply: Ongoing volunteers must be at least 16. Teens 14 and older can volunteer at many special events. Volunteers under 18 need parental consent.
how_to_apply: The page has no general form. Open roles link to postings (examples: Tustin Expanded Learning Volunteer, Youth and Government MUN Volunteer, Sports Volunteer at Laguna Niguel). Questions go through the contact form at ymcaoc.org/contact-us/.
notes: All ongoing volunteers complete an online orientation, child abuse prevention training and role training. Screening includes an application, waiver, ID copy and background check, with extra checks for higher-responsibility roles. Court-ordered community service is not accepted. The YMCA of Orange County Model Legislature and Court page describes the statewide YMCA Youth and Government program, so it is not listed separately.
duration: Varies by role
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: The page lists the program for ages 14 to 24 and older. Grade level, residency and other rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the page. The page says to contact the Workforce Development team. Phone numbers listed: Urban Services YMCA (415) 561-0631; Bayview Hunters Point YMCA (415) 822-7728; Chinatown YMCA (415) 576-9622.
notes: This is an umbrella page for several branch programs. Season, wage, hours and deadlines are not stated, so call a branch before a teen applies. The ymcasf.org/teens page lists teens ages 13-18 across programs, but it gives no details for Workforce Development. Contact emails on the page are obfuscated and were not confirmed, so none are listed.
pay_detail: Paid internships are mentioned at the Urban Services YMCA. Wage and hours are not stated. Other activities are not described as paid.

who_can_apply: LIT: for 14 and 15 year olds. CIT: for 16 year olds. No city or residency rule is stated. The page does not say whether a CIT must have done LIT first.
how_to_apply: Register online through the YMCA of Greater San Francisco registration site (the Register button on the overnight camps page) and pay the $150 deposit per session. Camp office: (650) 747-1200, Monday to Friday, 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
notes: This is a teen camp you pay for, not a job. To ask for aid, email the YMCA form with two kinds of proof of income. The page says replies take about 15 business days. Families can ask for up to 4 cabin mates who are within 2 years of age. Deposits are not paid back.
duration: LIT: one 6-day, 5-night session (Sunday to Friday). CIT: two weeks.
pay_detail: Each session needs a $150 non-refundable deposit at registration. The full price is shown only in the online registration system, not on the page. Financial assistance is available.

who_can_apply: Anyone at least 15 years old. No experience is needed. Some roles need a background check, and new volunteers go through a reference check.
how_to_apply: Download the Volunteer Application form from the page and email the completed PDF to volunteer@ymcasf.org. Staff follow up within 2 business days. You can name a preferred branch and program area.
notes: The FAQ says students can earn school service hours here. Your references are checked online, so it depends on how fast they reply. The Y has branches in San Francisco, on the Peninsula and in Marin. The page also offers group volunteering for 3 or more people.
duration: No daily minimum. The schedule is set with you.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Young people in San Francisco: teens 13 to 18 and young adults 18 to 24. Each project needs an Adult Ally, who is a mentor. It also needs a Fiscal Sponsor. That is a group that pays project costs, and YEF pays it back.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online grant form on the YEF page when the Spring 2027 round opens. You will have an interview. If you are picked, you go to a required meeting and turn in some forms.
notes: Grants can go to what youth need, projects that fix a problem in your area, or a new business. Teens also serve as YEF Community Funders. They decide which teen projects get grants. The page lists their schools but not how to join. In 2026, small grants of $500 to $2,000 ran July 17 to Aug 31, 2026. They were for supplies and first time projects only. Office hours at Urban Services YMCA are Monday and Wednesday, 1:00 to 4:00 p.m. Other days are by appointment only. Contact Amber Ly at aly@ymcasf.org.
duration: Spring 2027 grants: spending starts about March 1, 2027; the grant ends June 7, 2027.
pay_detail: Not a paid job. Grants pay for your project: up to $10,000 per round, or $500 to $2,000 for a mini grant.

who_can_apply: Must be at least 15 years old, in 10th grade or higher, and in good academic standing. A High School Authorization Form must be signed by members of your school. No prior training is required, according to the FAQ.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application on ymcasv.org (the Apply Today button on the cabin leaders page), get a High School Authorization Form signed by members of your school, and watch email for further instructions. The page recommends applying at least two weeks before your session dates.
notes: Camp Campbell is at 16275 Highway 9, Boulder Creek, CA 95006, per the cabin-leaders page. This is an unpaid volunteer role, so no work permit is needed. The same YMCA's Youth and Government program is already in ymca-youth-and-government-ca.json. Leaders in Training is also listed on the leadership page, but its age and details are not stated, so it is not a card.
duration: Five days per session (typically Monday to Friday). Session dates are not stated.
pay_detail: Pay not stated. The page says this is a way to earn Service-Learning credit for graduation.

who_can_apply: High school students. The postings list no other rules.
how_to_apply: Open the posting on the YMCA volunteer site and click the Volunteer button. Questions about tutoring? Contact Liz Burke at elizabeth.burke@ymcasv.org or 408-310-4257.
notes: The posting lists the City of Morgan Hill as a partner. It does not give a minimum age or say if there is a background check. So ask before you sign up. The same site marks other roles as Great for Teens. One is a youth basketball coach at the El Camino YMCA in Mountain View. That season runs Jan 11 to March 27 (no year given). It is 1 hour of practice a week plus a 1 hour Saturday game.
duration: Teen center tutoring is Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday; hours to be set.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The posting says the hours count as community service hours.

who_can_apply: YTI Youth Council: teens in grades 8 to 12; meets in Mountain View. Friday Night Live Council: grades 6 to 12 in the Gilroy and Morgan Hill area. The application asks for a parent's contact information.
how_to_apply: Fill out the short form. Use Apply Today or Register Today on the leadership page. Then text the advisor, Elena Chavez, at 559-405-3787. Email: elena.chavez@ymcasv.org.
notes: Confirm the 2026-27 meeting dates with the advisor before you apply. The Friday Night Live form is at https://forms.gle/1S4yBfha9JZFys7Y7. The leadership page says the program builds civic engagement, persuasive speaking and project planning skills. The same page lists Leaders in Training, but it gives no age and the registration search showed no open LIT sessions.
duration: In 2025-26, YTI ran August 2025 to May 2026 and FNL ran September 2025 to June 2026, with 6:30 to 8:00 p.m. meetings twice a month.
pay_detail: Unpaid. No cost is stated.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 16. Every CIT who signs up gets an interview. Teens who are 17 can come as a Volunteer Junior Counselor. No city rule is stated.
how_to_apply: Use the CIT Registration link on the Bear Valley page. Registering places you on a waitlist, and staff contact you to schedule a CIT interview.
notes: This is a camp program you pay for, not a job. Camp volunteers must be 17 or older and pass an interview. Y-Assist aid for camp is a separate application from YMCA membership aid; the page says replies take about 15 business days. Transportation to camp is not described on the page. Contact: BearValley@ymcasuperiorcal.org.
duration: One week per session.
pay_detail: $700 a week in 2026 (the same price as camper weeks). Y-Assist financial aid is available.

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12 from anywhere in California. Join a local delegation. Cost and sign-up steps are not posted on either page.
how_to_apply: Two ways to reach the program. Southern California: contact the program director at (626) 604-4210 or use the inquiry form on the YMCA of Orange County site. Silicon Valley area: click 'Sign up for more information' on the YMCA of Silicon Valley Leadership Development page, which opens the YMCA sign-up form. Neither page describes the application steps.
notes: Over 1,300 teens in more than 60 California delegations. The YMCA of Orange County page (Southern California) lists no Northern California contact. The YMCA of Silicon Valley lists the same statewide program and links a sign-up form for the Silicon Valley area. Ask the director which delegation serves your area, and ask about cost and scholarships. The YMCA of Silicon Valley Leadership Development page also lists other teen groups and a Model UN program for middle school students; they are not part of this entry.
duration: Weekly meetings plus conferences in November and February
pay_detail: The fee is not posted on either program page; ask your local YMCA about cost and scholarships

who_can_apply: Youth in Yolo County. The page does not list ages. Fee waivers are available.
how_to_apply: Find a local club and go to a meeting. Then finish online enrollment and pay the fee. Office: bbrinkhoushatch@ucanr.edu, 530-666-8703.
notes: The fee is non-refundable. A fee waiver or reduction form is available. Returning members update their online enrollment and send health forms to their club.
pay_detail: 2026-27 enrollment is $80 per youth (waiver or reduction available).

who_can_apply: Ages 17 to 24, living in Yolo County, and not in school right now, per the page. The page names foster care, homelessness, disabilities, parenting, leaving high school, and justice involvement as challenges the program serves.
how_to_apply: Contact the Workforce Development Program Manager at the Administrative Offices, (530) 757-5558, or drop by free office hours on Wednesdays from 3 to 6 p.m. at 2455 West Capitol Ave, #118, West Sacramento, CA 95691.
notes: Only the 17-year-old end of this guide's 13 to 18 range is covered. Older YCCA posts mention up to 300 paid hours; that figure is not on the current page and is not used here. Narrower and competitive: it is aimed at young people facing barriers and out of school. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Paid work experience. The pay rate and number of hours are not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Opportunities are limited and differ by branch. The Mary L. Stephens Davis Branch is not accepting applications right now. The page does not list a minimum age.
how_to_apply: Download the Youth Volunteer Application (PDF) from the volunteer page and email it or drop it off at the branch you want.
notes: Call the branch first (main number 530-666-8005). The page said the Mary L. Stephens Davis Branch was not accepting volunteer applications when checked.

who_can_apply: Ages 12 to 15 cannot volunteer alone. They must be with an adult or a supervised group. Ages 16 to 17 can volunteer alone with parent permission (youth waiver).
how_to_apply: Create an account on the Yolo Food Bank volunteer site. Use the Youth Volunteer Waiver for ages 12 to 17. Then sign up online for events. Email volunteer@yolofoodbank.org.
notes: Wear closed-toe shoes and gloves at events. You log your own hours in your volunteer account. Ages 12 to 15 must be with an adult or a supervised group.

who_can_apply: For the Service Award: students in grades K to 12 who live or go to school in Santa Clara or San Mateo County. High schoolers need 100 hours within 12 months. Other programs list no clear age rule.
how_to_apply: Create an account on the Do Service platform at volunteer.youthcommunityservice.org. Phone 650-858-8019 or email ycs@youthcommunityservice.org.
notes: They also offer a scholarship and one-day service pop-ups. It is based at 780 Arastradero Rd, Palo Alto.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24. No experience needed.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Google Form linked on youthradio.org.
notes: The page describes training and mentoring, not a formal paid internship. Ask whether it is paid. It is not on the City of Oakland's 2026 summer jobs list.
pay_detail: Pay not stated on the site

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 25, low-income or homeless youth (per the Berkeley Public Library jobs page).
how_to_apply: Call (510) 858-7229 or email community@youthspiritartworks.org (both on the home page) and ask about job training. The Berkeley Public Library jobs page lists jobtraining@youthspiritartworks.org.
notes: Read the home page on 2026-10-09. It says YSA serves transitional age youth 14 to 25 at 1740 Alcatraz Ave, Berkeley, with free drop-in hours, workshops and events; some workshop series pay a $300 stipend for full participation. The home page does not describe a job training program or its pay, so the 15 to 25 age range, the paid jobs and the jobtraining email come from the library page and are unconfirmed. The FAQ says YSA is not actively accepting applications. Ask before you plan around a job. Not on the City of Oakland's 2026 summer jobs list.
pay_detail: Job training rate not posted (checked 2026-10-09). The home page lists a $300 stipend for full participation in some workshop series.

who_can_apply: East Oakland youth. The City of Oakland list shows YU summer jobs for ages 14 to 21. YU serves ages 13 to 24 overall.
how_to_apply: Call 510-777-9909 or visit 8711 MacArthur Blvd, Oakland. The site gives no online form.
notes: YU's own site has no summer job details, so the ages and hours come from the City of Oakland's 2026 list. Also a referral partner for EBMUD's high school internship.
duration: About 100 hours over 4 to 6 weeks (City list)
pay_detail: Paid (100 hours of fully paid work per the City list); rate not posted

who_can_apply: Oakland middle and high school students. The City summer jobs list shows Media Careers for ages 16 to 21 (June to September).
how_to_apply: Use the Apply page at youthbeat.org/apply, or call 510-922-0060 or email youthbeatmedia@gmail.com.
notes: YouthBeat's own page does not state exact ages; 16 to 21 comes from the City of Oakland's list. Address is a PO box in Oakland.
pay_detail: Training is free; apprentice and PRO work is paid (rate not posted)
